title: fix(messaging)!: a receive leg that stops delivering is reconnected, and the SDK alone deletes frames we cannot unpack
body:
Adopts `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.33.2 and `affinidi-messaging-delivery` 0.1.20 (affinidi-tdk-rs #927) and wires the SDK's new receive-side controls into `vti_common::inbox` (#1978).

## Dependencies

- Workspace floors: `affinidi-messaging-sdk` `0.33.0` → `0.33.2`, `affinidi-messaging-delivery` `0.1` → `0.1.20`. `cargo update -p` moved only those two crates; no sibling TDK crate needed a bump (`affinidi-messaging-core` 0.1.11, `affinidi-messaging-didcomm` 0.15.10, `affinidi-tdk` 0.23.0 are unchanged).
- `cargo tree -d` shows no duplicate `affinidi-*` or `trust-tasks-*` crates.
- The delivery bump needs no wiring here. Its 10 s ack bound and 30 s slow-ack cooldown apply inside `MessagingService`.

## A receive leg that stops delivering is reconnected, within a bound

`run_inbox_watch` already saw this state: three status requests in a row unanswered while the socket reports connected. It now acts on it through a new `ReconnectGovernor` (R1.4):

- **Remedy:** `ATMProfile::reconnect_websocket()`. It re-authenticates, re-enables live delivery, and the mediator redelivers the inbox. The call is bounded to 10 s (R1.2) because it queues a command to the transport task. If the task does not take the command in that time, the task is wedged.
- **Rate:** at most one remedy per 5 min (`RECONNECT_MIN_INTERVAL`). While remedies do not restore delivery, the wait doubles up to 60 min, plus up to 10% jitter. Any answer from the mediator resets the backoff but not the 5 min floor, so a receive leg that dies again a minute after each reconnect is still reconnected only every 5 min.
- **Strikes:** a reconnected socket gets its own three strikes. If it is still dead after them, that is reported again.
- **vtc-service** (`Escalation::Never`): its session is published once in `state.didcomm` and cannot be rebuilt. Until now a dead receive leg there recovered only on the ~12-minute token-refresh reconnect. Now the VTC reconnects the socket about 90 s after the leg stops answering, then backs off as above. It never ends the session.
- **vta-service** (`Escalation::EndSession`): it used to end the whole session every time the alarm tripped, which meant a new ATM, re-authentication and republishing the bridge. That happened about every 90 s plus the supervisor's backoff for as long as the mediator was not delivering. Reconnecting is the better first step: it keeps the session, its published bridge and its in-memory TSP state. The VTA now reconnects first. Only when a reconnect has not restored delivery by the time the next remedy is due, or when the transport will not take the reconnect request, does it end the session for `MessagingConnect` to rebuild. The remedies after that alternate (reconnect, then rebuild) under the same backoff. The governor is owned by the supervisor's loop, so a rebuilt session inherits the backoff and does not start a fresh budget.
- **Overlap with the SDK probe:** the SDK's own probe (60 s idle, then 30 s to answer) will usually reconnect first. The watch is the second layer. It covers a socket that receives probe answers while status replies still go missing, and a transport that stops taking commands. Its reconnects are counted separately from the SDK's.
- **Error text (R6.4):** each failure is named by its class: no websocket transport for the profile, or a transport task that did not take the request within 10 s.

## `/diagnostics` → `inboxCollection`

`InboxHealth` gains:

- `reconnectsRequested`, `lastReconnectAt`, `nextReconnectNotBefore`: the watch's own reconnects.
- `receive`: a `ReceiveLegHealth` that mirrors the SDK's `ReceiveHealth` (`lastDataFrameAt`, `heldFrames`, `consumerStalledSince`, `probeOutstandingSince`, `probeReconnects`, `unprocessableDeleted`, `unprocessableRetained`). It is read from the SDK's `watch` when the snapshot is taken, so it is never staler than the SDK's last publish (R6.2). It is a mirror, not the SDK type, because it is a wire contract: it goes into `openapi.json` and `wire.ts`, and a field the SDK adds later must not change that contract silently.

`unprocessableDeleted` moves from `inboxCollection` to `inboxCollection.receive`, because deletion is now the SDK's job (see below). `openapi.json` and `wire.ts` are regenerated the way #1978 did it (`UPDATE_OPENAPI=1 cargo test -p vtc-service --test it openapi_snapshot`, then `npm run wire:generate`). The admin console does not read these fields yet.

vta-service has no equivalent surface. Its `/health` returns `{"status":"ok"}`, and the richer report is the `vta/health/details/0.1` Trust Task, whose shape belongs to the trust-tasks spec. The VTA's `InboxWatch` is updated the same way and is available for when such a surface exists.

## Who deletes a frame we cannot unpack: the SDK

Before this PR there were two owners. From 0.33.2, every SDK path that reports a frame on the unprocessable channel also decides whether to delete it:

- **Live DIDComm stream (new in 0.33.2):** frames with bad bytes are deleted at once. Policy rejections are deleted per `purge_policy_rejected`. Transient failures are deleted only after three failures over at least an hour. A `SecretsError` (our own key missing) is **never** deleted.
- **Pickup drain:** same rule as before.
- **TSP adapter:** same rule as before.

`run_unprocessable_quarantine` deleted every one of those frames on its second sighting, a minute or so apart. That meant a second deletion of a frame the SDK had already deleted, and, worse, a deletion of exactly the frames the SDK keeps on purpose: a `SecretsError` frame, and a transient failure after one minute rather than one hour. The SDK is the better owner. It classifies the failure from the typed `ATMError`, which VTI only sees as a reason string. It is the layer that holds the frame. And its rule matches across the live stream, the drain and TSP.

So:

- `run_unprocessable_quarantine` is replaced by `run_unprocessable_report(rx, health)`, which only counts (`unprocessableSeen`). It is given no `ATM` or profile, so it cannot delete anything, `SecretsError` frames included. That is enforced by its signature, not only by a check.
- Both services set `.with_delete_unprocessable(true)` explicitly, with a comment, because they rely on it.
- Removed with the quarantine: `Sightings`, `describe_frame`, `frame_id` and `UNPROCESSABLE_DELETE_AFTER`. The SDK's own WARN names each frame's id, envelope, sender and error class.
- The vtc-service integration test (`inbox_collection`) now pins the new owner: three anoncrypt frames are counted by the VTC, deleted by the SDK on their first delivery (`receive.unprocessableDeleted`), and the mediator inbox ends empty.

## Breaking (vti-common)

`run_inbox_watch` takes an `Arc<ReconnectGovernor>` instead of `exit_when_not_delivering: bool`, `run_unprocessable_quarantine` and the frame-description helpers are gone, and `InboxHealth.unprocessable_deleted` is removed. The same applies to `vta_service::messaging::service::run_inbound_loop`, which takes the governor. Hence the `!`.

## Tests

New unit tests in `vti_common::inbox`:

- reconnect backoff floor, doubling and cap
- at most one reconnect per interval
- 12 h of a dead receive leg comes to fewer than 20 reconnects, with gaps that never shrink and stay within the jitter bound
- a reconnect that works resets the backoff but not the floor
- `Never` never ends the session
- `EndSession` alternates reconnect → rebuild → reconnect, and recovery resets that
- a reconnected socket earns new strikes
- `receive` is read live from the SDK's watch
- the serialised `inboxCollection` shape, including that `unprocessableDeleted` lives only under `receive`
- the unprocessable report only counts

## Checks run locally

Running in parallel with CI; results will be posted as a comment.

## Checklist (vti-stack-development-guide)

- R1.2: the `reconnect_websocket()` call is bounded to 10 s.
- R1.4: reconnects are capped, backed off exponentially with jitter, and limited to one per 5 min. Session rebuilds go through the same governor.
- R6.2: `receive` is re-read from the SDK's watch on every snapshot, so it is never a latch.
- R6.4: each reconnect failure is named by its class (no transport, or transport task wedged). A rebuild says that a reconnect did not help.
- R6.5: reconnects and the SDK's view show up in `/diagnostics`, not only in logs.

title: fix(vta): an admin session whose replies stop arriving is noticed and rebuilt
body:
## Why

On 2026-10-05 two OpenVTC admin VTA sessions stopped collecting their mediator inbox for an hour. Every request still reached the VTA, but its replies queued until the mediator's per-peer cap refused them all. OpenVTC noticed nothing: `device_presence` logged its failures at debug level.

This is the OpenVTC follow-up to VTI #1978. It ships on the **published vta-sdk 0.63.3**. OpenVTC cannot move to vta-sdk 0.64 (where #1978 lands as `VtaError::RepliesNotArriving` / `VtaClient::receive_health()`) until `did-git-sign` (VGI) releases on `vta-sdk ^0.64`. Every published did-git-sign is on `^0.63`, so moving now would put two vta-sdk copies in the graph. That VGI release is itself blocked on a `trql-client` (affinidi-trust-registry-rs) release on trust-tasks 0.27 / TDK 0.23.

## What changes

- **Detection (`openvtc-core/src/vta_receive_leg.rs`, new adapter).** Counts consecutive **reply timeouts** on the admin session, using the two shapes vta-sdk 0.63.3 returns:
  - `TspTransport("timed out waiting for the TSP reply …")`
  - `DidcommTransport("timeout waiting for DIDComm response")`

  Any reply resets the count, including a refusal the VTA sent back. A failure to send counts as neither a reply nor a timeout. The count is fed by:
  - device-presence registration, listing and heartbeat (a periodic probe)
  - the launch-time `list_contexts`
  - the probe on a rebuilt session

  Two in a row means "replies not arriving". The module mirrors the SDK's `ReceiveLegHealth` / `REPLY_TIMEOUT_BREAKER` field for field and carries a `TODO(vta-sdk 0.64)` naming the blocker, so switching later only touches this module.
- **Text (R6.4).** The state reads as its own: "Your VTA received the request, but its replies aren't reaching this app — its message inbox isn't being collected (N replies missed in a row). Reconnecting…". It never says "unreachable" or reports an auth failure. `vta_failure` also stops calling a single reply timeout "could not reach your VTA".
- **Visibility.** The VTA panel has a **Replies** row under Transport:
  - **Healthy:** last reply age, plus any replies missed.
  - **Stalled:** `NOT ARRIVING`, what recovery is doing, the next attempt and when, and the last reconnect error.
  - **After a reconnect:** "Reconnected … waiting for its first reply" until one arrives.

  Device registration, listing and heartbeat failures log at WARN every time (they were debug) and also show in the panel and activity log.
- **Recovery (`openvtc/src/state_handler/vta_recovery.rs`).** The admin session is rebuilt by closing the old session (10 s timeout) and opening a fresh one (60 s timeout), whose connect drains the inbox. A probe (45 s timeout) then checks that a reply comes back.
  - Backoff is capped, jittered and exponential: 5 s doubling to 5 min, ±20% (R1.4).
  - One rebuild runs at a time.
  - The schedule resets only once a reply arrives on the new session, so a session that reconnects and stalls again keeps backing off instead of looping.
  - The rebuilt client replaces `admin_vta` in the runtime loop and the State-A loop, and reaches the device-presence task through a `watch` channel. The supervisor is created before the State-A loop, so a rebuild still running when a first join completes lands in the runtime loop.

## Tests

- **New tests cover:**
  - the reply-timeout classification
  - the tracker (two timeouts trip it, a reply resets it, clones share one count)
  - the text mapping (the runtime text and `vta_failure`)
  - the backoff schedule (5, 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 300, 300 s, jitter bounds, reset, no overflow)
  - a rebuild triggered by reply-timeout errors
  - no second rebuild while one is running
  - the backoff continuing after a reconnect that stalls again
  - the swap after a rebuild lands
  - the panel rendering, and presence failure/recovery reporting
- **Checks, all on published vta-sdk 0.63.3 with no `[patch]`:**
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo test --workspace`
  - `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`
  - `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`
  - `cargo deny check`

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). The rebuild's shutdown, connect and probe are each under `tokio::time::timeout`.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3). The tracker's `std::sync::Mutex` is only taken after the call has returned.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). Nothing is persisted; `admin_vta` is swapped only once a new session has connected.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). Rebuilds are capped and jittered, single-flight, and reset on a reply. The only request re-sent is a read (`list_contexts`).
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). A failed rebuild reschedules, and presence failures are reported without ending the loop.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). N/A.
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*). N/A, no wire types.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*). N/A.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*). "Reconnected" stays separate from "replies arriving" until a reply is seen. Presence failures are at WARN and shown in the panel.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1). No persisted state; a rebuild that lands after exit shuts the orphaned session down.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers. Detection covers only the wrapped calls, not every admin call. That is the R6.4 gap the SDK's own counter (vta-sdk 0.64) closes; it is tracked by the `TODO(vta-sdk 0.64)` in `vta_receive_leg.rs`.

title: fix(vta): an admin session whose replies stop arriving is noticed and rebuilt (#469)
body:
fix(vta): an admin session whose replies stop arriving is noticed and rebuilt (#469)

A session whose mediator inbox is not being collected still sends: the VTA
answers every request and the answers queue until the mediator's per-peer
cap refuses them. On 2026-10-05 two admin sessions sat like that for an hour
and nothing in OpenVTC said so; the device heartbeat failed at debug level.

- vta_receive_leg (new adapter): counts reply timeouts on the admin session
  (the TSP and DIDComm reply-timeout errors vta-sdk 0.63 returns), reset by
  any reply. Fed by device-presence registration/listing/heartbeat, the
  launch-time context fetch and the probe on a rebuilt session. Two in a row
  is "replies not arriving". It mirrors vta-sdk 0.64's ReceiveLegHealth /
  RepliesNotArriving (VTI #1978); TODO(vta-sdk 0.64) to switch once
  did-git-sign releases on that line (blocked on a trql-client release).
- The state reads as its own (R6.4): the request reached the VTA, its
  replies are not reaching this app. vta_failure no longer reports a single
  reply timeout as "could not reach your VTA".
- The VTA panel shows the receive leg (last reply, replies missed in a row,
  NOT ARRIVING and recovery progress). Device presence failures log at WARN
  and show in the panel.
- The admin session is rebuilt (old one closed, fresh one opened, which
  drains the inbox) on capped, jittered backoff: 5 s doubling to 5 min,
  +/-20% (R1.4). One rebuild runs at a time, every step has a timeout
  (R1.2), and the schedule resets only once a reply arrives on the new
  session. The new client replaces admin_vta in the runtime and State-A
  loops and reaches the presence task through a watch channel.

title: vta-service-v0.55.0
body:
### Fixed

- **messaging**: A node that stops collecting its inbox is noticed, and its peers stop paying for it ([#1978](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1978))

* fix(messaging)!: a node that stops collecting its inbox is noticed, and its peers stop paying for it

  A message waits in its recipient's mediator inbox until the recipient deletes
  it, and while it waits it counts against its sender's per-peer quota
  (`limits.queue.peer`, 50). On 2026-10-05 two OpenVTC admin sessions stopped
  collecting: 49 VTA replies queued for each, and every further reply was refused
  `503 e.p.limits.queue.peer` while the VTA logged a bare "failed to send TSP
  reply" every 30 s. Sends worked; nothing came back. This makes that state
  visible from both ends and stops the stack making it worse. It needs nothing
  from an unreleased affinidi-tdk-rs.

- **vtc**: Handle inbound messages concurrently, so a bind's bridge reply is read ([#1973](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1973))

The VTC's messaging loop awaited each inbound frame's handler before
  reading the next. An operation that arrives by messaging and then waits
  on a messaging reply therefore waited on itself: `cnm git namespace
  bind` over TSP sends the bridge a beginBind job and waits up to 30 s for
  the answer, which arrives on the same stream and is not read until the
  handler gives up. Observed live: the bridge answered in ~20 ms, the
  mediator relayed it in 0-1 ms, and the VTC read it 30.1 s after the
  request — "TSP reply had no waiter" — while cnm reported "the bridge did
  not answer". Any inline bridge job reached over DIDComm or TSP is hit the
  same way.

  The loop now spawns each frame's handler, bounded at 32 in flight, as
  the VTA's inbound loop has since the same defect was fixed there. Per-
  sender ordering is kept where TSP needs it (a relationship-control frame
  is a barrier for its sender's later traffic, Keyring VTI-43): SenderOrder
  moves from vta-service to vti-common so both nodes share it, and
  vta-service re-exports it at its old path.

  The reader is factored into run_inbound_loop so it can be tested: a
  handler that waits on a later frame completes (it hangs, and the test
  fails at its 5 s bound, with the loop made serial again), and an invite
  is still handled before its sender's following task.

title: vta-sdk-v0.64.0
body:
### Fixed

- **messaging**: A node that stops collecting its inbox is noticed, and its peers stop paying for it ([#1978](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1978))

* fix(messaging)!: a node that stops collecting its inbox is noticed, and its peers stop paying for it

  A message waits in its recipient's mediator inbox until the recipient deletes
  it, and while it waits it counts against its sender's per-peer quota
  (`limits.queue.peer`, 50). On 2026-10-05 two OpenVTC admin sessions stopped
  collecting: 49 VTA replies queued for each, and every further reply was refused
  `503 e.p.limits.queue.peer` while the VTA logged a bare "failed to send TSP
  reply" every 30 s. Sends worked; nothing came back. This makes that state
  visible from both ends and stops the stack making it worse. It needs nothing
  from an unreleased affinidi-tdk-rs.

- **vetting**: A new drip rate or live period no longer voids hidden-vetting attestations ([#1977](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1977))

requirementsDigest covered the whole hidden-vetting ext, so republishing how a
  community runs hidden vetting (dripPerTick, tickLength, vetter/token labels,
  events) moved the digest. A hidden vetter's attestation is bound to the digest,
  so every attestation in flight silently stopped counting: the proof verified
  and the join was decided request_more with nothing said. This held a live PCS
  join after the operator lowered the drip rate.

  requirements_digest now leaves those operational members out; the suite and
  keys stay covered, so an applicant still never binds to keys it was not shown.
  Label liveness is checked on its own when a proof is read.

title: fix(messaging)!: a node that stops collecting its inbox is noticed, and its peers stop paying for it
body:
## Problem

A message waits in its recipient's mediator inbox until the recipient deletes it, and while it waits it counts against its **sender's** per-peer quota (`limits.queue.peer`, 50 by default). On 2026-10-05 (mediator 0.37.0) two OpenVTC admin VTA sessions stopped collecting their inboxes. Each had 49 VTA replies waiting, the oldest an hour old, and every further reply was refused `503 e.p.limits.queue.peer`. The VTA logged `failed to send TSP reply` and `could not send a TSP relationship accept` about every 30 s. Sends were working and nothing was coming back. Nothing in the stack watched the receive leg end to end, and three behaviours made the backlog grow:

- The VTA had no inbox catch-up (the VTC has had one since VTI-50).
- Frames a node cannot unpack were never deleted. The SDK only reports them, so they sat in the inbox counting against their sender.
- vta-sdk's §7.2.2 D4 self-repair re-invited and resent after every reply timeout, with no limit across calls. Each call to a client that was not collecting queued two more replies.

The VTC's catch-up had problems of its own:
- **Unbounded (R1.4).** It re-asked for redelivery of an uncollectable backlog every 30 s, forever.
- **Logged at DEBUG only (R6.5).** A status request that went unanswered while connected, meaning the VTC was receiving nothing, never showed up at a visible log level.

The companion TDK PR is affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#927. It adds a receive-leg probe and reconnect, timeouts on the inbound chain, a bounded ack, and deletion of poison DIDComm frames in the SDK. **This PR depends on none of it** and builds against the released affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.33.

## Changes

**vti-common — new `inbox` module, shared by the VTA and the VTC**
- `run_inbox_watch`: the VTI-50 catch-up, now bounded.
  - Every 30 s it sends a status request. When something has waited longer than a live push takes, it asks the mediator to redeliver.
  - If the same oldest message is still there after a redelivery, the next redelivery request waits twice as long, up to 30 min, and the condition is reported once at WARN.
  - Three unanswered status requests in a row while the socket reports `Connected` mean the receive leg is dead. This is reported at WARN, and the session can optionally be ended.
- `InboxWatch` / `InboxHealth`: receive-leg health that is re-observed every check rather than latched (R6.2).
- `run_unprocessable_quarantine`: handles frames the SDK reports on its unprocessable channel.
  - On the first delivery the frame is reported and kept, because the failure may be transient and the catch-up is the retry.
  - On the second delivery it is deleted.
  - Each frame is named in a WARN with the sender the envelope claims (`skid`/`apu`, JWS `kid`, or plaintext `from`), the envelope kind, the type, the reason and the frame id. This is a deliberate R1.6 poison-message tradeoff, documented at the call site.
- `refused_recipient_not_collecting` classifies a refusal from the typed `QueueFullGate::Peer`; it does not match strings.
- `UncollectedPeers` logs one WARN per recipient, `{did} is not collecting its mediator inbox; replies to it are being dropped`, then logs at DEBUG for 5 min.

**vta-service**
- Runs the watch and the quarantine.
- When the receive leg is dead it ends the session, so `MessagingConnect` reconnects. The reconnect re-registers for live delivery and redelivers the stored inbox.
- TSP replies, relationship accepts and DIDComm replies refused per-peer now go through `UncollectedPeers`.
- An accept is not sent to a peer that was refused within the window. That peer re-invites after every reply timeout, so each accept was another refused send and another WARN.

**vtc-service**
- The catch-up now uses the shared, bounded watch, and the quarantine runs.
- Its TSP and DIDComm replies and accepts get the same per-peer handling as the VTA's.
- `/diagnostics` gains `inboxCollection`. The admin console's `openapi.json` and `wire.ts` are regenerated.

**vta-sdk (breaking: a new `VtaError` variant)**
- After `REPLY_TIMEOUT_BREAKER` (2) reply timeouts in a row, the D4 self-repair no longer re-forms the relationship or resends. It returns `VtaError::RepliesNotArriving { consecutive_timeouts }` ("the request was sent, but replies are not reaching this client … reconnect the session").
- Any reply closes the breaker. The breaker is shared by clones.
- `idempotency::is_transient` does not retry the new variant, and it has its own `suggested_fix` (R6.4).
- `VtaClient::receive_health() -> ReceiveLegHealth` exposes consecutive reply timeouts, time since the last reply, and time since the last timeout.

## Tests

- `vti-common` `inbox::tests` (18):
  - backoff never shrinks and reaches its cap;
  - a new backlog is asked for at once;
  - three unanswered requests mean not delivering, reported once per episode;
  - a request that was never sent is not evidence;
  - status-error classification;
  - frame description for authcrypt (`skid`/`apu`), anoncrypt, JWS, plaintext and garbage;
  - the sighting map is bounded;
  - per-peer refusal classification, including the sender gate being *not* matched;
  - one report per recipient per window.
- `vtc-service` IT `inbox_collection::an_unreadable_frame_is_deleted_on_its_second_delivery`:
  - runs the production listener on an embedded mediator;
  - three anoncrypted frames are reported on first delivery, deleted after the redelivery, and the mediator then reports an empty inbox;
  - **fails without the fix** (`unprocessable_seen: 6, unprocessable_deleted: 0`).
- e2e `inbox_collection::a_per_peer_refusal_is_recognised_as_the_recipient_not_collecting`: an embedded mediator with a per-peer cap of 3 and a recipient that never connects. It pins the classifier to the real mediator's `503` body.
- `vta-sdk` `client::receive_leg_tests` (7):
  - D4 still repairs one silent drop;
  - after 2 timeouts, the error is `RepliesNotArriving` and there are no further re-forms or resends;
  - a reply closes the breaker;
  - a keyed task is re-formed but not resent;
  - a transport failure does not count as a timeout;
  - the breaker is shared by clones;
  - the new variant is not transient.

CI-equivalent runs, all local:
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 5410 passed.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 2864 passed after regenerating the OpenAPI snapshot.
- Workspace doctests pass.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean, as are the narrowed vta-service builds and `vtc-service --features vetting-pcs`.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `npm run wire:check` are clean.

## Follow-ups (depend on affinidi-tdk-rs#927 shipping as affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.33.2)

- Surface the SDK's `ReceiveHealth` beside `InboxHealth`.
- Have the VTC call `ATMProfile::reconnect_websocket()` when its watch reports `notDelivering`. Today the VTC reports this but does not tear down its set-once session. Recovery currently comes from the SDK's token-refresh reconnect, about 12 min, and from #927's probe.
- OpenVTC: show `RepliesNotArriving` as its own state in the VTA panel, and rebuild `admin_vta` with capped, jittered backoff when it appears.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new `reqwest::Client::new()` or bare fetch; every new await on the network is bounded. The status request has the SDK's 10 s bound, and the delete enqueue has a 5 s timeout (R1.2).
- [x] No lock held across a network await. `InboxWatch` and `UncollectedPeers` use short `std` mutex sections only (R1.3).
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect (R2.1). N/A: health counters only.
- [x] Every retry is bounded and backed off. Redelivery doubles from 30 s to 30 min, and D4 now has a breaker across calls (R1.4).
- [x] Poll loops survive transient errors. The watch skips while disconnected, and a failed status request or redelivery is logged and retried on the next tick (R1.5).
- [x] Acks and deletes happen only after durable handoff — **flagged deviation**: unprocessable frames are deleted before handoff as a poison-message defence. The first failure is not treated as poison; the frame is deleted only on its second delivery, and the tradeoff is documented at the call site (R1.6).
- [x] New wire fields: `inboxCollection` in `/diagnostics` is camelCase and additive (outbound-only, so no `deny_unknown_fields`); `openapi.json` and `wire.ts` are regenerated. No new Trust Task URI (R3.*).
- [x] Config absence means the most restrictive behaviour (R5.*). N/A: no new config.
- [x] Logs and status claim only what was verified. "Not delivering" is reported only after the mediator failed to answer requests that were actually written to the socket. Background failures surface in `/diagnostics` (VTC) and through a session reconnect (VTA) (R6.*).
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" is answered for every mutation touched: in-memory health only, and frame deletion is idempotent at the mediator.
- [x] Deviations flagged: R1.6, above. The VTC does not reconnect itself yet (see Follow-ups).

title: fix(vetting): a new drip rate or live period no longer voids hidden-vetting attestations
body:
## Problem
`requirementsDigest` covered the entire `vetting.ext["org.openvtc.hidden-vetting"]` the VTC injects at serve time. Republishing **how** hidden vetting runs — `dripPerTick`, `tickLength`, `vetterLabels`, `tokenLabels`, `events` — therefore changed the digest. A hidden vetter's attestation binds the digest, so every attestation in flight stopped counting (`requirements-digest-mismatch`): the proof verified, the join was decided `request_more`, `superseded=false`, and nothing was logged. This held a live PCS ZKP join (first-vtc, 2026-10-05) after the operator changed the drip rate 100 → 20.

## Change
`vta_sdk::vetting::requirements::requirements_digest` leaves the operational members (`HIDDEN_VETTING_OPERATIONAL`) out of the hidden-vetting ext before digesting. **`suite`, `helperKey`, `tokenKey` stay covered** — `the_digest_covers_the_published_parameters` (keys) still holds, so an applicant never binds to keys it was not shown. Deny-list, so any parameter added later is covered by default. Label liveness is already checked independently when a proof is read (`token-label-not-live`, #1976).

The digest stays recomputable from the delivered criterion (both sides call the same function); OpenVTC only echoes the delivered digest, so no client change is needed.

## Upgrade note
Digests of existing **hidden** criteria change once on deploy (named criteria are unaffected); attestations made before the upgrade would need re-attesting — the same effect any parameter change had before, but now the last time.

## Spec impact
`requirementsDigest` is documented (docs/03-vtc/join-criteria.md) as covering everything about a criterion; the `org.openvtc.hidden-vetting` extension's operational members are now excluded. Doc line to follow if accepted.

## Tests
- vta-sdk: `operational_hidden_vetting_parameters_are_outside_the_digest` (drip, live period unchanged; keys, requirements change).
- vtc-service: `a_new_drip_rate_keeps_the_digest`; existing manifest/vetting/join suites with `vetting-pcs` pass (216 + 156).
- fmt, clippy -D warnings (vta-sdk, vtc-service + vetting-pcs).

title: fix(vtc): say why a hidden-vetting proof did not count
body:
## Problem
A live hidden-vetting (PCS ZKP) join was decided `request_more` / `met=false` with only `vetting:statements:1`. The proof verified (a refused proof is a 4xx, not `requestMore`), but its attestation was not counted, and nothing at INFO said why. The applicant saw "needs more vetting (statements:1)". That is the named path's wording, and they had presented a proof.

Every per-statement refusal in `vti_vetting_pcs::Verifier::submit` (`token-mismatch`, `no-token`, `token-double-spend`, `requirements-digest-mismatch`, `expired`, plus the counting rule's codes) ended up in the stored facts and nowhere else. The likely cause here: the operator changed the published hidden-vetting parameters. The criterion digest covers `dripPerTick`, `tickLength`, the live labels and the events (`manifest_criterion` injects them before digesting). So an attestation made before the change binds the old digest and is refused `requirements-digest-mismatch`. If a token label is no longer live, it is refused `no-token` instead.

## Change (R6.4)
- `vetting::hidden_facts` logs at INFO for each hidden submission: the number of attestations, how many counted, distinct vetters, needs, and the failure codes. No tag is logged.
- `pcs::explain_statements` logs the stale token labels and the digests the attestations were made under. Both are public parameters. It also renames the verifier's ambiguous `no-token` to `token-label-not-live` when the label is the cause.
- The applicant receives the reasons as needs `vetting:hidden:<code>`. The counting rule's `issuer-not-vetter` echo is dropped when a more specific code is present.
- When a hidden-vetting criterion is decided on the named path, that is logged and `vetting:hidden:no-proof` (or `unsupported` without `vetting-pcs`) is added.
- The new needs are outside vta-sdk's `Need` grammar (`Need::parse` returns `None`), so existing clients show them as they came. OpenVTC words them in OpenVTC/openvtc (companion PR).

## Tests
- `vetting::pcs::tests::a_token_under_a_label_no_longer_live_is_named_as_such`
- `vetting::tests::hidden_reasons_name_the_specific_cause`
- `vetting::tests::a_hidden_need_is_not_a_count`

## Checklist
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`, with and without `--features vetting-pcs`
- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service` (2832 passed) and `--features vetting-pcs` (2874 passed)
- [x] R6.4: operator log and applicant reason distinguish the causes
- [x] No wire break: needs are strings; the new ones are additive

body:
fix(vtc): say why a hidden-vetting proof did not count (R6.4) (#1976)

A PCS ZKP proof that verified but whose attestations were not counted was
decided requestMore with only vetting:statements:N, and nothing at INFO said
why. The usual cause is an operator changing the published hidden-vetting
parameters (dripPerTick, tickLength, live labels, events): the criterion digest
covers them, so every attestation made before the change binds the old digest
(requirements-digest-mismatch), or spends a token under a label no longer live.

- Log at INFO, per hidden submission: attestations, counted, distinct vetters,
  needs and the failure codes (never a tag). Log the stale token labels and the
  digests the attestations were made under, which are public parameters.
- Report a token under a label no longer accepted as token-label-not-live rather
  than the verifier's no-token, which reads like a forged token.
- Send the applicant the reasons as needs vetting:hidden:<code>, dropping the
  counting rule's issuer-not-vetter echo when a specific code is present.
- A hidden-vetting criterion decided on the named path (no proof carried, or a
  build without vetting-pcs) logs it and adds vetting:hidden:no-proof /
  vetting:hidden:unsupported.

The new needs are outside vta-sdk's Need grammar, so existing clients show them
verbatim.

title: fix(vetting): hidden-vetting join says why its proof did not count; draws follow the current rate
body:
## Live incident
An applicant's hidden-vetting (PCS ZKP) join was sent over TSP with `submit/0.3`. It came back `request_more` / `met=false` and the client showed "it still needs more vetting (statements:1)". The join page had called the application satisfied.

### Diagnosis
- **The proof was sent.** `join_flow.rs` refuses to submit a hidden-vetting application without a proof (`hidden_proof_refusal`). `Application::join_extensions` puts it under `extensions.hiddenVetting` for both 0.2 and 0.3. `join::build_join_submit_document` carries `extensions` unchanged on TSP and DIDComm alike. VTC `handle_submit` passes `body.extensions` to `submit_inner`, then to `criteria::govern`, then `vetting_facts`, then `hidden_facts`, then `pcs::decide`.
- **The proof verified.** A proof or challenge failure is a submit refusal (4xx), not `requestMore`. So the VTC verified the proof and counted none of its attestations. The verifier refuses an attestation in five ways, all silent at INFO: `requirements-digest-mismatch`, `no-token` (which includes a token label no longer live), `token-mismatch`, `token-double-spend`, `expired`.
- **Likely cause.** The criterion digest covers the published hidden-vetting parameters (`dripPerTick`, `tickLength`, labels, events). The operator changed the drip rate: the vetter was refused `overQuota`, asking 100 where the community drips 20. An attestation binds the digest of the applicant's vetting request at the time it was made, and its token's label. When either moves, the attestation can never count. The client's checklist did not know this.

## Commit 1: say why, and don't call it satisfied
- `Application::stale_hidden_attestation` / `holds_current_hidden_attestation` (`openvtc-core/src/vetting/applicant.rs`). An attestation whose `requirementsDigest` or token label the community no longer publishes no longer counts on the checklist.
- `join_flow.rs`: a join holding only such attestations does not spend a challenge. It stops with: "The community would not count your PCS ZKP proof … ask your vetter to attest again".
- `messaging::describe_join_needs(needs, hidden)`: on a hidden join, a `requestMore` now reads "the community did not count your PCS ZKP proof (it still needs 1 more vetter): <reason>". The reason comes from the `vetting:hidden:<code>` needs that VTI #1976 adds. The named path's wording is unchanged.

## Commit 2: draws follow the community's current rate
- Every manifest read updates every held vetter engine's parameters (`learn_mode` → `HiddenVetterState::take_reading`), with a `params_read_at` stamp. Before this, the schedule planned on the cached parameters before the read's answer arrived.
- Nothing is drawn unless the parameters were read within the last 10 minutes (`draw_hold`).
- `overQuota` ("asked for N; this community drips M") re-reads the manifest straight away, bypassing the 30 s gap, once per refusal. The next draw is capped at M. If the community still publishes the refused rate, drawing stops and the desk says why.
- The hidden-vetting view shows "Rate 20 tokens every 3 days · read 21:16 UTC".
- The ~32 rapid draws were catch-up of begun ticks, two passes of `MAX_DRAWS_PER_PASS` = 16 with in-flight draws excluded, not duplicates.

## Checks
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test --workspace`
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`
- [x] `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`
- [x] CHANGELOG under 0.5.0 → Fixed

Companion: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1976 (VTC logs the reason at INFO and sends `vetting:hidden:<code>`).

title: fix(vetting): hidden-vetting join says why its proof did not count; draws follow the current rate (#468)
body:
fix(vetting): hidden-vetting join says why its proof did not count; draws follow the current rate (#468)

* fix(vetting): a hidden-vetting join says why its PCS ZKP proof did not count

An attestation made before a community changed its published hidden-vetting
parameters binds the criterion digest of the time (the digest covers dripPerTick,
tickLength, live labels and events), or a token label no longer live. The VTC
verifies the proof and then counts nothing, and the reply said only
"needs more vetting (statements:1)" while the join page called the application
satisfied.

- The applicant checklist no longer counts an attestation whose digest or token
  label the community no longer publishes.
- A join holding only such attestations stops before asking for a challenge and
  says to ask the vetter to attest again.
- A requestMore on a hidden-vetting join reads "the community did not count your
  PCS ZKP proof: <reason>", with the community's vetting:hidden:<code> reasons.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vetting): hidden-vetting draws follow the community's current rate

Every manifest read (scheduled pass, desk open, before t/k, the 10-minute
TTL, the join flow's HTTP read) now adopts the published hidden-vetting
parameters into each engine held for the community at once
(VettingBook::learn_mode -> HiddenVetterState::take_reading), keeping the
enrolled keys, and dates them (params_read_at).

A pass used to ask for the manifest and then draw on the cached copy
before the answer landed. Draws are now held unless the parameters were
read within PARAMS_FRESH_FOR and no manifest question is open; the read's
answer runs the schedule again (awaiting_read -> vetter_refresh_due).

An overQuota refusal records the refused rate (and the rate the refusal
text names), asks for the manifest at once (bypassing the 30 s gap, once
per refusal), and draws nothing until a read after it is taken. After
that, draws under the label are held to the named rate; if the community
still publishes the refused rate and named none, drawing stops with a
distinct desk message until its parameters change (R1.4, R6.4).

The hidden-vetting view shows the rate with when it was read
("20 tokens every 3 days · read 21:16 UTC") and any hold.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(vgi-bridge): required_approvals — pull requests need N approving reviews to merge
body:
The pull-request gate decides who may open a pull request; who may merge is
the forge's permission model, which the bridge already drives from the
community's rights (owners admin, maintainers maintain, committers no
role). Nothing asked for review, though: outside owner review, the managed
ruleset required a pull request and the check, and no approval.

`required_approvals = N` (0-10, default 0) in the bridge config now puts N
approving reviews into every governed repository's protection: on GitHub
the `VGI commit trust` ruleset's pull_request rule, with approvals
dismissed by a later push and the last push approved by someone other than
its pusher; on Forgejo the branch protection's required_approvals with
stale approvals dismissed and no approvals whitelist. Only accounts with
write access count, so only the rights holders the bridge projects can
approve — the "approved members" of the community. Owner review keeps its
code-owner approval; the larger count applies.

It is applied when a repository's bootstrap runs (created or adopted).
The observed count is read back (counted only in the dismiss-stale shape)
and a rule asking for fewer is a new drift gap, ApprovalsBelow, rendered
into the existing protectionWeakened text item — no wire change — so an
inspection reports it and ruleset drift `enforce` puts it back.

vgi-forge: ProtectionSpec::required_approvals + approvals_needed(),
VgiConfig::required_approvals, ProtectionState/Projection
required_approvals, ProtectionGap::ApprovalsBelow (all non_exhaustive,
additive). BRIDGE.md §6e and the example config describe it, including that
a repository then needs a second rights holder to merge, and that the org's
base permission must not give members write access.

Tests: `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`. New: ruleset body + comparison (GitHub), observed count only in the dismiss-stale shape, every guard's plan carries it, drift gap below/above, Forgejo protection body + satisfaction (fields sent only when set, so existing requests are byte-identical), config default/bound.

title: fix(admin-ui): the namespace-rights card keeps its holders and Grant buttons inside it
body:
In the three-up row the card is narrow, and its grid's middle track was a bare 1fr, whose minimum is its content's width. A holder's name plus shortened DID (which does not wrap) widened the track past the card's edge, clipping the DID and pushing both Grant buttons out of view. The track is now minmax(0, 1fr); a holder may shrink, its name and DID stack when the line is short, and the DID ellipsises (the title attribute keeps the full DID on hover).

Checked by rendering the card's markup with `styles.css` in headless Chrome at 620 px (fits on one line, Grant buttons visible) and 400 px (name and DID stack, DID ellipsised). `vitest run src/plugins/repos.test.tsx`: 31 passed.

title: fix(vtc): handle inbound messages concurrently, so a bind's bridge reply is read
body:
The VTC's messaging loop awaited each inbound frame's handler before
reading the next. An operation that arrives by messaging and then waits
on a messaging reply therefore waited on itself: `cnm git namespace
bind` over TSP sends the bridge a beginBind job and waits up to 30 s for
the answer, which arrives on the same stream and is not read until the
handler gives up. Observed live: the bridge answered in ~20 ms, the
mediator relayed it in 0-1 ms, and the VTC read it 30.1 s after the
request — "TSP reply had no waiter" — while cnm reported "the bridge did
not answer". Any inline bridge job reached over DIDComm or TSP is hit the
same way.

The loop now spawns each frame's handler, bounded at 32 in flight, as
the VTA's inbound loop has since the same defect was fixed there. Per-
sender ordering is kept where TSP needs it (a relationship-control frame
is a barrier for its sender's later traffic, Keyring VTI-43): SenderOrder
moves from vta-service to vti-common so both nodes share it, and
vta-service re-exports it at its old path.

The reader is factored into run_inbound_loop so it can be tested: a
handler that waits on a later frame completes (it hangs, and the test
fails at its 5 s bound, with the loop made serial again), and an invite
is still handled before its sender's following task.

Tests: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; the two new tests pass, and the first fails as intended against a serial loop. `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vti-common -p vta-service` — 5340 passed; 1 timed out under full-suite load (`vta-service audit_coverage::every_consequential_task_records_an_audit_entry`, 300 s limit), which passes alone in 27 s and is unaffected by this change (vta-service only re-exports `sender_order`).
author: stormer78

title: fix(join): the join page shows a PCS ZKP proof as ready, not 0 statements
body:
Joining a PCS ZKP (hidden-vetting) community with enough vetter attestations gathered, the "Choose how to join" row read **Present your vetting statements as … — 0 statements ready to present**: it counted only `presentable_statements` (named), and hidden vetting has none — the proof is built from the held attestations.

- `JoinApplication.attestations` = `Application::hidden_held()`.
- A satisfied application holding attestations reads **Present your PCS ZKP proof as …** — *ready — proves N vetters vetted you, without naming them*. Named-path wording unchanged.

Test added to `the_vetting_row_names_its_persona_and_that_persona_s_standing`. Local: fmt, clippy -D warnings, openvtc tests.

title: ci(deps): hold rand_chacha at 0.3 while arkworks is on rand 0.8
body:
Dependabot's #1969 (`rand_chacha` 0.3 → 0.10) can't build: `rand_chacha` 0.10 implements `rand_core` 0.10's traits, but `vti-vetting-pcs` passes its `ChaCha20Rng` to arkworks, which uses the `rand` 0.8 / `rand_core` 0.6 traits. The build fails with `no function or associated item named from_seed found for ChaCha20Rng`.

Bridging the two trait sets isn't worth it. `Issuer::derive` seeds this RNG to generate every community's PCS keys, so any change to how its stream is consumed would re-key every deployment. The `signerChanged` refusal (#1960) would then block every publish.

This adds `rand_chacha` to Dependabot's ignore list for **major** updates only, next to the existing `rand` hold, which has the same cause. 0.3 patch releases still come through. Lift it when arkworks moves off `rand` 0.8.

#1969 is closed in favour of this.

title: fix(vetting): a lost hidden-vetting enrolment is asked for once more
body:
Pairs with OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1972, which lets a VTC re-issue a lost `pcs-root` enrolment answer to the same PCS identifier (bounded to 3 re-issues per label).

Without this, a client already refused `alreadyEnrolled` latched the label as lost (`lost_enrolment`) and never asked again — so a stranded vetter (devote-hotel, vetter/2026-10) would never collect the re-issue.

- `HiddenVetterState::lost_reasked` (serde-skipped when false): under a lost label the schedule asks **once** more, then stops; a refusal of that ask leaves it spent, an opened answer clears the lost label. A newly lost label earns a fresh ask.
- `k` (get tokens) clears the flag — asking by hand is worth one more try; the VTC bounds re-issues.
- The desk / outlook call the enrolment lost only once the extra ask is refused (not while it is still to run or in flight); the lost-enrolment words now say it refused to issue again and that `k` asks once more.
- Against a VTC without #1972: one extra refused request per lost label, then the old behaviour.

Tests updated/added in openvtc-core and openvtc. Local: fmt, clippy -D warnings, workspace tests (default and no-default-features), docs.
author: stormer78

title: fix(vetting): a lost hidden-vetting enrolment is asked for once more (#466)
body:
fix(vetting): a lost hidden-vetting enrolment is asked for once more (#466)

A vetter refused alreadyEnrolled under a label it holds no credential for was
latched as lost and never asked again until the next label. VTI #1972 lets a
community re-issue a lost answer to the same PCS identifier, so the schedule
now asks once more under a lost label (HiddenVetterState::lost_reasked) and
stops only when that ask is refused too; k clears the flag to ask again by
hand. The desk calls the enrolment lost only once that ask is answered.

title: fix(vtc): a vetter who lost the enrolment answer is re-issued it, to the same identifier only
body:
A vetter whose client lost the `vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-root` answer before unblinding it (a restart, a dropped message) had no way back until the next label. The VTC keeps only *that* a member enrolled, never the answer, and every re-ask was refused `alreadyEnrolled`, so the vetter had no credential, no tokens and no tickets for the rest of the month. This happened to a vetter in production. OpenVTC now persists its blinding before it sends. Recovery from a loss still needs this side.

## The change

`pcs_issue::enrol` now re-issues when the member already holds the label **and** the request's `id` equals the `EnrolmentRecord.id` they are bound to. It signs the new blinded request instead of refusing it. The idempotency key is (member DID, label, bound PCS id).

- **Another identifier is still refused.** The identifier check now runs before the held-label check, so a held label with a different `id` is answered `identifierRebound`. Before, it was `alreadyEnrolled`, which was the wrong reason: the request carries a second key, not a lost answer.
- **There is a bound.** `MAX_REISSUES_PER_LABEL = 3` per (member, label). The count is persisted on the enrolment row (`EnrolmentRecord.reissues`, `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]`, so existing rows read and write unchanged). Past the bound the answer is `alreadyEnrolled` again, which is exactly the behaviour before this change. I chose a count over a minimum interval on purpose. A dropped message is retried at once, and an interval would refuse that retry. OpenVTC also latches on `alreadyEnrolled` and stops asking, so a spurious refusal would strand the vetter. The count alone bounds the signatures per label to 1 + 3.
- **Enrolment is serialised** (`ENROL_LOCK`, a process-wide `tokio::sync::Mutex` held from reading the record to writing it back). Without it, two requests for one member that were in flight together both read the record before either wrote it, so two re-issues could both pass the bound. That race already existed before this change, and it was worse: two concurrent *first* enrolments under *different* identifiers would both be signed. That gave one member two class credentials, which the §13 C2 binding exists to prevent. The lock covers store and signing work only, never a network await (R1.3). Enrolment happens once a month per vetter, so the lock does not contend.
- **The audit row is distinct.** A re-issue writes the new `AuditEvent::HiddenVetterReissued { label, reissue }` instead of `HiddenVetterEnrolled`. Like the enrolment row, it carries no PCS identifier. The label is not pushed a second time, so `enrolled_counts` (the `hidden/show` count) still counts members, not signatures.
- **The wire contract is unchanged.** A re-issue answers in the first enrolment's `Response` shape (the unit test validates it against the generated schema). The current OpenVTC client therefore unblinds it without any change whenever it asks again with fresh blinding.

`AuditEvent` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so the new variant and the new payload struct in `vti-common` are additive, not breaking. `vtc-service` is `publish = false`.

## Why a re-issue cannot give one vetter two votes

I checked each of these claims against the code before relying on it:

1. **The credential is bound to the identifier, and the identifier to the secret key.**
   - `pcs_issue::enrol` checks `request.id` against the bound `record.id` (`vtc-service/src/vetting/pcs_issue.rs:346`). It then parses that same `id` (`:361`) and passes it to `Issuer::issue_root` (`:366`, then `vti-vetting-pcs/src/issuer.rs:173-185`).
   - The crate's `issue_root` refuses unless `verify_root_request(hvk, f_root, id, request)` holds (`predicate-credential-system-0.1.0/src/pcs/construction.rs:1327-1350`). That check verifies `R_issue` (`construction.rs:592-620`): the commitment `C` opens to `m_hid` whose first component is `usk`, **and** `id = Tag(usk, c_0)`, **and** `T_0 = Tag(usk, s)`, all on the same `usk` variable (`:602`, `:611-617`).
   - Under `Tag_DDH`, `id = g_1^usk` (`kiprf/ddh.rs:10`, `:32`, eval at `:169-175`), so one `id` corresponds to exactly one `usk`. Every credential a member can hold is therefore on the same key.
2. **Every tag derives from that key.** `Attest` computes `T_j = Tag(usk_j, H_0(id_applicant))` (`construction.rs:1188-1190`). The tag depends on `usk` and the applicant's `id` only (`:1065`), not on which credential is shown. Design doc §13 C2 states the same requirement: a refreshed root credential must yield the same tag.
3. **Proofs require pairwise-distinct tags.** `CheckAtts_P` rejects duplicate tags with `DuplicateAttester` (`construction.rs:846-849`) and `T_0` reuse with `SelfAttestation` (`:851`). It runs in `check_proof_in_context`, which the verifier calls (`vti-vetting-pcs/src/verifier.rs:200`). Two attestations from one vetter, whichever of its credentials made them, are refused rather than counted.
4. **The token drip is per member/label/tick.**
   - `drip` keys its once-a-tick row on `(member_did, label, tick)` (`pcs_issue.rs:178`, `:474`) and caps the batch at the published quota in `Issuer::issue_tokens` (`issuer.rs:205-210`).
   - It reads nothing `enrol` writes, so a re-issue changes no token count. The new test checks this directly: after three re-issues, the served tick is still refused, and the next tick is still capped at the drip rate.

The vetter's grant is still checked first, so a removed vetter cannot be re-issued.

## Tests

- `pcs_issue::tests::a_lost_enrolment_answer_is_reissued_to_the_same_identifier_only` covers:
  - same id with fresh blinding is re-issued, unblinds, and matches the spec response shape;
  - a different id under the held label is refused `identifierRebound`;
  - the count is persisted and the label is recorded once;
  - the fourth re-issue is refused `alreadyEnrolled`;
  - `enrolled_counts` stays 1;
  - the drip's once-a-tick and quota still hold.
- `pcs_issue::tests::an_enrolment_row_without_reissues_reads_and_writes_as_before` checks that a stored row from before this change round-trips byte-for-byte.
- `a_vetter_enrols_once_and_draws_its_quota`: the "twice under one label" step is now a re-issue that leaves the enrolment count at 1.
- `tests/it/hidden_vetting_tasks.rs` runs the same cases over the Trust Task wire, with the declared codes.
- `vti-common`: `hidden_vetter_reissued_round_trip`.

## Spec impact

The `pcs-root/0.1` declaration of `alreadyEnrolled` (trust-tasks spec, as generated into `trust-tasks-rs` 0.27.7) reads:

> This member already holds a credential under `label`. One per member per label is what makes distinct tags distinct people.

After this change the code is returned only once the re-issue bound is spent, and the rationale is slightly off: what makes distinct tags distinct people is one *identifier* per member, not one *credential*. Suggested wording for a spec PR (not opened here):

> `alreadyEnrolled`: This member already holds a credential under `label` and the community will not re-issue it again. A community MAY re-issue a credential under a label the member already holds, to the identifier they are bound to, so that a client that lost the answer can recover; it SHOULD bound how many times. Re-issue to the same identifier adds no attester, because every tag derives from the key behind the identifier; a different identifier is refused `identifierRebound`.

`identifierRebound` needs no change. Its text ("`id` is not the identifier this member was bound to") now also covers a held label asked for under another id. The response schema is unchanged.

## Client note (OpenVTC)

Nothing in the wire contract changes. However, a vetter who was **already** refused `alreadyEnrolled` under the current label is latched by OpenVTC (`lost_enrolment`), which stops asking until the label moves on. That vetter needs the client to ask once more (a client-side follow-up) to pick up the re-issue this change allows.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no outbound clients touched
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): `ENROL_LOCK` covers local store reads/writes and CPU signing only
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): the record is written after signing, as before. A crash after the write but before the reply costs one re-issue of the bound, never an extra vetter
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): re-issue is idempotent in effect on (member, label, id) and bounded to 3 per label
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): no wire type changed. The new audit payload is camelCase; the stored row change is additive with `serde(default)`
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): the audit row is written after the store write, as for enrolment
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): see above
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

## Checks run locally

All run on macOS with `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1`:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --features vetting-pcs --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service --features vetting-pcs --no-fail-fast`: 2859 of 2866 passed on the first run. The 7 failures:
  - Six are `admin_ui::tests::*` (4) and `routing_modes::path_mode_admin_*` (2). They need the real admin-UI bundle, which `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1` skips (CONTRIBUTING notes this). They are unrelated to this change.
  - One was `hidden_vetting_tasks::a_vetter_enrols_draws_and_an_applicant_gets_a_challenge`. My first version of that test used up the unauthenticated limiter's burst of 10 (a 429). I fixed the test, and all 13 `hidden_vetting_tasks` tests pass on the re-run.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service --features vetting-pcs --doc`: ok
- `cargo nextest run -p vti-common`: 625 passed. `cargo test -p vti-common --doc`: ok

title: vta-sdk-v0.63.3
body:
### Fixed

- **vtc**: An administrator may withdraw a member's registry consent, never grant it ([#1962](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1962))

A member's consent to be published in the community's trust registry is
  their own privacy decision, given with `registryConsent` on
  `vtc/join-requests/submit` and copied onto the member record as
  `publish_consent`. `vtc/members/update` let an administrator set it either
  way, so an administrator could publish someone who had said no.

  `vtc/members/update` now only lowers it. `publishConsent: true` for a
  member whose consent is `false` is refused with
  `vtc/members/update:consentGrantForbidden` before anything is written, so
  no other field in the request is applied either. `true -> false` (a
  takedown) and re-stating the current value still succeed. The only way
  consent becomes `true` is the member's own `registryConsent` on a join
  submit, including a rejoin, which writes a fresh member record.

  The specification declares no code for this, so it is minted under the
  task's namespace (Trust Tasks SPEC §8.5) as
  `vta_sdk::protocols::members::MEMBER_UPDATE_ERR_CONSENT_GRANT_FORBIDDEN`
  and listed as consumer-minted in the VTC's error-code census, which fails
  the day the specification declares it.

  A withdrawal already reaches the registry: the `MemberUpdated` naming
  `publishConsent` enqueues an `UpdateMember` job, and the syncer deletes the
  member's record (a delete, not `Departed`). An integration test now drives
  that end to end through the route.

  docs/03-vtc/trust-registry.md no longer tells operators to record consent
  for pre-#1682 members with `publishConsent: true`; that is refused now, and
  such a member gives consent by rejoining.

Release notes

Sourced from hyper-util's releases.

v0.1.21

Additions

  • Add crate-level documentation. (#327)
  • Add client::legacy::Builder::http2_header_table_size() method. (#274)
  • Add client::legacy::Builder::http2_max_concurrent_streams() method. (#274)
  • Add client::legacy::Builder::http2_max_local_error_reset_streams() method. (#277)
  • Add client::legacy::connect::HttpConnector::set_mark() method. (#303)
  • Add rt::tracing::WithSpanExecutor<E>, hyper_util::rt::tracing::CurrentSpanExecutor<E>, and hyper_util::rt::tracing::MkSpanExecutor<E, F> executors. (#323)

Fixes

  • Fix client::legacy::Client so that it properly validates CONNECT responses. (#315)
  • Fix client::legacy::Client to cancel the idle interval once its pool empties. (#292)
  • Fix client::legacy::Client to properly handle IPv6 addresses when using a SOCKS proxy. (#302)
  • Fix client::pool::cache to preserve readiness with clones. (#297)
  • Fix client::pool::cache to wake its waiters in FIFO order. (#298)
  • Fix client::pool::singleton::Singleton to properly handle cancellation. (#299)
  • Fix client::pool::singleton::Singleton to share errors with all waiters. (#296)
  • Fix client::proxy::matcher handling for IP wildcards. (#309)
  • The tokio/net feature is narrowed to the client-legacy feature flag, from the client feature flag. (#276)
  • Various fixes to the client::legacy::Client's SOCKS proxying. (#302) (#307) (#308) (#310)

Changes

This release contains a minor behavioral change for users of the tracing feature flag to be aware of.

This feature flag was introduced in v0.1.11. When enabled, rt::TokioExecutor<E> began propagating the currently active tracing::Span to spawned tasks when hyper::rt::Executor::execute() is called. This caused issues for some users, due to background tasks keeping a span open for the duration of a long-lived connection.

This behavior has now been removed from rt::TokioExecutor<E> (#322) by default. A collection of executor wrappers have been added to a new rt::tracing submodule, to provide facilities for instrumenting a client or server's spawned tasks. See the module-level documentation of rt::tracing for more information.

To temporarily preserve the previous rt::TokioExecutor<E> span propagation behavior, enable the rt-tracing-exec-force feature. Note that this feature flag will be removed in a future release.

This release bumps the rust edition from 2021 to 2024.

  • Add client::legacy::Builder::http2_header_table_size() method. (#274)
  • Add client::legacy::Builder::http2_max_concurrent_streams() method. (#274)
  • Add client::legacy::Builder::http2_max_local_error_reset_streams() method. (#277)
  • Add client::legacy::connect::HttpConnector::set_mark() method. (#303)
  • Add rt::tracing::WithSpanExecutor<E>, hyper_util::rt::tracing::CurrentSpanExecutor<E>, and hyper_util::rt::tracing::MkSpanExecutor<E, F> executors. (#323)

Fixes

  • Fix client::legacy::Client so that it properly validates CONNECT responses. (#315)
  • Fix client::legacy::Client to cancel the idle interval once its pool empties. (#292)
  • Fix client::legacy::Client to properly handle IPv6 addresses when using a SOCKS proxy. (#302)
  • Fix client::pool::cache to preserve readiness with clones. (#297)
  • Fix client::pool::cache to wake its waiters in FIFO order. (#298)
  • Fix client::pool::singleton::Singleton to properly handle cancellation. (#299)
  • Fix client::pool::singleton::Singleton to share errors with all waiters. (#296)
  • Fix client::proxy::matcher handling for IP wildcards. (#309)
  • The tokio/net feature is narrowed to the client-legacy feature flag, from the client feature flag. (#276)
  • Various fixes to the client::legacy::Client's SOCKS proxying. (#302) (#307) (#308) (#310)

Changes

This release contains a minor behavioral change for users of the tracing feature flag to be aware of.

This feature flag was introduced in v0.1.11. When enabled, rt::TokioExecutor<E> began propagating the currently active tracing::Span to spawned tasks when hyper::rt::Executor::execute() is called. This caused issues for some users, due to background tasks keeping a span open for the duration of a long-lived connection.

This behavior has now been removed from rt::TokioExecutor<E> (#322) by default. A collection of executor wrappers have been added to a new rt::tracing submodule, to provide facilities for instrumenting a client or server's spawned tasks. See the module-level documentation of rt::tracing for more information.

To temporarily preserve the previous rt::TokioExecutor<E> span propagation behavior, enable the rt-tracing-exec-force feature. Note that this feature flag will be removed in a future release.

title: chore(vta-sdk): release v0.63.3
body:
## 🤖 New release * `vta-sdk`: 0.63.2 -> 0.63.3 (✓ API compatible changes)
Changelog

## [0.63.3](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-sdk-v0.63.2...vta-sdk-v0.63.3) — 2026-10-05 ### Fixed - **vtc**: An administrator may withdraw a member's registry consent, never grant it ([#1962](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1962)) A member's consent to be published in the community's trust registry is their own privacy decision, given with `registryConsent` on `vtc/join-requests/submit` and copied onto the member record as `publish_consent`. `vtc/members/update` let an administrator set it either way, so an administrator could publish someone who had said no. `vtc/members/update` now only lowers it. `publishConsent: true` for a member whose consent is `false` is refused with `vtc/members/update:consentGrantForbidden` before anything is written, so no other field in the request is applied either. `true -> false` (a takedown) and re-stating the current value still succeed. The only way consent becomes `true` is the member's own `registryConsent` on a join submit, including a rejoin, which writes a fresh member record. The specification declares no code for this, so it is minted under the task's namespace (Trust Tasks SPEC §8.5) as `vta_sdk::protocols::members::MEMBER_UPDATE_ERR_CONSENT_GRANT_FORBIDDEN` and listed as consumer-minted in the VTC's error-code census, which fails the day the specification declares it. A withdrawal already reaches the registry: the `MemberUpdated` naming `publishConsent` enqueues an `UpdateMember` job, and the syncer deletes the member's record (a delete, not `Departed`). An integration test now drives that end to end through the route. docs/03-vtc/trust-registry.md no longer tells operators to record consent for pre-#1682 members with `publishConsent: true`; that is refused now, and such a member gives consent by rejoining.

title: fix(join): a wrapped invitation paste is mended, not refused
body:
Pasting a VIC that the terminal had line-wrapped put raw newlines (plus indentation / `│` panel borders) inside JSON strings — DIDs, proof values — so the paste failed as "not valid JSON".

- `openvtc_core::join::pasted_json_readings(text)`: readings best-first — as given; then with panel borders and zero-width chars stripped per line, and line breaks *inside strings* removed with their surrounding spaces; and a variant keeping one space at the wrap (a wrap that fell on a real space). Breaks between tokens are left alone; escapes are tracked so `\"` doesn't end a string.
- `load_pasted_vic` tries each reading that parses and shape-checks against the invitation's **proof**; the first that verifies is stashed (with an info line saying it was mended). A wrong mend fails verification, so guessing can only refuse a paste, never accept a tampered one.
- The entry-page paste sniffer also sees `{` behind a panel border.

Tests: wrapped/bordered paste mended; wrap-on-space variant; pretty JSON left meaning-identical; escaped quote; end-to-end wrapped VIC through the paste parser. fmt, clippy -D warnings, workspace tests and docs pass locally.

title: fix(vetting): tickets follow the live PCS mode; get tokens in one key; enrolment answers survive restarts
body:
## What was wrong

1. **PCS mode was cached forever.** `hides_vetters()` returned true whenever this client held a hidden-vetting engine for the community, whatever the community published now. So a VTC that turned PCS ZKP off kept gating that vetter's tickets on an enrolment it no longer needed, and attesting still went down the hidden path. The ticket gate decided from that remembered state and never re-read it.
2. **A lost enrolment answer was a month-long dead end.** The blinding that opens a `pcs-root` answer was held only in memory. A restart between the ask and the answer, or a second enrolment asked while the first was in flight (the VTC answers the first and refuses the second with `alreadyEnrolled`), lost it. The VTC issues one credential per member per label and keeps no copy to send again.
3. **Getting tokens was hard to find**, `t` only refused, and a new vetter waited up to an hour ("on the next pass") to enrol.
4. **The manifest was fetched several times in seconds** (repeated `d`, or passes chained on answers).
5. The copy had problems: a doubled `..`, and the full refusal appeared in both the banner and the "You vet for" row.

## What changed

**Live mode (`openvtc-core/src/vetting/mode.rs`, new)**
- The mode is now a *reading* of the join manifest (`vetting.ext` / `org.openvtc.hidden-vetting`, served live from the VTC's stored criteria). It is persisted as last-known on `KnownCommunity::vetter_mode` together with `read_at`. Read failures are kept in memory and say which kind they are: unsent / unanswered / refused / unreadable (R6.4).
- Both the DIDComm and REST manifest paths record the reading. Every consumer now uses the same reading: the badges (Communities, desk, join, journey), the ticket gate, attesting and the drip.
- TTL is 10 min. A stale reading is re-read when the desk is opened, and on the 5 s sweep while the desk stays open, at most once per 2 min per community (R1.4). The desk shows the reading's age or the failure next to the last-known value.

**Tickets**
- `t` asks the community afresh and decides only on an answer that arrived *after* it asked:
  - named → a named ticket with no gate;
  - PCS ZKP → the enrolment/token gate;
  - failure → no ticket, and the message says why.
- The wait is bounded (R1.2). Mode switches are announced ("first-vtc switched from PCS ZKP to named vetting.").
- Tickets record the mode they were issued under, and are marked when that differs from the community's current mode.
- If `t` finds no tokens, it runs the get-tokens pass itself where that can help. Otherwise it says exactly when tokens can come (next window / next label date) and what the operator can do.

**Tokens / enrolment**
- `k` on the desk gets tokens: it enrols if needed, then draws every window that has begun. It reports per community what it is doing or what blocks it. It never draws ahead of the schedule.
- The enrolment blinding is saved to the protected config **before** the request is sent, using a bounded synchronous save. A late answer after a restart still opens.
- No second enrolment is sent while one is unanswered.
- A newly minted engine is saved.
- A received vetter grant runs the vetter side within seconds, and the first draw follows the enrolment answer.
- Manifest re-reads wait ≥30 s after the last ask or answer, and never overlap an open question.

## VTI changes needed (not made here)
- **Unblocking an already-lost enrolment:** `vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-root` should *re-issue* rather than refuse with `alreadyEnrolled` when the member already holds `label` **and** the request presents the same PCS identifier `id` the member is bound to (`EnrolmentRecord.id`).
  - This cannot give one vetter two votes. The credential is bound to `id = Tag(usk, c0)`, every attestation tag derives from `usk`, and applicant proofs require pairwise-distinct tags.
  - Tokens are rate-limited per member/label/tick, independently of the credential.
  - A request under a different `id` stays `identifierRebound`.
- **What an operator can do today:** publish hidden vetting again with a new live period first in `livePeriods`, e.g. `["2026-10b","2026-10"]`. The vetter presses `k` and enrols under `vetter/2026-10b`.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). The ticket's mode read is bounded by the 30 s query window plus a hard 35 s bound. The save-before-send is bounded at 15 s.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). The enrolment blinding is now durable *before* the send. The ticket is created only after the mode answer.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). Mode re-reads are limited to once per 2 min, manifest re-reads to once per 30 s, and save-failure retries are capped by `VETTER_REFRESH_RETRIES`. Concurrent enrolments are no longer sent.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6)
- [x] New/changed wire types: none on the wire. New persisted types are camelCase; `AskedEnrolment` is `deny_unknown_fields`.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*). An unknown or failed mode issues no ticket.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [ ] Deviations: `HiddenVetterState` (`deny_unknown_fields`) gains `enrolmentsAsked`, so a config written by this build will not load in an older build while an enrolment is in flight. This follows the earlier precedent for that struct.

## Tests
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features` and `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc` all pass.

New tests cover:
- a stale reading being replaced;
- a PCS→named switch issuing a named ticket with no gate;
- a named→PCS switch gating the ticket;
- failures being surfaced by kind, plus the bounded wait;
- the lost enrolment message (said once, no `..`, with dates and the operator hint);
- ticket mode marking;
- get tokens (not enrolled → enrol + draw; window drawn → exact next window; lost → hint);
- a stored blinding opening an answer after a restart;
- a refused enrolment dropping its blinding;
- a grant triggering immediate enrolment;
- manifest re-ask throttling.
