Changelog

## `vta-sdk`

## [0.63.2](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-sdk-v0.63.1...vta-sdk-v0.63.2) — 2026-10-05 ### Added - **keys**: Serve keys/sign-sshsig — git commit signing without key export ([#1957](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1957)) did-git-sign exported its persona's key with keys/export-secret on every commit, because keys/sign cannot produce an SSHSIG signature: it frames caller bytes under the opaque-signing domain tag (VTI-VTA-003/007), which is the point of that hardening. keys/sign-sshsig/0.1 (trust-tasks-tf #732, trust-tasks-rs 0.27.6) takes a digest, a namespace and a hash algorithm. The VTA builds the PROTOCOL.sshsig signed data itself and signs it as ProtocolDefined, so the signature verifies as an SSHSIG statement in that namespace and as nothing else. It is gated on a new constrained capability under VTI-VTA-007, `sign-sshsig` (registered upstream as signSshsig), derived wherever `sign` is; `sign` is accepted in its place, and an entry narrowed to sign-sshsig alone cannot reach the generic oracle. Scope, the context signing policy and its daily quota apply through the same chokepoint as keys/sign, and the success is audited once as keys.sign-sshsig with the namespace and digest. The spec's declared codes are rendered: keys:invalidArgument for a digest of the wrong length or an algorithm the key cannot perform, keys/sign-sshsig:failedPrecondition for an inactive key. ### Fixed - **vti-common**: The secret-Debug census knows hidden-vetting token labels are public ([#1958](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1958)) #1956 added `HiddenVettingChangedData.token_labels` (the hidden-vetting audit row), and the workspace census in `vta-sdk/tests/secret_debug_census.rs` flags any `Debug`-deriving field whose name contains "token". The field holds label names (`token/2026-10`, `token/event/`) that every applicant and vetter reads from the join manifest, not tokens, so it joins NOT_SECRET with what it holds. This turned main's `Test (workspace)` job red. - **vtc**: Say why a PCS challenge was refused ([#1954](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1954)) A hidden-vetting proof is bound to a single-use challenge the community issues over vtc/vetting/pcs-challenge/0.1, and the community spends it when the proof arrives. Every way that spend could fail - the challenge expired, was already used, was never issued, or is not the one the proof was built over - reached the applicant as one `malformedRequest` with the cause in a sentence. A client could not tell "you took too long" from "your proof was built over the wrong challenge", which is the difference between "try again" and "your client has a bug". Each failure is now a typed `ChallengeRefusal` that travels from `pcs_challenge::consume` through `pcs::decide`, the vetting facts and the criterion evaluation to the join spine, and goes out on the Trust Task path under a code of its own: - `vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeNotIssued` (details.reason `not_found`) - `vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeAlreadyUsed` (details.reason `gone`) - `vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeExpired` (details.reason `gone`, plus `details.expiredAt`) - `vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeMismatch` (details.reason `conflict`) and the same four local parts under `vtc/join-requests/supplement:` when a supplement carries the proof. Neither specification declares a challenge code yet, so they are consumer-minted under the task's own slug (SPEC 8.5), as `requestAlreadyOpen` is; the constants live in `vta_sdk::protocols::join_requests` for clients to match on, and the error-code census lists them as consumer-minted so it fails the day the specification adopts them. Surfaces that carry no code keep the same 400 `Validation`, now with a sentence that says which failure it was. The message never contains the challenge value. Single-use is unchanged: a submission still spends the challenge whether or not it is accepted, including on a mismatch. The row is now taken atomically (`take_raw`) rather than read then removed, and a spent marker holding no challenge - only the expiry - is left in its place so a second attempt is told "already used" rather than "never issued". An expired challenge is put back as it was so repeated attempts keep saying "expired". Both go at the retention sweep after `expires_at`, as the challenge always did; both writes are `insert_if_absent`, so a challenge asked for in the meantime is never overwritten. Each refusal is logged with its kind and the applicant, never the challenge.
## `vti-common`
## [0.38.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vti-common-v0.37.2...vti-common-v0.38.0) — 2026-10-05 ### Added - **keys**: Serve keys/sign-sshsig — git commit signing without key export ([#1957](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1957)) did-git-sign exported its persona's key with keys/export-secret on every commit, because keys/sign cannot produce an SSHSIG signature: it frames caller bytes under the opaque-signing domain tag (VTI-VTA-003/007), which is the point of that hardening. keys/sign-sshsig/0.1 (trust-tasks-tf #732, trust-tasks-rs 0.27.6) takes a digest, a namespace and a hash algorithm. The VTA builds the PROTOCOL.sshsig signed data itself and signs it as ProtocolDefined, so the signature verifies as an SSHSIG statement in that namespace and as nothing else. It is gated on a new constrained capability under VTI-VTA-007, `sign-sshsig` (registered upstream as signSshsig), derived wherever `sign` is; `sign` is accepted in its place, and an entry narrowed to sign-sshsig alone cannot reach the generic oracle. Scope, the context signing policy and its daily quota apply through the same chokepoint as keys/sign, and the success is audited once as keys.sign-sshsig with the namespace and digest. The spec's declared codes are rendered: keys:invalidArgument for a digest of the wrong length or an algorithm the key cannot perform, keys/sign-sshsig:failedPrecondition for an inactive key. - **vtc**: Hidden vetting (PCS) is turned off, read back and run with events from the console ([#1956](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1956)) * feat(vtc): hidden vetting (PCS) is turned off, read back and run with events from the console Completes the console's hidden-vetting surface on top of #1955, with the three tasks trust-tasks-tf #729 specified (trust-tasks-rs 0.27.5): - `vtc/vetting/hidden/withdraw/0.1` turns hidden vetting off for a criterion. Named vetting is untouched; enrolment rows and the spent-token ledger stay, so a later publish works with the same keys. Withdrawing a criterion with none is `withdrawn: false`, not an error. - `vtc/vetting/hidden/show/0.1` answers an administrator with the stored configuration — each event's `approvedBy` and `graceDays`, which the manifest leaves out — plus how many members are enrolled under each live vetter label and each event's demand against its floor. Counts only, never which members. - `vtc/vetting/hidden/publish/0.1` now holds the approval rules its draft states: a new or changed `approvedBy` must be the publishing signer (`approverNotSigner`) — it was an unchecked string, so an administrator could approve in anyone's name — and an approver who has asked to vet at the event is refused (`approverInEvent`). An approval already stored may be re-sent by anyone, so a re-publish keeps it. - Every publish and withdrawal is audited as `HiddenVettingChanged` (new `vti-common` audit variant; the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`). ### Fixed - **vtc**: Working in the admin console counts toward the idle timeout ([#1953](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1953)) The console signed out operators who were using it. The idle timeout (`auth.admin_idle_timeout`, 900s) is measured from `Session::last_seen`, and only a cookie-authenticated request through the `AuthClaims` extractor advanced it. Most of what the console sends is now a signed Trust Task document to `/v1/trust-tasks`, which authenticates by its proof and reads no session, so a busy operator stopped producing activity. Fifteen minutes after the last cookie-borne call the renewal was refused and the session-deadline watcher showed Login. Counting every signed document would be wrong the other way: the action badge, counts and banners post signed reads on timers, and an unattended tab would never time out. Only the console can tell input from a poll, so: - The console notes real input (pointerdown, keydown, wheel, touchstart) and sends `X-VTC-User-Activity` on a document posted within 60s of some (`admin-ui/src/lib/user-activity.ts`). Timers in an idle tab send none. - The route records activity only for a document that ran successfully, was verified as a known signer, and whose principal (the signer, or the administrator its console key acts for) owns the session the cookie names (`vti_common::auth::touch_cookie_session_for`, which authenticates the cookie exactly as the extractors do). A document signed by one identity cannot keep another's session alive, and a refused one counts for nothing. Renewals and timer-driven reads still never count, so the daemon still decides when an operator who walked away is signed out.

title: fix(vetting): hidden-vetting ticks are windows of time, drawn on a schedule
body:
## Why

`vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-tokens/0.1` now defines a tick as a window of time (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#734, OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1960, trust-tasks-rs 0.27.7). Tick `t` of a label is `[labelStart + t·tickLength, labelStart + (t+1)·tickLength)`. `labelStart` is midnight UTC on the 1st for `token/YYYY-MM` and on the event's `startDate` for `token/event/<id>`. `tickLength` is published in the criterion's `org.openvtc.hidden-vetting` ext, and is `P3D` when absent. openvtc sent whole days since 1970 (about 20000), so a VTC on the new rule refuses every draw as `tickNotYet`.

## Compatibility

**VTI #1960 is merged. A VTC built from VTI main refuses epoch-day ticks, so this has to ship before such a VTC is deployed.** Older VTCs accepted any counter, so they also accept the new ticks.

## What changed

- **Ticks per label.** `HiddenParams.tickLength` is parsed as days/hours with a minimum of `PT1H`. A malformed value falls back to the default and logs a warning. `due()` works out the tick for each label. It owes every tick that has begun and was not served, oldest first, and never asks for a tick that has not begun. A stored epoch-day tick is treated as nothing served and dropped (`settle_ticks`).
- **Schedule.** `hidden_vetting_poll` runs the vetter side shortly after each window opens, with jitter (at most an eighth of the window, capped at 20 minutes), and at least once an hour. It runs whether or not the vetter vetted anyone. `m`, and `d` in the new view, still run it by hand. This replaces the hourly call from #449.
- **Rollover.** Each pass re-reads the manifest of every community the vetter vets for, including ones that already have an engine. It then runs on the published labels, rates, events and tick length (`HiddenVetterState::plan` / `adopt_published`), so a new month re-enrols and draws under the new label. The keys stay pinned. If the published helper or token key changes, drawing stops and the vetter is told once (`rekeyed_at`).
- **Draws in flight (bug found on the way).** `TokenWallet` dropped all pending serials on every `prepare`, and the snapshot never stored them. openvtc restores the engine between every request and its answer, so no served batch could ever be unblinded. Pending serials are now kept per `(label, tick)` and stored in `VetterSnapshot::pending`.
- **Refusals.** `tickNotYet` waits five minutes and shows no notice. `alreadyServed` is recorded as served. Every other declared `pcs-root` / `pcs-tokens` / `event-mode` / `pcs-challenge` code gets a plain-English sentence and is kept for the view.
- **UI.** `h` on the vetting desk opens *Hidden vetting* for each community. It shows the enrolled labels and when each was enrolled, and tokens held, usable and spent (a local counter). It also shows the live token labels, rate and tick length, the last draw, the next window, event requests against the group floor, and the last refusal. `d` or Enter draws now.
- The design doc gains §19.7. The CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` section lists Fixed, Added and Breaking (new struct fields, `TokenWallet::receive` takes the label and tick).

## Tests

New tests cover: tick-of-label (month and event starts, window edges, PT12H, the default and malformed values), catch-up that never draws ahead, migration of old epoch-day ticks, `tickNotYet` / `alreadyServed` / other refusals through the inbound handler, rollover onto live labels and re-enrolment, a key change stopping the drip, several draws in flight surviving a snapshot and answered out of order (pcs crate), the pacer's jitter, retry and hourly floor, the view's rendering, and the `h` / `d` keys.

Run locally, all green: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` (1905 passed, 20 ignored), `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`, and the `dev-overrides` clippy and test.

on the 1st of a token/YYYY-MM label's month or on a token/event/<id> label's
startDate, at the tickLength the community publishes (P3D when absent). The
client sent whole days since 1970 (~20000), which a community on the new rule
refuses on every draw as tickNotYet. Older communities accepted any counter,
so the new ticks work against both.

- HiddenParams reads tickLength (days/hours, at least PT1H; malformed is the
  default with a warning). due() computes the tick per label and owes every
  begun-but-unserved tick of the current label, oldest first, never one ahead
  of the clock; stored epoch-day ticks are read as nothing served and dropped.

  each tick window opens, with jitter, and at least hourly, whether or not the
  vetter vetted anyone. m and the new view's d still run it by hand.
- Each pass re-reads the manifest of every community vetted for and runs on
  the labels, rates and tick length published now, so a new month re-enrols
  and draws under the new label; the keys stay pinned, and if the published
  helper or token key changes the drip stops and the vetter is told once.
- The wallet keeps pending serials per (label, tick) and the snapshot stores
  them. They were not stored at all, and openvtc restores the engine between
  every request and its answer, so no served batch could be unblinded.
- tickNotYet waits five minutes with no notice, alreadyServed is recorded as
  served, and every other declared pcs-root / pcs-tokens / event-mode /
  pcs-challenge code is said in plain words.
- A Hidden vetting view (h on the desk) shows enrolment, tokens held / usable /
  spent, live labels, rate and tick length, last draw, next window, event
  requests against the group floor, the last refusal, and d to draw now.

title: fix(vetting): a finished join leaves the Applications list
body:
## Problem
A vetting application stayed in **Vetting → Applications** after its persona was admitted, next to the joins still under way. Nothing ever removed it; only abandoning (`x`) did.

## Fix
- **Hidden while you're a member:** the Applications list leaves out an application whose persona is an **active** member of its community. If that membership ends, the application reappears. Leaving and rejoining as the same persona then presents the statements it still holds, matching the rejoin rule in #445.
- **Cleared once it can't be used again:** a new `VettingBook::retire_joined(joined, now)` drops an application when its persona is an active member **and** nothing in it could be presented again: every named statement is past `validUntil` and no hidden-vetting attestation is held.
  - It runs on the hourly sweep, which also fires at start-up, next to the cleanup of applications whose persona was deleted (#448).
  - It logs "Cleared N finished vetting application(s) — joined, and its statements have expired."
- **Fits #450:** #450's Communities "Joining" section already hides an application once a membership row exists, so the two agree.
- **CHANGELOG:** entry under `[0.5.0]`.

## Tests
- New core test `a_joined_application_goes_once_nothing_in_it_could_be_presented` covers three applications:
  - joined with nothing to present: removed;
  - joined with a still-valid statement: kept, since a rejoin could use it, until it expires;
  - not joined: untouched.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`: all pass.

title: fix(communities): list joins still being vetted; no "Connecting..." without a community
body:
## Problems

1. **Communities was empty during a join.** An applicant with a vetting application under way and no membership saw "You haven't joined any communities yet … Press j to join your first community". That was true, but it read as though nothing were happening.
2. **The top bar said "Connecting..." when there was nothing to connect to.** With no membership there is no community session. The startup seed set `Connecting`, and `apply_session_aggregate` only moved the indicator when a session changed. With zero sessions nothing ever changed, so it stayed on `Connecting` for the life of the process, even though the persona listener had connected.

## Changes

### Communities: a *Joining* section
- `CommunitiesState` has a new `joining: Arc<[JoiningSummary]>`, built in `sync_from_config` by `joining_summaries`. It holds one row per vetting application that:
  - is for a persona the account still holds (`config.account.personas`), and
  - has **no membership record** for the same community and persona. After a submit, the Pending and then Active row already says everything this row would. A terminal record (left, rejected, withdrawn) also means the application was used; a re-join starts from `j`. An application for the same community under a *different* persona is a separate join, so it is still listed.
- Each row shows the community (display name or shortened DID), "as <persona>", and where it stands, from `vetting_actions::joining_standing`: for example "1 of 1 statement — ready to join" or "0 of 1 statement — waiting for your vetters". The text has no key letters, because the Vetting page's keys (`j`, `c`) do other things on this panel.
- With no membership, the header reads "Not a member of any community yet — you are applying to <X>" (or "to N communities"). The welcome text now appears only when nothing is under way.
- A single cursor covers memberships and then joining rows (`selected_index`; documented on the field). All membership keys take an index into `items`, so they do nothing on a joining row. On a joining row, **Enter** sends the new `VettingAction::OpenApplication(id)`, which calls the existing `focus_application` and opens the application's journey. The key hints show `⏎ open application` there.
- Pending memberships are unchanged.

### Connection indicator
- `apply_session_aggregate` now gets its result from a pure `aggregate_status`:
  - any session up → `Connected`
  - sessions registered but none up → `Connecting`
  - **no sessions → `NoActiveCommunity`**
- The startup seed now always applies it, so an account without a community lands on "No active community" and the activity log says so. Behaviour for accounts with sessions is unchanged. Joining later registers a session, and the indicator moves to Connecting and then Connected as before.

## Tests
- `main_page`: an application with no membership becomes a joining row (community, persona label, standing); a satisfied application reads "ready to join"; a submitted join is not listed twice, while one under a different persona is; an application whose persona was deleted is not listed; the selection can stay on a joining row through a sync.
- `communities_panel`: a join in progress replaces the empty state with accurate wording; several joins are counted; the empty state is kept when nothing is under way; joining rows come after memberships, and the hints on a joining row offer no membership keys.
- `ui::pages::main`: Down reaches a joining row, Enter sends `Vetting(OpenApplication(id))`, and `f` does nothing there.
- `state_handler`: no session gives `NoActiveCommunity` (this clears a leftover `Connecting`); with sessions the result is Connecting, then Connected.

## Checks
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace`
- `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`

CHANGELOG: two new bullets under `0.5.0` → `### Fixed`.

title: spec(appendix): register key-export, room-present and room-open
body:
The capability registry in C.2 omitted three capabilities the reference implementation gates on and the Trust Tasks device-binding Capability enum registers (keyExport, roomPresent, roomOpen). key-export is the separate export capability VTI-VTA-003 requires, implied by administrator alone. room-present and room-open gate rooms/keys/present and rooms/keys/open; each is constrained signing or decryption under VTI-VTA-007's distinction rather than the generic oracle, and split from the other so indexing a room does not confer reading it.

Follow-up to #56, which noted the gap.

title: fix(vetting): a vetter learns a community turned on PCS ZKP, and never signs a named statement for it
body:
## Problem
A vetter for first-vtc saw **⚠ VETTERS NAMED** on a request, although first-vtc now runs PCS ZKP and the applicant saw ✓ PCS ZKP.
- **The vetter's copy is stale.** The vetter side has its own copy of each community's requirements and its own PCS enrolment (`hidden_vetter`). Both are refreshed only by `refresh_vetter_communities`, the hidden-vetting tick, and only from `RefreshRequirements` (`m` on an *application*). A vetter-only member has no application, so in practice it never ran.
- **It's worse than a wrong badge.** `attest` chooses the hidden path by `hidden_vetter(..)`, the enrolment. Without enrolment it signs a **named** statement. That carries the vetter's DID to a community that promised not to need it, and the applicant's hidden-vetting application can't use it.

## Fix
- **A new action:** the vetter part of `RefreshRequirements` is now its own `refresh_vetter_side`, exposed as `VettingAction::RefreshVetterSide`. It re-reads every community we vet for, then enrols or drips each PCS community's schedule. `m` still runs it.
- **It runs on its own:** from the main loop's hourly tick, which also fires at start-up.
- **Attest guard:** if the community's requirements say it hides its vetters (`hidden_vetting` / `hidden_published`) but this vetter isn't enrolled yet, attesting is refused and nothing is signed. The vetter is told "…you are not enrolled for it yet, so nothing was signed. Enrolling now — attest again in a moment.", and the enrolment starts.
- **CHANGELOG:** entry under `[0.5.0]`.

## Tests
- No new unit test: the paths need a live `ActionCtx` (TDK / messaging).
- The change reuses the existing refresh and tick code unchanged; only its triggers and the guard are new.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`: all pass.

title: fix(vtc): the drip is a window of time, a signing-key change never re-keys hidden vetting, and it runs on one criterion
body:
Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#734 (`trust-tasks-rs` 0.27.7) for hidden vetting (PCS).

## Fixes
- **Token draw rate (`pcs-tokens:tickNotYet`).**
  - Before: `tick` was a counter the vetter chose, and only "once per tick" was enforced, so ticks could be drawn back to back.
  - Now: tick `t` of a label is the window `[start + t·tickLength, start + (t+1)·tickLength)`. The start is the first of the month for `token/<YYYY-MM>`, and the event's `startDate` for `token/event/<id>`. A tick that hasn't begun is refused. A begun tick that was never served can still be drawn once, so total issuance under a label is capped at `rate × ticks elapsed`.
  - Code: `HiddenVettingConfig::{label_start, current_tick}` and `pcs_issue::drip`.
- **`tickLength`:** a new publish member, an ISO 8601 duration in days and/or hours of at least PT1H, default `P3D`. It is stored, published and returned by `show`, and a configuration stored before it reads as `P3D`.
- **Signing-key change (`hidden/publish:signerChanged`).**
  - Before: publish re-derived the keys and overwrote them, so a signer rotation or a restore from another key silently broke every enrolled vetter.
  - Now: publish refuses when the stored `hvk`/`tvk` aren't what the signer derives. The deliberate way to re-key is withdraw, then publish under a new period.
- **Second criterion (`hidden/publish:otherCriterion`).**
  - Before: enrolment, the drip and the challenge use the first criterion that has hidden vetting (`pcs_tasks::config_for`), so a second criterion accepted proofs nobody could mint for.
  - Now: publish refuses while another criterion has it on.
- **Console:**
  - the hidden-vetting section shows and edits the tick length, validated in the browser, saved together with the drip rate;
  - "Turn on hidden vetting" is disabled for a second criterion, with the reason shown, instead of only a warning.
- **Docs:** `docs/03-vtc/vetting.md` updated.

## Wire-behaviour change for clients
A client that counts ticks itself (1, 2, 3…) now gets `tickNotYet` for any tick that hasn't begun. Ticks count from 0, from the label's start. openvtc's `zkp-pcs` client will need to compute ticks from `tickLength`. The current test harness already uses past monthly labels, so only the event test changed.

## Tests
- `hidden_vetting_tasks`:
  - `publish_refuses_a_second_criterion_and_keys_its_signer_no_longer_derives` covers `otherCriterion`; `signerChanged` after the stored `hvk` is tampered with; the withdraw-then-publish recovery; and `tickLength` being echoed in `published`.
  - `an_approved_event_opens_its_label_at_the_tier_rate` covers over-quota at tick 0 (nothing recorded), `tickNotYet` at tick 1, then the tick-0 draw.
- `vetting::pcs` unit tests: tick-length parsing (accepted and refused forms), and the tick a monthly or event label is in at a given instant.
- The error-code census has witnesses for the three new codes, and the conformance fixtures carry `tickLength`.
- `HiddenVettingCard.test.tsx`: tick-length edit (an invalid value disables Save), the second criterion's Turn-on disabled, and the drip save carrying `tickLength`.

Run locally:
- PCS-related tests with `--features vetting-pcs`: 72/72.
- admin-ui: vitest 809/809, `tsc -b` clean.
- clippy `-D warnings`: clean on the workspace and on `vtc-service --features vetting-pcs`.
- The full suites (vtc-service with and without the feature, and the vta-sdk censuses) are running; results will follow in a comment.

`Cargo.lock`: only the `trust-tasks-rs` 0.27.5 → 0.27.7 entry changes.

title: fix(vtc): the drip is a window of time, a signing-key change never re-keys hidden vetting, and it runs on one criterion (#1960)
body:
fix(vtc): the drip is a window of time, a signing-key change never re-keys hidden vetting, and it runs on one criterion (#1960)

Three gaps in hidden vetting (PCS), closed with the rules trust-tasks-tf #734
specified (trust-tasks-rs 0.27.7):

- **The drip had no rate.** A tick was a counter the vetter chose, and the
  only rule was one draw per tick — so a vetter could draw ticks 0, 1, 2, …
  back to back. A tick is now the window
  `[label start + t·tickLength, label start + (t+1)·tickLength)`, the label
  start being the first of the month for `token/<YYYY-MM>` and the event's
  first day for an event label. A tick that has not begun is refused
  (`pcs-tokens:tickNotYet`); a begun tick not yet served can still be drawn
  once, so a device that was off catches up and never gets ahead. `tickLength`
  is a new publish member (ISO 8601 days/hours, default `P3D`), stored and
  published; a configuration stored before it reads as `P3D`.
- **A signing-key change silently re-keyed it.** The helper and token keys
  are derived from the credential signer. Publishing after the signer
  changed replaced them without a word, and every enrolled vetter's
  credential stopped verifying. Publish now refuses when the stored keys are
  not what the signer derives (`hidden/publish:signerChanged`); withdrawing
  and publishing again under a new period is the deliberate way to re-key.
- **A second criterion was accepted.** Enrolment, the drip and the challenge
  are served from one configuration (the first criterion that has one), so a
  second criterion accepted proofs nobody could mint for. Publish now refuses
  while another criterion has hidden vetting (`hidden/publish:otherCriterion`).

Console: the hidden-vetting section shows and edits the tick length beside the
drip rate, and "Turn on hidden vetting" is disabled, with the reason, for a
second criterion. docs/03-vtc/vetting.md describes all three.

title: fix(vetting): the directory searches as the application you are on, never a deleted persona
body:
## Problem
After deleting a persona (`make-barrel`) and applying again as a new one (`cloth-best`), searching first-vtc's vetter directory failed:

> The persona the directory would be searched as is not available.

It still failed after a restart.
- **The cause:** `sync` built one `DirectoryCommunity` per *community*, taken from the **first** application to it. The deleted persona's application was still saved in the book, so it came first, and `search_directory` couldn't find an identity to sign the request as.
- **Why a restart didn't help:** deleting a persona (`DidDeleteOutcome::apply`) removed its keys and identity but left its vetting applications in the saved book.

## Fix
- **The directory:** one entry per application whose persona this account still holds (`config.identities`). `open_directory` opens on the application you're looking at, matched by id, so two applications to one community search as their own personas. When there are two, the entries read "community — as <persona>".
- **Deleting a persona** drops its vetting applications, with a log line. Their DID is gone, so they can never be used again.
- **Applications left by earlier deletions** (whose persona has no record in `account.personas`) are cleared on the hourly tick, which also fires at start-up. That's judged on the persona record, not the loaded identity, which can be missing for a run without the persona being gone.
- **CHANGELOG:** entry under `[0.5.0]`.

## Tests
- New `the_directory_never_searches_as_a_persona_that_is_gone`.
- `sync_lists_applications_and_tickets` now gives its persona an identity.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`: all pass.

title: fix: the join page no longer freezes the app when quit
body:
## Problem

On a join page (reported on the vetting page, "Choose how to join"), the app froze: no key worked, not even Esc or F10, and the process had to be killed.

## Root cause

`openvtc/src/state_handler/mod.rs`: when the join flow returned `JoinExit::Exit` (F10 on any join page sends `Action::Exit`, which the join loop turns into `JoinExit::Exit(UserInt)`), the runtime loop broke out with `Ok(join_flow::JoinExit::Exit(interrupted)) => break interrupted`. Every other exit fires `terminator.terminate(..)` first; this one didn't. The state handler then shut down and returned. The UI (`ui/mod.rs`) leaves its loop **only** on an interrupt, and `main` joined the two with `try_join!`, so the screen stayed up. Every key went into an action channel nobody read, and Ctrl-C is just a key in raw mode, so only `kill` ended the process.

The page in the report is the one the join flow draws (requirements already read). F10 freezes it because the join flow handles that key. On the "asking" variant, the runtime loop handles F10 and terminates correctly.

### The inbound-backlog theory, checked and ruled out
- The DIDComm event channel is unbounded (`state_handler/mod.rs`, `mpsc::unbounded_channel()` for `didcomm_event_tx`). The delivery layer's merged inbound is unbounded too (`affinidi-messaging-delivery` 0.1.19 `service.rs`), and its subscriber broadcast drops with a log when it lags; it never blocks. Nothing fills up and blocks while the join flow owns the loop.
- The UI and the handler run in the **same** task on the main thread (`block_on`). crossterm's `EventStream` wakes it from its own thread. So keys, redraws and an idle join loop's `JoinCancel` don't need the worker threads. Even a fully starved runtime could not make Esc do nothing on that page. Only a handler that has stopped, or is stuck in an un-raced await, can.

## Fix
- **Root cause:** fire the terminator on the runtime loop's `JoinExit::Exit`.
- **Structural:** `main.rs` `run_session` replaces `try_join!`. Whenever the handler stops (Ok or Err), it fires the terminator via `Terminator::ensure_terminated`, which never overwrites a reason already given. A missed exit can no longer strand the screen. A handler error now also closes the screen and restores the terminal; before, `try_join!` dropped the UI with raw mode still on. The other direction is bounded too: once the screen has closed, the handler gets `SHUTDOWN_GRACE` (10 s) to finish, then the session ends with an error that names the stall (R1.2).
- **Ctrl-C always quits.** It reaches us as a key in raw mode and no page bound it, so the "Ctrl-C stays live" that the join and setup sequences race the interrupt for was unreachable. The UI now fires the terminator directly, so quitting doesn't depend on the handler reading its actions.
- **Bounded persona connect (R1.2).** In `openvtc-core` `add_listener`, the resolve, authenticate and websocket steps are bounded at 30 s. On timeout the half-opened ATM is shut down, since it has no `Drop` and would otherwise keep the one-socket-per-DID slot, and a distinct "timed out" error comes back (R6.4). The join flow's inline-mint listener start sits on the key path and is now raced against the interrupt.

## Tests
- `main.rs` tests:
  - `the_screen_never_outlives_a_handler_that_stopped_without_saying_so` is the regression test. Confirmed: it times out with the old `try_join!` composition and passes now.
  - `a_failed_handler_closes_the_screen_and_reports_why`
  - `a_reason_already_given_is_not_overwritten`
  - `a_stuck_handler_cannot_hold_the_process_after_the_screen_closed`
- `ui/mod.rs`: `ctrl_c_is_a_hard_quit_and_nothing_else_is`

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide)
- [x] R1.2: outbound waits are finite (listener connect bounded; shutdown bounded)
- [x] R1.4: no new polling loops
- [x] R6.4: distinct error text ("mediator connect timed out after 30s" vs SDK connect errors; "did not finish shutting down" on exit)
- [x] R3.6: no endpoint or shape changes
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`, `cargo doc` with `-D warnings`

F10 on a join page returned JoinExit::Exit to the runtime loop, which

title: feat(keys): serve keys/sign-sshsig — git commit signing without key export
body:
did-git-sign exported its persona's key with keys/export-secret on every
commit, because keys/sign cannot produce an SSHSIG signature: it frames
caller bytes under the opaque-signing domain tag (VTI-VTA-003/007), which
is the point of that hardening.

keys/sign-sshsig/0.1 (trust-tasks-tf #732, trust-tasks-rs 0.27.6) takes a
digest, a namespace and a hash algorithm. The VTA builds the
PROTOCOL.sshsig signed data itself and signs it as ProtocolDefined, so the
signature verifies as an SSHSIG statement in that namespace and as nothing
else. It is gated on a new constrained capability under VTI-VTA-007,
`sign-sshsig` (registered upstream as signSshsig), derived wherever `sign`
is; `sign` is accepted in its place, and an entry narrowed to sign-sshsig
alone cannot reach the generic oracle. Scope, the context signing policy
and its daily quota apply through the same chokepoint as keys/sign, and
the success is audited once as keys.sign-sshsig with the namespace and
digest. The spec's declared codes are rendered: keys:invalidArgument for a
digest of the wrong length or an algorithm the key cannot perform,
keys/sign-sshsig:failedPrecondition for an inactive key.

vta-sdk: TASK_KEYS_SIGN_SSHSIG_0_1 (ReadOnly), VtaClient::sign_sshsig, and
protocols::key_management::sign_sshsig re-exporting the generated types
plus signed_data(), checked against a real ssh-keygen signature. MCP guard
classifies it Sensitive; conformance witness built from the generated
types.

Consumer: OpenVTC/verifiable-git-infrastructure#141 (did-git-sign signs through this task, falling back to export against an older VTA). Spec capability registry: trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#56.

Tests: `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client` — 5374 passed; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt --check` clean. New: signature verifies over the SSHSIG signed data and not over the bare digest or another namespace; narrowed entry refused by the generic oracle; either capability accepted, neither refused before key lookup; both declared refusals; audit row carries namespace + digest; role-derivation parity with `sign`.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.27.7
body:
### Specifications

- **vtc/vetting**: A drip tick is a time window, and publish refuses a changed signer or a second criterion ([#734](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/734))

* spec(vtc/vetting): a drip tick is a time window, and publish refuses a changed signer or a second criterion

  Three holes in hidden vetting's community half, all draft edits in place
  (SPEC §5.2):

  - pcs-tokens/0.1: `tick` was the vetter's own schedule counter, so "once per
    tick" bounded nothing — a vetter could draw tick 1, 2, 3 … in the same
    minute, and the drip, whose purpose is the velocity cap, was unbounded.
    A tick is now a window: tick `t` (t ≥ 0) of a label is
    [start + t·tickLength, start + (t+1)·tickLength), where a label starts at
    00:00:00Z on the first day of its month (`token/<YYYY-MM>`) or on the
    event's `startDate` (`token/event/<id>`). A tick that has not begun is
    refused with the new `pcs-tokens:tickNotYet` (retryable); a begun, unserved
    tick stays drawable once (catch-up), so a member draws at most dripPerTick
    × ticks begun. Zero-based because the schema's `minimum` is 0, which keeps
    the generated `tick: u64` unchanged.
  - hidden/publish/0.1:
    - `tickLength` (ISO 8601 days/hours, at least PT1H, default P3D) in the
      payload, and required in `stored` and `published`; a configuration stored
      before it existed reads as P3D.
    - `signerChanged`: stored keys that differ from what the current signer
      derives are refused rather than silently replaced (every enrolled vetter's
      credential would stop verifying). Re-keying is the explicit
      withdraw-then-publish, under a new period.
    - `otherCriterion`: hidden vetting runs on at most one criterion, because
      enrolment, the drip and the challenge are served from one configuration.
  - hidden/show/0.1: `stored` and `published` carry `tickLength`.

  Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).

title: feat(sender-delegation): a signer names the one sender that may carry its documents
body:
Stacked on #642 (a consumer may require a proof over DIDComm). Draft: a spec to agree on before anyone implements it. Nothing here is released.

## Why

The VTA, the VTC (verifiable-trust-infrastructure #1739) and the did-hosting RP (affinidi-webvh-service #213) act on a DIDComm or TSP document only when its proven signer **is** the transport sender. That rule stays. It leaves no route for a signer that cannot send.

The case that needs one: a browser wallet signing in to an RP as a per-site persona. The persona's keys, key agreement included, are held by its VTA and never released. The VTA can sign as the persona (`vault/sign-trust-task`). It cannot be the DIDComm or TSP sender of the wallet's message. The wallet can send, but only as itself. Today the wallet refuses persona sign-in over DIDComm/TSP and uses REST (`vault/proxy-login`).

## What

`sender-delegation/0.1` is a signed Trust Task document that is never dispatched. The signer issues it to name:

- one delegate: the transport sender allowed to carry the documents;
- one consumer (`recipient`);
- the `id` of each covered document (1 to 16);
- a lifetime of at most 300 seconds (`expiresAt` is REQUIRED).

Its proof is `authentication`, by a key under the signer's `authentication`. It stands in for the transport authentication the signer cannot perform.

A consumer that accepts one:

- still verifies and authorizes each covered document as its own `issuer`. The delegate gains no authority;
- keys replay protection on the document's `issuer` and `id`;
- routes responses to the delegate;
- SHOULD decline delegation for approvals and consent decisions.

Signer requirements: the maintainer signs a delegation only behind the same gates as the covered documents, and only for a delegate the requester is entitled to name.

Privacy: a producer names a **pairwise** delegate for a pairwise signer. Delegating every persona to the wallet's long-lived DID would link the personas at every consumer.

Carriage:

| Binding | Where |
|---|---|
| DIDComm 0.2 §5.1 | a `sender-delegation` attachment on the envelope message |
| TSP 0.1 §5.5 | a `senderDelegation` member of the envelope. Refused in non-nested routed mode, where the authenticated sender is the last hop. |

Generated Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings are included.

## What an implementation would need (not in this PR)

- **VTI (VTA):**
  - `vault/sign-trust-task` must sign a persona's operational documents under `authentication`, with the persona key listed under `authentication`. It pins `assertionMethod` today, so the RP refuses a persona-signed `auth/authenticate` even before delegation comes into it. That means a `0.3` with a purpose, or the maintainer choosing it by type.
  - A way to sign a `sender-delegation/0.1` behind the same gates, restricted to a delegate the caller controls.
- **affinidi-webvh-service (and the VTA/VTC as consumers):** verify the delegation per the consumer requirements in `verify_sender_bound`, before accepting signer ≠ sender. Take it from the DIDComm attachment or the TSP envelope member. Route the reply to the delegate.
- **Wallet:** mint a pairwise transport identity per persona and RP, reachable through its mediator.

## Checks

- `npm run build`: 522 specs validated.
- `npm run check-bindings`: all agree.
- `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all` and `npm run build-ts-bindings`: no drift.

title: spec(auth/step-up): approve-response 0.5, every response carries the approver's assertionMethod proof
body:
Adds `auth/step-up/approve-response/0.5`. Every approve-response now carries the approver's `assertionMethod` proof. Passkey (webauthn) evidence is checked in addition to that proof, never instead of it.

Refs OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1757. That PR already enforces this rule in the VTA and the VTC against 0.4. This version makes the spec say the same thing.

## Why

In 0.4 a `webauthn` response MAY omit the framework `proof`. But the document is the approver's statement of a decision. A WebAuthn assertion signs the challenge, not the document around it. So anyone holding a captured assertion could wrap it in a document of their own and pick its `decision`, `grantedAcr` and `subject`.

## What changes from 0.4

- **`proofRequirement: REQUIRED`.** Every response carries a proof with these properties, whatever evidence it attaches:
  - it is made for `assertionMethod`;
  - its key is listed under the signer's `assertionMethod` relationship;
  - the signer's DID is the `issuer`.
- **The signer is the approver.** That is the subject in self step-up, and the delegated approver in delegated step-up. When the approver signs through a console key that the relying party's own state records as acting for an administrator, the approver is that administrator. In self step-up the approver must be `payload.subject` (`subjectMismatch` otherwise).
- **Passkey evidence is in addition.** A `webauthn` assertion is still checked in full (WebAuthn L2 §7.2). The approver its credential resolves to must be the same approver the proof established.
- **Order.** The consumer checks the proof and ties the signer to the approver before it looks up the pending step-up. A refused document does not use up the step-up, so no other party can spend an approver's challenge.
- **Error codes.** A missing proof is `proofRequired` and an invalid one is `proofInvalid` (SPEC §8.3). `noGate` now covers only an evidence kind the relying party does not recognise or did not offer.
- **Examples.** Every example is signed for `assertionMethod`, including the two webauthn examples.

Nothing else changes: the payload schema is the same as 0.4 apart from the version in its URIs.

## Checks

- `npm run validate`: 522 specs valid.
- Bindings regenerated for Rust (`cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen`, `cargo fmt --all`), TypeScript, Go and Dart.
- `npm run check-bindings`: all four languages agree; 1087 error codes match.
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features --lib approve_response::v0_5`: 3 passed.

title: spec(backup): require an end-to-end confidential channel for backup export and import
body:
## Summary

Three VTA backup tasks now **MUST** be carried over a channel confidential end-to-end between the producer and the recipient, in both 1.0 and 1.1:

- `vta/backup/initiate-export`
- `vta/backup/initiate-import`
- `vta/backup/finalize-import`

DIDComm with authenticated encryption and TSP qualify. A channel confidential only hop by hop does not, the HTTPS binding included.

The same requirement covers the community's backup and the node-neutral family, all 0.1:

- `vtc/backup/export` and `vtc/backup/import`
- `backup/initiate-export`, `backup/initiate-import` and `backup/finalize-import`

## Export record before release

`vtc/backup/export` and every `initiate-export` version (`vta/backup` 1.0 and 1.1, `backup` 0.1) **MUST** now record the export durably **before** the envelope or descriptor is returned. They **MUST** refuse the export when they cannot record it. Previously this was a **SHOULD**. A copy released unrecorded cannot be recalled.

## Why

- **`initiate-export`** carries `password`. Its response carries the descriptor that retrieves the bundle the password unlocks.
- **`finalize-import`** carries `password` for a bundle whose ciphertext may have travelled over HTTPS.
- **`initiate-import`** carries no secret. Its `stream` response, though, carries a bearer credential for writing into the agent. Requiring one channel for the whole import keeps the slot, the password and the commit readable by the recipient alone.

Over HTTPS, TLS terminates wherever the operator terminates it. Whoever holds that point would hold the password next to the bundle, which is every key the agent has.

## What a recipient does

- It refuses any other channel with `permissionDenied`.
- It refuses after it has established entitlement, and before it serializes state, mints a slot or derives a key.
- The refusal **SHOULD** name the bindings it accepts.

The bundle bytes themselves are ciphertext. They may still move over HTTPS (`transportUrl`) or chunk by chunk.

## Change type

This is a prose-only normative change to draft specs. No schema, error code or generated binding changes. `npm run validate` passes.

A sibling of #643. The VTI implementations are OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1733 (VTA) and OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1755 (VTC).

title: spec(device): register the keyExport capability
body:
## Summary

Registers `keyExport` (`key-export` in the `0.1` casing) in the shared device `Capability` enum, and names it in `keys/export-secret/0.1`'s Authorization section.

`keys/export-secret` authorizes against "standing over the key's scope" and leaves the shape of that grant to the implementation. Where the grant is a device capability, there should be a registered value rather than one private value per implementation, as #351 did for `roomPresent` and `roomOpen`. The VTA already gates export on this capability (VTI-VTA-003: export "MUST be gated by a capability distinct from the capability to use the key").

## Changes

- `specs/device/_shared/{0.1,0.2}/device-binding.schema.json` adds the value to `Capability`. The enum is additive, so a consumer that does not recognise it ignores it.
- `specs/keys/export-secret/0.1/spec.md` names the value and states that a custodian **MUST NOT** treat a `sign` grant as a `keyExport` grant, and that `keyExport` confers no other capability. The reason is the one VTI-VTA-002/003 give: a producer that may *use* a key loses that ability the moment its entitlement changes, while a producer that *took* the key keeps it.
- Bindings are regenerated for Rust, TS, Go and Dart. `npm run validate` and `npm run check-bindings` pass.

There are no version bumps and no CHANGELOG entry; release-plz assigns those.

title: feat(git-ns): separation of duties for elevated rights, with an audited break-glass
body:
## What

Separation of duties for git-ns rights, with an explicit break-glass (decision of 2026-09-25).

**Normal rule.** An *elevated* right (`git.ns.admin`, `git.repo.create`, `git.repo.own`) must be granted by someone other than its recipient. Self-grants of `git.repo.maintain` and `git.commit.sign` stay allowed.

**Escape hatch.** A member who already has the authority to grant an elevated right, but cannot give it to themselves, uses `git-ns/right/break-glass`. It takes effect at once, never expires, carries a mandatory justification, and stays flagged, and in front of every other administrator, until one of them ratifies or revokes it.

## Specs

| Spec | Change |
|---|---|
| `git-ns/right/grant` **0.3** | New fixed rule 7, separation of duties: `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`, with a message that names break-glass. The rule is compared after delegation, so a console key cannot grant its principal. A table lists the tasks it also binds: drift/resolve `adopt`, repo/adopt (naming yourself an owner), namespace/reseat (to yourself). `bind` and `repo/create` are explicitly not self-grants. Rules 3 and 4 now count only *counting* records: no `expiresAt`, and not an unratified break-glass. This folds in reseat 0.2's expiring-record reading. |
| `git-ns/right/break-glass` **0.1** (new) | Payload `{right: ElevatedRight, resource, justification}`, with no `subject` and no `expiresAt`. There are two entitlements: grant authority over the right (the usual case is a ns admin taking an explicit `own`), or community admin plus a headless namespace for `git.ns.admin` (reseat to self). `sideEffects: destructive`. The response is not sent until the record and the highest-severity audit event are durable. That event records the justification, the entitlement and the step-up evidence. Every administrator of the namespace gets a signed notice. Policy may disable (`:disabled`), defer (`effectiveAt`) or require more. It can never suppress the audit, the notices or the surfaces. Break-glass is enabled by default. |
| `git-ns/right/ratify` **0.1** (new) | Another administrator clears the flag: a community admin, or a holder of grant authority whose own right is not an unratified break-glass. Never the grantee (`:selfRatification`). The request is bound to the `breakGlass.at` the ratifier read (`:recordChanged`). |
| `git-ns/right/break-glass-notice` **0.1** (new) | The VTC's signed push to every community admin and ns admin of the namespace, for the events `breakGlass`, `ratified` and `revoked`. Policy cannot narrow who receives it. |
| `git-ns/right/revoke` **0.3** | Any community admin may revoke an unratified break-glass record. It never counts toward last-owner/last-admin, and policy cannot refuse the revocation. Revoking one is audited and announced. |
| `git-ns/view` **0.4** | Records carry `breakGlass`. Every unratified break-glass record, with its justification, goes to every community admin, every ns admin of its namespace and every owner of its resource, whatever else the caller may see. |
| `git-ns/_shared` **0.4** | Adds `BreakGlass {by, at, justification, effectiveAt?, ratifiedBy?, ratifiedAt?}`, `RightRecord.breakGlass` and `ElevatedRight`. The registry projection is unchanged, and `breakGlass` is never published. |

## Choices worth reviewing

- **Step-up is not in the spec.** SPEC §7.3 item 13 forbids a spec from declaring a step-up requirement. break-glass therefore requires the audit row to record the evidence of any step-up the VTC applied, and recommends that such a step-up be bound to the request. The VTC (VTI) requires a passkey (aal2, user verification) bound to the request, unconditionally.
- **Ratify is a separate task, not a field on grant.** Its entitlement, its refusals and its instance binding differ from a grant's. A grant of a right the subject already holds through break-glass returns the record unchanged; it never ratifies it as a side effect.
- **Ratified records keep `breakGlass`**, with `ratifiedBy`/`ratifiedAt` set, as history. "Unratified" means `ratifiedBy` is absent.
- **Unratified break-glass does not count toward the invariants.** Otherwise a community admin who reseated a headless namespace to themselves could never be revoked, because they would be the last admin.
- **The rule for drift/resolve, repo/adopt and reseat is stated in grant 0.3**, the way reseat 0.2 stated its last-admin reading for the other tasks, instead of in new versions of each. The next versions should declare `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed` in their `errorCodes`. In particular, **#640** (drift/resolve 0.3) and **#635** (reseat 0.3) should add it along with an adopt/reseat step. This PR does not touch them, to avoid conflicts.

## Coordination

- #640 (drift/resolve 0.3 recipient binding): complementary. Once `subject` is bound, the self-grant check compares `subject` with the resolver.
- #635 (reseat 0.3, bridge/job 0.4): reseat to oneself becomes break-glass.
- #639 edits drift/resolve 0.2 in place. There is no overlap in files.

## Implementations

- VTI (vtc-service, admin console, `cnm`): OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1745. It builds against this branch through a local `[patch]` and needs a `trust-tasks-rs` release carrying these modules before its CI can pass.
- openvtc TUI (Repos panel banner): OpenVTC/openvtc#384.

## Checks

- `npm run build`: passes.
- `npm run check-bindings`: 527 specs agree across TS/Rust/Go/Dart, and 1110 declared error codes match Rust `ERROR_CODES`.
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features` on the new modules passes, including `rejects_invalid_examples`.

No version or CHANGELOG edits. A trust-tasks release is needed before the consumers can leave draft.

title: spec!: conform vetting, member and endorsement credentials to DTG VSC/VAC and the predicate registry
body:
This updates the vetting, witness, member and endorsement Trust Task specs so that every DTG credential they define conforms to the DTG Credentials Core Specification (WD 0.6.0) and the DTG VSC predicate registry.
- Every credential uses the `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v1` context and carries `issuerScope`.
- The retired `EndorsementCredential` and `WitnessCredential` types are gone.

Every spec touched is `status: draft`, so the changes are in place (SPEC §5.2).

This is a **draft** so it lands together with its consumers: dtg-credentials 0.12 (OpenVTC/dtg-credentials#33), then the VTI and OpenVTC migrations. The DTGWG reviewed and agreed the migration plan.

## Credential shapes

| Where | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `vetting/session/0.1` (the Vetting Statement) | `EndorsementCredential`; `endorsement.type` = `https://firstperson.network/endorsements/identity-vetting/0.1` | `StatementCredential` with predicate `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc/vetted/1`. The body is in `object.value` with no `type`, `issuerScope` is `directed`, and `taskDigestMultibase` is now MUST. |
| `vtc/vetting/vetters/grant/0.1`, `vetting/request/0.1` (vetter eligibility) | `EndorsementCredential` with `CommunityRole` | A community-issued `AuthorityCredential`: `authority { scope: <community>, actions: ["role:vetter"], maxAttenuation: 0 }`, `issuerScope: "public"` |
| `vtc/join-requests/decide/0.1`, `vtc/members/{personhood/assert,personhood/revoke,renew,rotate}/0.1` | `roleVec`, a role endorsement | **`roleVac`**, a community-issued VAC with `actions: ["role:<name>"]` |
| `vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.2` | `statementType` = endorsement type URI | `statementType` = the predicate IRI. `eligibleVetters.role` is matched as `role:<role>` in a community VAC. The DCQL examples filter `StatementCredential` + `credentialSubject.predicate`. |
| `vtc/endorsements/*` | mints an `EndorsementCredential` | mints a `StatementCredential`: predicate = registered `typeUri`, `object.value` = the claim, `issuerScope: "public"`. New error code `predicateNotIssuable` for profiles only a member may issue, such as `vetted/1`. |
| `vtc/endorsement-types/*` | `CommunityRole` reserved | Entries are predicate IRIs, and verifiers fail closed on unlisted ones. Roles are never registered. |
| `witness/session/0.1`, `witness/session/submit/0.1` | VWC | `StatementCredential` with predicate `witnessed/1`: subject = issuer of the witnessed credential, `object.digestMultibase`, `issuerScope` at least `directed` |
| `vtc/members/credentials/0.1`, `vault/credentials/{get,receive,query}` examples | `VerifiableMembershipCredential` / no DTG context | Real DTG VMCs. The grant is `public`. The member acknowledgement is `directed`, with the real digest of the printed grant. |

All recomputed `requirementsDigest` and statement digests are reproducible from the printed documents.

## Binding changes (source-breaking)
- **Rust:**
  - `role_vec` becomes `role_vac` (the field, the builder setter and serde) in decide, personhood assert/revoke, renew and rotate.
  - `current_role_vec_id` becomes `current_role_vac_id` in members show/list/update.
  - New error code `PREDICATE_NOT_ISSUABLE`.

title: feat(messaging/message/status): let a sender confirm on evidence that its message was collected
body:
A sender's only signal that a message arrived is seeing it in its send
queue (`messaging/message/list`) and later seeing it gone. That signal is
wrong in both directions.

- A recipient connected live collects within milliseconds, before any poll
  has seen the message queued, so a collected message leaves no evidence
  at all.
- A message leaves the send queue the same way whether the recipient took
  it, the mediator expired it, or its account was removed.

A sender that retries on missing evidence re-sends collected messages. One
that treats absence as delivery records lost messages as delivered.

`messaging/message/status/0.1` answers, per message the requester sent:
`queued`, `delivered` (handed over, not yet acknowledged), `collected`,
`withdrawn`, `discarded` or `unknown`. A conforming mediator records, when
a message whose sender it knows leaves the queue, a short-lived receipt
keyed under that sender, and the reason comes from who removed the
message. The mediator answers only for the requester's own sending and
says `unknown` for everything else, so the task cannot be used to probe
for other accounts' messages.

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in

  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(vtc): hidden vetting can be read and withdrawn, and an event approver names themselves
body:
## Why

Hidden-vetter admission (`vtc/vetting/hidden/publish/0.1`) could be turned on but not off, and its stored configuration could not be read. Because publish replaces `events` wholesale and the manifest omits each event's `approvedBy`, re-publishing from what an administrator *can* read silently un-approved live events. publish/0.1's own Threats section anticipated "a future companion read task".

## What

- **`vtc/vetting/hidden/withdraw/0.1`** (new): turn hidden vetting off for one criterion.
  - Payload `{ criterionId }`; response `{ criterionId, withdrawn, requirementsDigest }`.
  - Idempotent: `withdrawn: false` is a success, not an error.
  - Named vetting is unchanged.
  - Enrolment rows and the spent-token ledger are not deleted. Republishing later derives the same keys.
  - Error: `noSuchCriterion`.
- **`vtc/vetting/hidden/show/0.1`** (new, read-only, proof REQUIRED because it discloses approver DIDs). Response:
  - `{ criterionId, enabled, requirementsDigest }`;
  - when enabled, also `stored` and `published` (same shapes as publish's response), `enrolledVetters` (count per live `vetter/<period>` label), and `eventStatus[]` (`groupFloor`, `groupSize`, `approved`, `live`).
  - Counts only: the community **MUST NOT** disclose which members enrolled or asked.
  - `dependentRequired` keeps the enabled-state members together.
  - Error: `noSuchCriterion`.
- **`vtc/vetting/hidden/publish/0.1`** (draft, edited in place):
  - a new or changed `approvedBy` must be the signer's principal (`approverNotSigner`);
  - an unchanged stored value may be re-sent by any administrator;
  - an approver who asked to vet at the event is refused (`approverInEvent`);
  - audit guidance (who, criterion, deltas — never a reason);
  - Threats now points at `show`.
- Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.

## Checks run locally

- `npm run validate`: 689 specs validated.
- `npm run check-bindings`: all agree; 1515 declared error codes match.
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate,vtc --test conformance hidden`: 15 passed, including both new specs' `rejects_invalid_examples` tests.

title: feat(vtc): live admin console events — a hint-only subscription
body:
## What

- **`vtc/admin/events/subscribe/0.1`**: an administrator's console opens **one live channel per session** with a signed subscribe (console key) naming the topics it renders: `actions | acknowledgements | joinRequests | members | singleAdminMode | config` (minItems 1), plus an optional opaque `since` resume token. The `#response` (effective `topics`, `heartbeatSeconds`, `resumed`, `resumeToken`) is the first document on a stream. Event documents follow it.
- **`vtc/admin/events/event/0.1`**: the hint. It carries `{topic, at, count?, resumeToken}`, with `count` only on `actions`, `acknowledgements` and `joinRequests`. It has no response. Its proof is RECOMMENDED: SPEC §4.7.2 defaults to SHOULD over HTTPS and §7.3 item 8 forbids declaring less, but a console still accepts an unsigned hint, since a hint grants nothing. A hint **MUST NOT** carry record data, record identifiers or personal data.
- **`vtc/admin/events/_shared/0.1/topic.schema.json`**: holds `Topic` and `ResumeToken`, which both tasks use.
- **HTTPS binding 0.3** (`bindings/https/0.3`, registered in `website/assets/bindings.js`): adds §2.1 *Streamed responses*. 0.2 stated explicitly that it defined no streaming variant, so this needed a binding change. It is a MINOR change and additive.

## Design

- **Hints only.** The console reacts to a hint by re-fetching through the existing signed reads, so authorization stays on every read. The stream can neither leak a record nor grant a read.
- **Per-topic authorization.** Each topic is bound to one read. A community sends a topic's hints only to a caller who could perform that read, and checks this for every hint. If the caller's readable topics shrink, the community ends the stream rather than silently narrowing it, and the console's re-subscribe reports the new set.
- **No latched status.** The console shows live only while bytes keep arriving within 2 × `heartbeatSeconds`. When they stop, it shows offline at once and falls back to polling.
- **Resumption.** `since` is in-band. An unknown or foreign token is never an error: the community answers `resumed: false` and the console re-reads every topic, so a token cannot be used as an oracle.

## The binding addition (§2.1)

- The client sends the ordinary `POST /trust-tasks` with `Accept: text/event-stream, application/json;q=0.5`.
- Refusals stay JSON under the §4 status mapping. A stream is never opened to carry an error.
- On success the server answers `200` with `text/event-stream`, and the `#response` is the first event.
- Each event carries one complete document on a single `data:` line, with no `event:` field.
- The SSE `id` carries the task's resume token. Comments are heartbeats, and 2 × the interval with nothing received means the stream is dead.
- Resumption is in-band only. `Last-Event-ID` is a cross-check, and a mismatch is `malformedRequest`.
- Either side may close at any time. A close is not cancellation, no `trust-task-error` is sent after the `#response`, and a stream ends no later than the bearer credential that opened it.
- The lifecycle and security-profile sections gain the matching rows.
- Native `EventSource` reconnection (a bodiless `GET` with no `Authorization`) is deliberately not offered. Every connection and reconnection is a freshly signed request, so the client reads the stream with a streaming `fetch`.

No framework change was needed. `messaging/monitor/subscribe` + `event` already establish the pattern of a `#response` followed by separate fire-and-forget documents on a live connection.

## Checks

- `npm run validate` and `npm run build` pass.
- All four bindings were regenerated, and `npm run check-bindings` reports that all agree.
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --no-default-features --features vtc,validate --test conformance` passes (399), including the 8 new tests.
- `--lib` passes (126) when `acl` is added to the feature set. The lib unit tests reference the `acl` family (`UNIT_TEST_FAMILIES`), so `--features vtc,validate --lib` alone does not compile, and that is not caused by this change.

title: feat(vtc): cooling-off actions, a reduction-pending notice and an offline-write record type
body:
These fill three gaps the VTC implementation found in the `vtc/admin/actions` family (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1920).

### 1. Cooling-off actions: `vtc/admin/actions/_shared/0.2`, and `list`/`show`/`cancel`/`acknowledge` 0.2
Some removals of an administrator have no third party who can consent. These are parked for a cooling-off period (24h by default) and land on their own unless the requester cancels. The 0.1 schema could not express this. The implementation had to leave out `threshold` and `expiresAt`, which the prose says it must not, and put the landing time in `ext`.

0.2 adds:
- `category: coolingOff`
- `landsAt` (date-time)
- `cancellableBy` (closed enum, `requester`)
- `closedReason: landedAfterCoolingOff`
- `callerRole: subject`, so the subject can follow the action

The four task specs are copies of 0.1 pointed at `_shared` 0.2, with minimal prose changes and a "Changes from 0.1" section. Their request payloads and error codes are unchanged. `list/0.2` has three new invalid fixtures for cooling-off actions.

### 2. `vtc/members/authority-reduction-pending-notice/0.1`
VTC → subject, one-way, proof REQUIRED, issuedAt REQUIRED. It is modelled on `authority-reduced-notice/0.1` and sent when a reduction is parked. `authority-reduced-notice` (`agreement: unopposed`) still reports the landing. The prose explains why the subject cannot block the reduction: a veto would protect a compromised subject. The notice gives them time and knowledge instead.

### 3. `vtc/operator/offline-write/0.1`, a record type that is never sent
An acknowledge action needs a Type URI for an offline operator write (`vtc admin emergency-bootstrap` and its siblings), and these commands are not Trust Tasks. This record type gives them one. The action names it as `typeUri` and carries the record `{command, dids[], host, at}` as `payload`.

It declares `sideEffects: none`, proof OPTIONAL and no response. The prose says it is not a request, and that a consumer receiving one answers `unsupportedType`. It extends the registry's existing documents that are never sent on their own (`auth/step-up/approver/attest`, `auth/signing-key/authorize`). It is a spec, not a `_shared` component, because only a spec has the resolvable Type URI that `typeUri` needs. The `acknowledge/0.2` example now uses it.

### Checks
- `npm run validate`: 682 specs; no new warnings.
- Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.
- `npm run check-bindings`: all agree.
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --lib`: 126 passed.
- Conformance tests for the new and changed modules (`--features vtc,validate`), including examples round-tripping through the generated types and the invalid fixtures: 41 passed.

title: spec(git-ns)!: activity/list 0.1 declares the `source` its ActivityItem requires
body:
## Defect

`specs/git-ns/activity/list/0.1/payload.schema.json`: `$defs/ActivityItem` has `required: [at, action, source]` and `additionalProperties: false`, but no `source` in `properties`. The schema is unsatisfiable: no item validates, so no non-empty `#response` does, and a consumer that validates rejects every conforming response. The `Source` enum (`audit` | `job`) sits in `$defs` unreferenced. The spec prose, its examples and the VTC implementation all carry `source`; only the schema lost it.

Not a generator defect: `build-ts-bindings` inlines faithfully. The generators propagated the hole (Rust emitted an untyped `source: serde_json::Value`, the codegen's fallback for a required member with no schema).

Reported by the VTA browser plugin's `packages/core/tests/inbound.consent-schema.mjs` ("no shipped schema requires a member it does not define") against `@openvtc/trust-tasks` 0.22.7:

```
'git-ns/activity/list/0.1/payload.js PAYLOAD_SCHEMA#/$defs/ActivityItem: requires source',
'git-ns/activity/list/0.1/payload.js RESPONSE_PAYLOAD_SCHEMA#/$defs/ActivityItem: requires source'
```

## Fix

- `ActivityItem.properties.source` → `{"$ref": "#/$defs/Source"}`. Draft spec; the schema now accepts the wire its prose and implementation already use, so edited in place (SPEC §5.2).
- `scripts/build-registry.mjs`: the unsatisfiable-schema lint added after `provision/integration/0.3` (#326) checked only the root and `$defs.Response`. It now walks every subschema closed by `additionalProperties: false` (skipping `const`/`enum`/`default`/`examples`). Against main it reports exactly this defect and nothing else.
- All four bindings regenerated.

## Breaking (Rust)

`trust_tasks_rs::specs::git_ns::activity::list::v0_1::ActivityItem.source` changes from `serde_json::Value` to the generated `Source` enum, hence the `!`. Go/Dart gain a typed `Source` field; TS gains `source` on the interface and in the embedded schema.

## Evidence

- `npm run validate`: unfixed spec + new lint → fails with `#/$defs/ActivityItem: required names \`source\`…`; fixed → `Validated 676 specs`.
- `npm run check-bindings`: all agree (676 TS / 671 Rust / 676 Go / 676 Dart).
- `trust-tasks-ts` `npm test`: 79/79. `cargo check -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features`: clean.
- Plugin test against 0.22.7: 10/11 (the failure above). Against this branch's packed `trust-tasks-ts`: 11/11.

title: spec(vtc/vetting): a drip tick is a time window, and publish refuses a changed signer or a second criterion
body:
Three gaps in hidden vetting's community half. All are draft edits made in place (SPEC §5.2).

## pcs-tokens/0.1: a tick is a time window

`tick` was "the vetter's own schedule counter". So "once per tick" bounded nothing: a vetter could draw ticks 1, 2, 3 … within a minute, and the velocity cap the drip exists for was unbounded.

- **Label start:** `00:00:00Z` on the first day of `<YYYY-MM>` for `token/<YYYY-MM>`, or on the event's `startDate` for `token/event/<id>`.
- **Ticks:** tick `t` (`t` ≥ 0) is `[start + t·tickLength, start + (t+1)·tickLength)`. It is zero-based because the schema's `minimum` is already 0, which leaves the generated `tick: u64` unchanged.
- **New `pcs-tokens:tickNotYet`** (retryable): the tick has not begun. `alreadyServed` is unchanged. A begun tick that was never served stays drawable once, as catch-up. A member therefore draws at most `dripPerTick` × ticks begun.
- **A producer SHOULD draw at a random moment inside the window,** as the hidden-vetting design (§5.1) describes.

## hidden/publish/0.1

- **`tickLength`:** an optional payload member, an ISO 8601 duration in days and/or hours (`^P(?:\d+D(?:T\d+H)?|T\d+H)$`, at least `PT1H`), defaulting to `P3D`. It is **required** in `stored` and `published`. A configuration stored before it existed reads as `P3D`.
- **`signerChanged`:** stored keys that differ from what the current signer derives are refused instead of being silently replaced, which would break every enrolled vetter. Re-keying is an explicit withdraw then publish, under a new period. Conformance item 5 now names this code, and the Threats section points to it.
- **`otherCriterion`:** hidden vetting runs on at most one criterion, because enrolment, the drip and the challenge are each served from a single configuration.

## hidden/show/0.1

`stored` and `published` carry `tickLength`.

## Checks

- `npm run validate`: 690 specs.
- `check-bindings`: all agree.
- Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.
- vetting conformance: 46 passed.

title: fix(join): read the current requirements on every join; mark named vetting as a disclosure
body:
## 1. The join page used a stale manifest
After joining against first-vtc, then turning on PCS ZKP there, the join page still said **Vetters: named**. The live manifest does carry `vetting.ext["org.openvtc.hidden-vetting"]`, and I checked that OpenVTC's full path parses it as hidden: `read_mode`, then `read_manifest` (0.3) → `learn_manifest_in` → `hidden_vetting()`. The cause was in `enter_community`:
- Once the book knew the community, `Knowledge::Vetting` / `NoVetting`, the page was built from the stored copy and **never asked again**.
- So a community that turned on hidden vetting, changed its requirements, or started vetting at all still showed what it said before.

**Fix:** a known community is re-read with `learn_over_http` on every join. That's the bounded REST read that needs nothing of us. It also adopts the new manifest into any application under way and records the signing keys. If it fails, the stored copy stands in and the activity log says "Could not read X's current requirements (…); showing what it said last time."

## 2. Named vetting is shown as a disclosure, PCS ZKP as protected
New `badges::vetters_named()` (orange **⚠ VETTERS NAMED**) and a green **✓ PCS ZKP** badge (it was purple). Each comes with `caution()` / `protected()` sentence styles and shared wording:

| | Named | PCS ZKP |
|---|---|---|
| Applicant | "the community will see which vetters vouched for you — each statement carries its vetter's DID" | "…learns that enough vetters vouched for you, not who they were" |
| Vetter | "your statement goes to the community with your DID on it — it will know you vouched for this person" | "your attestation is counted in a zero-knowledge proof — the community never learns it was you" |

**Shown on:**
- the join page ("How it protects you")
- Review and send
- the application's Vetters line
- the desk's "You are" line
- both journey titles (now always badged one way or the other)
- the **attest form, right above "I attest"**, where the vetter signs

## Tests
- Updated `the_page_says_whether_vetters_are_hidden_and_how_it_signs` (the named badge and wording).
- New `the_attest_form_says_whether_the_vetter_is_named`.
- CHANGELOG entries under `[0.5.0]`, which isn't published yet.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`, `cargo doc -D warnings`: all pass.

title: fix(vtc): a departing member who was never published leaves no failed registry job
body:
When a member leaves with `purge`, the VTC queued a `DeleteMember` registry job unconditionally (`registry/syncer.rs` resolved it straight to `SyncAction::Delete`). For a member who never consented to publication, the registry has no record. It refused the delete with `taskFailed` (its answer for an unknown key), the VTC classified that as permanent, and the job failed on its first attempt. It then stayed in the console's Failed jobs until someone discarded it.

## Change
- **`DeleteMember` checks the mirror first**, as `MarkDeparted` already does.
  - With a mirror record, it deletes as before.
  - Without one, the new `SyncAction::DeleteIfPresent` reads the registry and deletes only if the record exists.
  - A transient read failure is retried.
  - A read the registry can't answer falls back to the delete. A purge is an erasure, so a mirror that lost a record must not leave the membership published.
- **`delete_member` treats the declared `registry/record/delete:notFound` as success**, the same tolerance `delete_trust_record` already has.
- **Console copy:** the Failed jobs text pointed at `vtc sync-jobs retry` on a stopped daemon. It now points at the Retry and Discard buttons beside it, and says when discarding is right.
- **Stale doc comment** on `sweep_failed_sync_jobs` corrected: a permanent refusal fails a job immediately.

## Tests
New `registry::syncer` tests:
- `deleting_a_member_who_was_never_published_completes_without_a_delete`: one read, no delete, queue empty.
- `a_purge_deletes_a_record_the_mirror_lost`.
- `a_refused_read_falls_back_to_the_delete`.
