title: perf: raise TEE keys/sign throughput (vsock storage, fewer round trips, multi-core REST)
body:
## Summary

Load tests of the VTA in a Nitro Enclave found that `keys/sign` throughput is capped by serial sections, not by hardware. This PR removes them in seven independent commits, so each can be kept or dropped on its own. Together they take a c6g.xlarge appliance (1-vCPU enclave) from about 80 to about 195 keys/sign per second, and let bigger enclaves use their CPUs: a c6g.4xlarge with a 2-vCPU enclave reaches about 345, and with a 4-vCPU enclave about 380 to 400.

Only one commit depends on another: the one-write framing changes code added by the storage pool. The rest apply on their own.

## Commits

| # | Commit | What | Risk for review |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `fix(vti-common): pool the enclave's vsock storage connections` | All enclave storage went through one connection behind one mutex. Now a pool of up to 8. Also fixes a stale-response bug: a cancelled request could leave its response for the next caller. | Low; enclave builds only |
| 2 | `fix(vta-enclave): log to stderr only while vsock logging is down` | Every log line was also written synchronously to the enclave console, which nobody can read in production. | Low; enclave builds only. CI does not build the `vsock-log` feature, so this is checked by hand only |
| 3 | `perf(vti-common): send each vsock storage request in one write` | Length and payload went out as two packets. Depends on 1. | Low |
| 4 | `perf(vta-service): read the caller's ACL entry once per keys/sign` | Both sign gates read the same ACL row. Both gates still run, in the same order. | Low; authorization code, so worth a careful look |
| 5 | `perf(vta-service): reuse the context record for the keys/sign custody check` | The context row was read for the policy and again for the custody base path. Adds `effective_context_policy_and_record` (vta-support) and `derive_record_key_in_context` (key custody). | Medium; adds a second entry point to key custody. It falls back to reading the context when the record does not match |
| 6 | `perf(vta-service): serve REST on one worker per CPU` | REST ran on a current-thread runtime, so the VTA used at most one CPU. Now multi-threaded with more than one CPU; unchanged with one. | High; affects every deployment. Handlers now run in parallel, not only interleaved at awaits, so existing non-atomic read-modify-writes become likelier to race |
| 7 | `perf(vta-enclave): serve REST on vsock directly, without the inbound socat` | socat forked per inbound connection, and new connections timed out under load. The VTA now binds vsock itself when the entrypoint sets `VTA_REST_VSOCK_PORT`. | High; changes the enclave entrypoint (part of the image measurement) and the boot path: the parent's connections are refused until the VTA binds |

Commits 4 and 5 take a sign from 10 storage operations to 8.

## Results

`keys/sign/0.1` over REST through a load balancer, EdDSA over 32 bytes, from 50 agents in 5 contexts, open-loop stepped rates of 4 minutes each. "Healthy" means no errors and p95 under 150 ms. Approximate saturation in keys/sign per second:

| Build | c6g.xlarge, 1-vCPU enclave | c6g.4xlarge, 2-vCPU enclave | c6g.4xlarge, 4-vCPU enclave |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` before this PR | about 79 (healthy at 70) | not measured | not measured |
| + 1 | about 97 (healthy at 85) | not measured | not measured |
| + 1, 2 | about 165 (healthy at 160) | about 235 to 245 (see note) | not measured |
| + 1 to 5 | about 195 (healthy at 160, p95 63 ms) | about 287 (p95 30 ms at 235, 4 errors) | not measured |
| + 1 to 7 (this PR) | about 195 (healthy at 160, p95 59 ms) | about 345 (p95 114 ms at 320, 13 errors) | about 380 to 400 (p95 41 ms at 320, 7 errors; 309 ms at 400) |

Below saturation the latency gain is larger than the ceiling gain: on c6g.4xlarge with a 2-vCPU enclave at 235/s, p95 was 600 ms with commits 1 and 2, 30 ms with 1 to 5, and 12 ms with all seven.

The "+ 1 to 5" and "+ 1 to 7" rows are this branch exactly, built and run as they are. Note: the c6g.4xlarge figures for "+ 1, 2" and the 600 ms baseline come from builds with extra timing and counter logging, which is not part of this PR. While investigating, each change was also measured one at a time; those runs found commit 6 worth nothing on a 1-vCPU enclave (it keeps one thread there) and commit 7 worth no throughput but removing connect-timeout errors (7 → 0 at 320/s on a 4-vCPU enclave).

## How the bottlenecks were found

- Storage round trips were serial (commit 1), and console logging serialised every request on the stderr lock (commit 2).
- With those fixed, a 2-vCPU enclave sat half idle at its ceiling. The parent answered each storage request in about 33 µs, yet the round trip measured inside the enclave grew from 0.4 ms to about 4 ms under load. The time was the reply waiting for the single REST thread to poll it (commit 6). More storage connections (32 instead of 8) did not help, which ruled out the pool.
- Each sign made 10 storage round trips, 4 of them repeats or reads of data that almost never changes (commits 4 and 5 remove 2; the audit-key cache below would remove the other 2).
- Inbound socat cost little CPU (about 0.2 core) but caused connection timeouts while forking (commit 7).

## Not in this PR (follow-ups)

- **Audit key cache.** Every audited operation reads the active audit key from storage twice (the marker, then the key). Caching it in `AuditKeyStore` saves both, but a cache per store instance misses a rotation through another instance (the VTC builds several on one keyspace), and it breaks `vti_apv_022_a_waiver_that_cannot_be_audited_is_refused`, which simulates an audit outage by deleting the active marker. Needs a design that keeps VTI-APV-022 (a cache per keyspace that fails closed, or a different fault injection agreed for the test).

It is worth doing. It takes a sign from 8 storage operations to 6, and measured against this PR without it:

| Shape | This PR (no cache) | This PR's changes + audit-key cache |
|---|---|---|
| c6g.xlarge, 1-vCPU enclave | about 195 (healthy at 160) | about 220 (p95 193 ms at 220, 0 errors) |
| c6g.4xlarge, 2-vCPU enclave, commits 1 to 5 only | about 287 (p95 30 ms at 235, 4 errors) | about 300 (p95 15 ms at 235, 0 errors) |
| c6g.4xlarge, 4-vCPU enclave | about 380 to 400 (p95 309 ms at 400, 169 errors) | about 475 to 480 (p95 44 to 49 ms at 400, 22 to 43 errors) |

The cache runs used builds with the extra timing and counter logging, which cost some throughput (with a 2-vCPU enclave, all seven commits reached about 345 without that logging against about 310 with it and with the cache), so the cache figures are more likely low than high.

- **Audit chain lock.** Each audited operation holds the chain lock across one storage insert. With a 4-vCPU enclave, releasing the lock before the insert made 400/s fully healthy and cut p95 at 480/s from 374 to 111 ms. That prototype is not crash-safe (a failed insert leaves a gap in the chain), so it needs a design, not this PR.
- **Parent proxy inbound cap.** `MAX_CONCURRENT_CONNECTIONS = 256` in `deploy/nitro/enclave-proxy/src/channels.rs`. With commit 7, the remaining errors past about 400/s are this cap rejecting load-balancer connections.
- **Replies in one write.** The parent proxy still writes each storage reply as two packets.
- **Overload has no back-pressure.** Past saturation, health checks fail and the appliance restarts instead of shedding load.
- **Restart with a large audit log.** The first audited write after a restart reloads the chain head by scanning the whole audit keyspace over vsock. This will be reported separately.
- **CI does not build `vsock-log`.**

## Checks

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`, workspace doctests, and the vtc-service audit tests
- The enclave feature set (`rest,didcomm,vsock-store,vsock-log,tenant-overlay`) checked and linted on Linux
- Pre-existing on `main`, not from this PR: clippy errors in `vta-persona` (`store.rs`), `vtc-service` (`acl/resource_grant.rs`, `git_ns/projection.rs`) and `vta-service` (`routes/mod.rs:656`) with Rust 1.95; `vti_08_context_create_fits_half_a_default_worker_stack` fails on macOS
- Each change ran on real appliances (c6g.xlarge, c6g.4xlarge) as above

title: vta-sdk: keep a trust-task rejection's code and details instead of flattening to Protocol(String)
body:
## Problem
`vta-sdk` turns most trust-task rejections into `VtaError::Protocol(format!("trust task failed [{code}]: {message}"))` (`vta-sdk/src/client/mod.rs`, the rejection mapping before `seal_vault_secret`). The payload's `details` is read only for `unsupportedType` / `unsupportedVersion`. For every other code it is dropped, and the code itself survives only inside a sentence.

As a result, callers:
- can't act on data the VTA already sends, and
- have to string-match the code out of the message to tell rejections apart. That's the drift a typed error is meant to prevent.

## Concrete case
`persona/profile/delete` refuses a bound face with `persona/profile/delete:bound` and `details.personaDids` (`vta-service/src/trust_tasks/persona.rs`, `handle_profile_delete`).

OpenVTC needs those DIDs. A face can be worn by a persona the client can't see from its own memberships, for example another client sharing the VTA or a `pnm` binding. OpenVTC's prompt should say *who* wears the face before it offers to take the face off them.

Because the SDK drops `details`, OpenVTC (OpenVTC/openvtc#430) currently:
- matches `delete:bound]` in the error string, and
- parses the count from "N persona(s) are bound to this profile".

So it can only say "worn by N personas", not which ones. The same applies to the `versionConflict` rejections, whose `details.currentVersion` is also lost.

## Proposal
Add a variant that keeps the rejection as data, for example:

```rust
VtaError::Rejected { code: String, message: String, details: Option<serde_json::Value> }
```

Keep `Display` producing today's `trust task failed [{code}]: {message}` text, so log and error output doesn't change. The existing special cases (`permissionDenied`, `transportUnavailable`, `unavailable`, `unsupportedType`/`unsupportedVersion`) stay as they are.

Possibly add helpers such as `VtaError::rejection_code()` / `rejection_details()`, so callers can match on `code.rsplit_once(':')` for the local part without parsing strings.

## Acceptance
- A `persona/profile/delete:bound` rejection exposes `details.personaDids` to the caller.
- A `…:versionConflict` rejection exposes `details.currentVersion`.
- The `Display` output of existing errors is unchanged.

Once this ships, OpenVTC's `openvtc_core::persona::profile::worn_by` string-match can be replaced with a typed read, and the prompt can name the DIDs.

title: fix(identity): a face worn outside this account's communities is asked about again
body:
## Problem
Deleting a face failed with a dead-end error:

> persona profile delete failed: … trust task failed [persona/profile/delete:bound]: 1 persona(s) are bound to this profile

The delete prompt decides whether to send `unbind` from OpenVTC's binding map. That map is built only from this account's community memberships (`PersonaReadJob::targets`). The VTA counts bindings in every context, so a persona wearing the face anywhere else was invisible to OpenVTC. Examples are another OpenVTC profile sharing the same VTA, or a binding made with `pnm`. In that case the delete went out without `unbind`, the VTA refused it, and nothing on screen offered a way forward.

## Fix
- `openvtc_core::persona::profile::delete` now returns `Deleted::{Done, Worn(n)}`. A `delete:bound` refusal to a delete sent without `unbind` comes back as `Worn(n)` instead of an error. The count is read from the refusal message, because the SDK's `Protocol(String)` drops the payload's `details` (`personaDids`).
- A new `PersonaOutcome::ProfileWorn` re-arms the same delete confirmation with `unbind: true`. Its status line says how many personas outside your communities wear the face and that `y` takes it off them.
- It never retries with `unbind` on the holder's behalf. That would take the face off personas the holder was never told about.

## Follow-up (SDK)
`vta-sdk` turns trust-task rejections into `trust task failed [{code}]: {message}` and drops `details`. Keeping `details` would let this prompt name the persona DIDs instead of only counting them.

## Tests
- `a_bound_refusal_reads_as_worn_with_its_count` (core) checks the message parsing, including a non-bound refusal.
- `a_face_worn_elsewhere_is_asked_about_again_not_failed` checks the re-arm, the status line, and that `y` sends `unbind`.
- `cargo test -p openvtc -p openvtc-core`: all pass. clippy: clean.
- Not yet checked by hand in the TUI.

title: fix(identity): s shows one value while values are hidden
body:
## Problem
On **My Identity → Your attributes**, with values hidden (the default, "values hidden — v to show"), pressing `s` ("show one") did nothing. The selected row kept reading "(hidden)".

## Cause
With values hidden, the listing is fetched without values. `RevealValue` only fetched a value when `is_withheld_sensitive` was true, and that requires values to have been requested. Every other case lifted the mask over the in-memory value, but no value was in memory. `value_line` then drew "(hidden)" as before.

## Fix
`RevealValue` now fetches the one value (`pool::reveal`) whenever the row has none in memory and isn't stale. That covers both the withheld-sensitive case and the values-hidden case. A value already in memory is still only unmasked, with no round-trip, and a second `s` still hides it.

## Tests
- New: `a_reveal_while_values_are_hidden_fetches_the_one_value`.
- `a_reveal_names_one_fact_and_toggles_off`: its fixture now holds values. The test's premise is "the value is already in memory", and the old fixture had none; it only passed because of the bug.
- `cargo test -p openvtc`: 810 passed. clippy: clean.
- Not yet checked by hand in the TUI.

title: fix(identity): a face editor drops references to attributes the pool no longer holds
body:
## Problem
Editing a face that references an attribute no longer in the pool fails on every save:

> persona profile write failed: … validation error: profile references 1 attribute(s) the pool does not hold: 01M44…

The header said "2 ticked", but only one box was ticked. The missing attribute had no row, so it couldn't be unticked and the face could not be fixed from the editor. This happens when two clients share one VTA (and so one attribute pool) and one of them deletes an attribute another's face still uses.

## Fix
- When the editor opens, `live_refs` is split against the pool listing. References to attributes the pool no longer holds are left out of `ticked` and counted in a new `ProfileForm::dropped` field.
- This is only done against a pool that has loaded and read cleanly (`loaded && load_error.is_none()`), so an unreachable VTA never makes every reference look missing.
- The editor shows an orange line, "N attribute(s) this face showed are no longer in your pool — saving removes them from the face", so the change is stated before the save.

## Tests
- New: `the_editor_drops_references_to_attributes_the_pool_no_longer_holds` covers the clean-read case, the failed-read case and the not-yet-loaded case.
- `cargo test -p openvtc`: 810 passed. `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets`: clean.
- Not yet checked by hand in the TUI.

title: fix(join): the cursor can reach Send an open request
body:
## Problem
On the vetting page for a community that vets the people who join, moving the cursor down from **Apply as** took the selection marker away from every row. **Send an open request** could never be highlighted or taken.

## Cause
`KnownVetting::rows()` built the row list from the cursor position: the nested "Apply as" row was only listed while the cursor was on or inside the vetting route. Moving down from it set `row = 3`, the list rebuilt without "Apply as" (3 rows), and index 3 was past the end. Pressing ↓ again wrapped back to the vetting route, and pressing ↑ went back to "Apply as".

## Fix
- `rows()` always includes `ApplyAs`, so each index names the same row no matter where the cursor is.
- A new `KnownVetting::shows()` hides "Apply as" when drawing unless the vetting route is selected. The page looks the same as before.
- A new `KnownVetting::step()` replaces the inline modulo arithmetic. Moving ↓ from the vetting route opens "Apply as". Moving ↑ from below lands on the route itself, never on a hidden row.
- Removed `nested_rows`, `row_is_vetting` and `row_count`, which nothing used any more.

## Tests
- New: `the_cursor_reaches_every_way_in_and_never_rests_on_a_hidden_row` walks the cursor both ways and checks it never rests on a hidden row.
- `cargo test -p openvtc`: 809 passed. `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets`: clean.
- Not yet checked by hand in the TUI.

The vetting page built its row list from the cursor: the nested "Apply as"

title: vti-common-v0.37.2
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: A community serves governance/capability/* — members list its capability modules, administrators enable them, and the trust registry follows ([#1948](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1948))

* feat(vtc): a community serves governance/capability/* — members list its capability modules, administrators enable them, and the trust registry follows

  OpenVTC's Capabilities panel sends a signed governance/capability/list/0.1
  to the community's VTC DID over DIDComm or TSP, and the VTC answered
  unsupportedType: it only ever relayed git-trust writes outward. The VTC is
  the source of truth for which capability modules a community has enabled;
  its Trust Registry is a projection, whose own enable/disable are admin-only
  and only switch which record families it accepts.

  "Capability module" (a pluggable governance capability, git-trust first) is
  kept apart from ACL capabilities throughout: crate::capability_modules,
  trust_tasks::capability_module_tasks, AuditEvent::CapabilityModuleChanged.

  list/enable/disable 0.1 are served on the document spine (DISPATCHED_URIS),
  so DIDComm, TSP and HTTPS route them and discovery lists them; every reply,
  refusals included, is signed, addressed to the requester and threaded.

  - list answers members and administrators (an application entry and unknown
    DIDs get permissionDenied), filters on status as the registry does (absent
    means enabled), and answers the generated #response that
    trust-tasks-capability-client's parse_capability_reply reads. Admins
    holding vtc.config.admin also see each decision's projection in ext.
  - enable/disable need vtc.config.admin (VTI-ACL-030) and a step-up bound to
    the document (VTI-APV-015) — the destructive class. They do not park for
    consent: VTI-APV-018–020 / VTI-VTC-022 ask that of authority-conferring
    acts, and a module confers no ACL authority. config.authority defaults to
    the VTC DID and may name nothing else; any other config member is
    configInvalid rather than silently ignored. Declared codes
    unknownCapability, alreadyEnabled, configInvalid, notEnabled are emitted.

  The decision (version, config, enabledAt/By, generation, projection status)
  is persisted in the community keyspace first and audited; the new
  capability_modules::Projector then sends governance/capability/enable|
  disable as the registry's admin via TrustRegistryClient::
  project_capability_module (TSP > DIDComm selection, schema-checked payload).
  alreadyEnabled/notEnabled are success. Transient failures back off 5 s to
  1 h with jitter; a refusal is marked failed, audited once
  (projectionFailed), warned, and still retried at the cap so fixing the
  registry converges. Results are recorded only against the generation sent;
  no lock is held across the round trip.

  The git-trust manifest is a pinned copy of the registry's; enablement does
  not yet gate [hooks.git-trust] or the git-ns projection.

title: VTC: messaging/message/status reply lost on the 12-minute token-refresh reconnect, bounced as unsupportedType
body:
## What we see

A running VTC logs this pair every **12 minutes**, exactly (:05:20, :17:20, :29:20, :41:20, :53:20):

```
WARN vtc_service::messaging: enveloped Trust Task refused — trust-task-error returned task="https://trusttasks.org/spec/messaging/message/status/0.1#response" thid=… status=422 code=unsupportedType
WARN vtc_service::messaging: received unhandled problem-report — not replying (a reply would loop) from="did:webvh:…:mediator" code=e.p.delivery.refused comment=Message not accepted for delivery
```

It isn't a security problem and no delivery is lost, but it's a real defect and fills the logs with noise.

## Diagnosis so far (not yet confirmed)

1. `affinidi-messaging-delivery`'s `outbox_drain_loop` (every 10s, `vtc-service/src/messaging.rs`) calls `DidCommTransport::outbox_status` → `trust_tasks().message_status()`, which waits for the mediator's reply over the websocket (`send_message(…, wait_for_response = true)`).
2. affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.33.0 refreshes the access token and **reconnects the websocket at 80% of the token's TTL** (`websocket.rs`, `refresh_after_secs`). A 15-minute token gives the 12-minute cadence. The reconnect calls `fail_pending_requests()`, which drops the waiter.
3. The mediator's reply (threaded correctly, `thid` = envelope id, checked against mediator 0.37 `trust_tasks.rs`) then arrives with no waiter. It goes to the VTC's general inbound router, which has no handler for a `#response` and answers with a `422 trust-task-error`.
4. The mediator won't deliver that error (`e.p.delivery.refused`) and sends the VTC a problem-report. The VTC correctly doesn't reply, so it stops there.

The SDK treats the failed `message_status` as "receipts unavailable" and falls back to the outbox listing for that round, so the push itself still settles.

## Open questions

- **Why every cycle?** A ~300µs query on a 10s poll should rarely overlap the reconnect, yet it hit 5/5. Something makes them coincide. Candidates: the refresh's HTTP `refresh()` call is awaited inside the websocket task's `select!` while a query is queued, or the reply is held and flushed after the reconnect.
- **Why is the outbox ever non-empty?** `outbox_status` sends nothing for an empty hop-id list, so a query every cycle means the VTC holds an outbox entry that keeps being polled. Check the outbox keyspace for a member push that never settles.
- Do pushes in flight across a reconnect ever escalate to a second transport (a duplicate delivery to the member) because their receipt was lost?

## Likely fixes

- **SDK (affinidi-tdk-rs):** keep reply registrations alive across a self-initiated token-refresh reconnect, or re-issue the query instead of failing it, so the late reply reaches its waiter.
- **VTC (this repo):** the inbound Trust Task router should never answer an unsolicited `#response` with an error. Drop it with a debug log, the same rule as for problem-reports. Check whether vta-service's router has the same behaviour.
- Consider logging the proactive refresh/reconnect at INFO so this pattern can be read from the logs.

title: Should a VTC's identifier be required to be "public", or may a restricted community be "directed"?
body:
The spec says, in three places that a VTC's identifier can only truthfully be declared `public` ("a community that cannot be found cannot be joined"). This is likely too strong due to the following reasons:

1. __Restricted communities are contemplated.__ The VTC definition says a VTC may be "a family … a company … a nation state." A family community's identifier is likely not something public so that anyone can find it.
2. __Joining is by invitation, not only discovery.__ A prospect joins via a VIC (verifiable invitation credential), which contains the community's identifier. The prospect does not "find" the community — they are invited. So "cannot be found, cannot be joined" does not justify `public`.
3. __"Findable" and "public" are being conflated.__ Resolvability (can the DID document be fetched?) and correlation scope (how widely is the identifier intended to be correlated?) are different properties. A community's identifier must be resolvable by whoever verifies its members' credentials — at minimum, its members — which is `directed`, not `public`


Proposed: a VTC's identifier is `directed` at minimum (its members must be able to find it) and `public` if the community is open to outsiders; never `pairwise` (a community has more than one member). This matches the witness case, which is already "directed at minimum."

Decision: is `public` a hard requirement (every VTC discoverable by anyone, for third-party verification) or a choice (a restricted community may be `directed`)? If a choice, the three places in the spec - (`verifiable_trust_community.md`, `body.md` VMC section ~383, and the Correlation Scope section) - have to be updated; if a requirement, the "family to nation state" range needs reconciling.

title: feat(vtc): a community serves governance/capability/* — members list its capability modules, administrators enable them, and the trust registry follows
body:
## Problem

OpenVTC's per-community **Capabilities** panel sends a signed
`governance/capability/list/0.1` Trust Task — enveloped over DIDComm or TSP — to
the community's **VTC DID**. vtc-service did not serve `governance/capability/*`
at all: the envelope handler reached `dispatch_trust_task_core`, found no arm,
and answered `unsupportedType`. The only capability traffic the VTC had was the
*outbound* git-trust hook relay to its Trust Registry (#681).

Settled architecture: **the VTC is the source of truth for which capability
modules a community has enabled; the Trust Registry is a projection.** The
registry's own `governance/capability/enable|disable` are admin-only (its
`admin_dids`, i.e. the VTC) and only switch which record families
(`git-trust/grant|revoke`) it accepts.

Also: an answered `join-requests/status` poll logged nothing at INFO (only the
re-delivery paths warned), which made a stuck-join investigation read as "no
polls arrived".

## Design

**Naming.** "Capability" already means an ACL capability on an administrator's
entry (#1924/#1927). The new concept is a *capability module* throughout:
`crate::capability_modules`, `trust_tasks::capability_module_tasks`, audit event
`CapabilityModuleChanged`, log text "capability module". The ACL capability that
gates enabling one is `vtc.config.admin`.

**Served tasks** (`trust_tasks/capability_module_tasks.rs`). `list`, `enable`,
`disable` 0.1, wire types from `trust_tasks_rs::specs::governance::capability`
(generated `Payload` / `Response`, `error_codes`), added to `DISPATCHED_URIS`,
so DIDComm, TSP and HTTPS all route them and discovery lists them. Every reply —
refusals included — goes through the spine: signed (`sign_response`), addressed
to the requester and threaded (`respond_with` / `reject_with`, SPEC §4.9).

**State** (`capability_modules/mod.rs`). One row, `capability-modules/state`, in
the `community` keyspace (beside profile/branding; backed up with them): per
module `version`, `enabled`, `config`, `enabledAt`/`enabledBy`,
`disabledAt`/`disabledBy`/`disableReason`, a `generation`, and the registry
`projection` (`pending|applied|failed`, attempts, lastError, nextAttemptAt,
appliedAt). Available modules: `git-trust` 0.1. Its manifest is parsed into the
generated `CapabilityManifest`; no shared crate publishes it, so it is a
member-for-member copy of the registry's (`git_trust.rs`), pinned by
`the_git_trust_manifest_is_the_registrys`.

**`list`** — any member (live ACL entry) or administrator (incl. a console key's
admin); an `application` entry (bridge / external signer — not a membership) and
DIDs with no entry get `permissionDenied`; unsigned REST gets `proofRequired`.
`status` absent ⇒ `enabled`, `available` ⇒ not enabled, `all` ⇒ both — the
registry's `handle_list` filter. Entry shape `{manifest, enabled, enabledAt?}`,
validated against the generated `#response`, parsed in tests with
`trust_tasks_capability_client::parse_capability_reply` (incl. a request built
by the client's own `build_list_document`). Administrators holding
`vtc.config.admin` also get `ext["org.openvtc"].projection`.

**`enable` / `disable`** — `vtc.config.admin` (VTI-ACL-030, via
`capable_signer`; suspended / expired entries refused as elsewhere), then every
check that decides the outcome (declared codes `unknownCapability`,
`alreadyEnabled`, `configInvalid`, `notEnabled`), then a **step-up bound to the
document** (`acl::bound_step_up`, VTI-APV-015) — the VTC's form of the
`destructive` class (vtc-capability-modules.md §4.1; the enable spec asks the
same of disable). Not parked in the action list: second-party consent is what
VTI-APV-018–020 / VTI-VTC-022 require of authority-conferring/-reducing acts,
and enabling a module confers no ACL authority, so single-administrator mode has
nothing to waive. `config.authority` defaults to the VTC DID; any other
authority, or any other config member (e.g. `grantOnRole`, which lives in
`[hooks.git-trust]` and nothing here would read), is `configInvalid` (R3.2).
Companion modules (`delegate`) are not supported yet. Refused without an audit
writer rather than made unaudited.

**Projection.** The handler persists, audits (`CapabilityModuleChanged{enabled|
disabled}`), wakes the projector and answers with `projection.status: pending`;
it never calls the registry. `capability_modules::Projector` (spawned in
`server.rs` when a registry client exists, supervised like the hook relay) sends
`governance/capability/enable|disable` through the new
`TrustRegistryClient::project_capability_module` — on
`MessagingRegistryClient` that is the existing signed round trip with the
registry client's TSP > DIDComm selection (REST has no governance surface →
permanent refusal), payload checked against the published schema before it
leaves. `alreadyEnabled` / `notEnabled` (extended codes, or the registry's
current `taskFailed` + `already_enabled:` / `not_enabled:` prefix) are success.
Transient failures back off 5 s·2ⁿ to 1 h with jitter; permanent ones mark
`failed`, write `CapabilityModuleChanged{projectionFailed}` once on the
transition, warn, and retry at the cap — fixing the registry side converges
without re-sending. A result is recorded only against the generation it was
sent for. No lock is held across the round trip (state lock covers local store
ops only).

**Not in this PR.** Enablement does not yet gate the VTC's own git-trust
machinery (`[hooks.git-trust]` relay, git-ns projection) or discovery; a module
the VTC holds no decision for is never projected (so a registry enabled by hand
is never disabled behind the operator's back).

**`join-requests/status` logging** (second commit). `answer` now logs one INFO
line per answered poll: request id, applicant DID, status, whether it was the
id-less form, whether a resend was asked, `credentialsDelivered`, and the resend
decision. No PII beyond the DID the join logs already carry.

## Files

- `vtc-service/src/capability_modules/mod.rs` — new: definitions, state, plan/commit, audit, projector.
- `vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/capability_module_tasks.rs` — new: the three handlers + tests.
- `vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs` — module, dispatch arm, `DISPATCHED_URIS`, `DISPATCHED_WITHOUT_PROOF` (list's proof is RECOMMENDED).
- `vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/member_tasks.rs` — `acting_party` / `Actor` made `pub(super)`.
- `vtc-service/src/registry/{client,messaging,mod}.rs` — `project_capability_module`, `CapabilityModuleChange`, mock, reply classification + test.
- `vtc-service/src/server.rs` — projector spawn.
- `vti-common/src/audit/{event,mod}.rs` — `AuditEvent::CapabilityModuleChanged` (enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so additive).
- `vtc-service/admin-ui/src/plugins/audit.tsx` — label for the new event.
- `vtc-service/src/routes/join_requests/status.rs` — the INFO line.
- `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/03-vtc/trust-registry.md` — flow + operator docs.

## Tests

Run locally on macOS (Rust stable):

- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` — **2842 passed**, 0 failed (incl. discovery, `dispatcher_routes_every_dispatched_uri`, `the_dispatched_set_declares_the_proofs…`, conformance/error-code census, size census).
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client` — **5362 passed**.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --doc` — passed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.

New tests (`trust_tasks::capability_module_tasks::tests`, `capability_modules::tests`, `registry::messaging::tests`):
- member list on REST/DIDComm/TSP: signed, issuer = VTC, recipient = member, threadId = request id, parses with `parse_capability_reply`; no projection ext for members
- the client's own `build_list_document`, signed, is answered on its thread
- non-member refused `permissionDenied` (signed, threaded refusal); `application` entry refused
- status filter: absent/enabled/available/all before and after enable; bad status → `malformedRequest`
- admin listing carries the projection status
- VTI-ACL-030: moderator / member / stranger refused enable and disable `permissionDenied`, nothing written, nothing projected
- VTI-APV-015: enable without a bound step-up is refused and writes nothing
- enable persists (authority defaulted to VTC DID), handler never calls the registry, projector sends it, status → applied, not re-sent; audit `enabled`, `projected`
- projection failure: transient → pending + backoff; permanent → failed + one `projectionFailed` audit row; then converges
- declared refusals: unknownCapability (slug, version), configInvalid (foreign authority, unknown member), notEnabled, alreadyEnabled
- disable keeps the row, audits the reason, projects only the current generation
- manifest is schema-valid and equal to the registry's; backoff bounded; registry reply classification (extended + legacy idempotent codes)

## Spec / open questions

- **`list` access is host policy, not spec.** `governance/capability/list/0.1`
  declares no access rule ("hosts MAY restrict `available`/`all` listings to
  community members or operators while leaving `enabled` open"). This VTC
  restricts *every* listing to members + administrators. Its proof is only
  RECOMMENDED, so the list URI is in `DISPATCHED_WITHOUT_PROOF` with the reason
  (an unsigned REST caller is refused `proofRequired`; DIDComm/TSP always
  require one at the spine).
- **No access error code declared for `list`** — refusals use the standard
  `permissionDenied`.
- **Which ACL capability gates enable/disable** is not stated anywhere;
  `vtc.config.admin` was chosen (the community's configuration). A dedicated
  capability would need an `acl/_shared` change upstream.
- **Consent class.** Implemented as bound step-up only (see Design). If
  reviewers want N-of-M consent instead, it needs a new `Act`, an action-list
  kind and a pinned summary template (also mirrored in the console).
- **The git-trust manifest has no shared source**; the copy is pinned by test
  against the registry's literal. The list spec's own example adds
  `lifecycleHooks`; the registry's manifest does not, and this follows the
  registry.
- **The registry emits `taskFailed` + message prefix** rather than the declared
  `governance/capability/enable:alreadyEnabled` / `disable:notEnabled`; both are
  accepted here.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide.md §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no new client; the registry round trip's existing 60 s reply window bounds it.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — the state lock is released before `project_capability_module` and re-taken to record the result.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — the VTC is the source of truth; the projection is a resumable pending record keyed by generation, and the registry answers convergently.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — 5 s·2ⁿ capped at 1 h with jitter; enable/disable are convergent at the registry.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — a failed pass is logged and the loop continues; panics restart under the supervisor.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a (no acks/deletes added).
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — generated spec types only; replies validated against the published `#response`; stored state is camelCase + `deny_unknown_fields`; consumer is `trust-tasks-capability-client` (OpenVTC), tested.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — absent `status` ⇒ `enabled`; unknown future status ⇒ `enabled`; no registry ⇒ decision held, projection pending with the reason.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — "acknowledged" only on a registry answer; failures in projection status, audit row and warn log.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — before the state write: nothing happened, the spine released the id; after it: the projector re-drives on the next boot/pass.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none.

## Repo checklist (CONTRIBUTING.md)

- [x] `cargo check` passes for the entire workspace
- [x] `cargo test` passes (see Tests)
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` clean
- [x] New public functions have `///` doc comments
- [x] Security-sensitive changes include tests (auth, ACL)
- [x] Conforms to the VTI specification; cites VTI-ACL-030, VTI-APV-015, VTI-APV-018–020/VTI-VTC-022 (why not consent)
- [x] No divergence to record
- [x] PR title is a conventional commit
- [x] No `version = ` edits
- [x] Commits are signed off (DCO)

title: cnm-cli-v0.27.1
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: A cooling-off suspends its subject, and single-administrator mode can remove now (VTI-APV-019, VTI-APV-022) ([#1944](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1944))

* feat(vtc): a cooling-off suspends its subject, and single-administrator mode can remove now (VTI-APV-019, VTI-APV-022)

  Removing another unrestricted administrator when nobody else can consent
  waits out a cooling-off (acl.removal_cooling_off, default 24 h). Until now
  the subject kept full authority for that whole window, and in
  single-administrator mode there was no way past it.

  Suspension (vtc-action-list.md §8.2). From the moment a cooling-off
  reduction is raised until it lands or is cancelled, the subject's entry
  authorizes nothing. The suspension is set on the entry wherever it is read
  (acl::storage::get_acl_entry / list_acl_entries), and VtcAclEntry::can,
  can_any and can_approve answer false for it, so every gate refuses without a
  per-handler check. The signed administrative door (resolve_admin_claims,
  console keys included), the git-ns door (acting_as), require_capability and
  ACL reads refuse with a message naming the action and when it lands. The
  subject can still sign in, read the action list (callerRole: subject) and
  cancel a request of its own; its event stream carries only actions and the
  mode banner. It approves and decides nothing, acknowledges nothing, and is no
  role assigner for the attrition guard; raising a cooling-off checks the guard
  as though the subject were already gone, and only one cooling-off runs on a
  subject at a time. Its sessions are revoked at suspension, as any reduction's
  are. The row is never changed, so cancelling restores it exactly. A
  suspended subject cannot raise a counter-removal, so the first to act wins
  outright; refuse_if_reduced_first stays as a backstop.

  The suspension is derived from the open action and kept beside the entry as
  a marker (suspended:<did> in the ACL keyspace). admin_actions::save writes
  it before an action that suspends and lifts it after one that no longer does
  (R2.1), so a crash can only over-restrict, and reconcile_suspensions settles
  either half at start (before serving), on every sweep, and after a restore.

  Remove now (vtc-action-list.md §8.5, single-administrator mode only). No new
  task: a reduction's payload carries ext["org.openvtc"].immediate =
  {confirm, actionId?}. confirm must be the subject's DID (or the action id
  being landed), checked before any gesture; the gesture is bound to the
  payload digest, which includes `immediate`, so a gesture for the delayed
  removal is never spent on the immediate one or the reverse (VTI-APV-015).
  Sending the same operation with `immediate` naming an open cooling-off lands
  it now. Refused without the mode (naming the cooling-off and that the mode
  is host-set), on a mismatched confirmation, without the gesture, and by the
  attrition guard. Audited Critical as SingleAdminMode reductionImmediate
  before the write, then AuthorityReducedUnopposed, and the subject is told.
  The landed cooling-off closes landedAfterCoolingOff with ext landedNow; a
  reduction that never waited enters the history with the same marker.

- **vtc**: A subject may relabel its own entry; single-administrator mode is one person under many identifiers (VTI-ACL-052, VTI-APV-022) ([#1941](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1941))

Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#54 and #55 (both merged).

  VTI-ACL-052 item 2 — a subject may change its own entry's label and
  nothing else, on every door that writes it (acl/update 0.1 and 0.2,
  acl/grant re-stating the same entry, vtc/members/update). No step-up: the
  label confers no authority (VTI-ACL-001). The change is audited as a
  MemberUpdated row naming the old and new label and `labelSetBySubject`,
  and the entry carries `label_set_by_subject` (serde-default false,
  cleared when anyone else sets the label), shown to other parties as
  `ext["org.openvtc"].labelSetBySubject` on acl/list and acl/show 0.2 — an
  ext member, so the published response schemas are untouched. A request
  that changes the label and anything else is refused whole. A subject's
  own write never re-affirms a delegation under review.

  VTI-ACL-052 item 3 (as widened by #55) — in single-administrator mode a
  subject whose entry has unrestricted act scope (granting::is_unrestricted:
  a community-admin acting everywhere with its full ceiling) may modify its
  own entry on acl/update/0.2 and acl/change-role/0.2. It takes the
  subject's step-up bound to the operation (VTI-APV-015) and a Critical
  SingleAdminMode{event: selfEditWaived} row written before the write
  (acl::single_admin::authorize_self_edit), and is refused if it would leave
  no live unrestricted entry (narrowing, demoting or shortening the life of
  the only one). Ending the subject's vtc.roles.assign is attrition-checked
  like any removal. Every other self-edit is refused as before, and the
  refusals now say what the subject may do instead.

  VTI-APV-022 ([#55](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/55)) — single-administrator mode waives second-party consent
  whether or not other administrators' entries exist: one person may hold
  an administrator entry per device, and the node cannot tell one person's
  identifiers from two people's. gesture_then_consent_for and the session
  door's require() no longer test for an empty approver set; git-ns rule 7
  is waived the same way (others_eligible is gone). A reduction of another
  administrator (VTI-APV-019) is not parked for a third party's consent in
  the mode: it takes the unopposed path — step-up, notice to the subject,
  Critical row — and keeps its cooling-off, which now lands in the mode even
  with a third administrator present (recheck_cooling_off and the sweeper's
  invalidation skip the "a third party can now consent" check).

- **vtc**: A cooling-off suspends its subject, and single-administrator mode can remove now (VTI-APV-019, VTI-APV-022) ([#1944](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1944))

* feat(vtc): a cooling-off suspends its subject, and single-administrator mode can remove now (VTI-APV-019, VTI-APV-022)

  Removing another unrestricted administrator when nobody else can consent
  waits out a cooling-off (acl.removal_cooling_off, default 24 h). Until now
  the subject kept full authority for that whole window, and in
  single-administrator mode there was no way past it.

  Suspension (vtc-action-list.md §8.2). From the moment a cooling-off
  reduction is raised until it lands or is cancelled, the subject's entry
  authorizes nothing. The suspension is set on the entry wherever it is read
  (acl::storage::get_acl_entry / list_acl_entries), and VtcAclEntry::can,
  can_any and can_approve answer false for it, so every gate refuses without a
  per-handler check. The signed administrative door (resolve_admin_claims,
  console keys included), the git-ns door (acting_as), require_capability and
  ACL reads refuse with a message naming the action and when it lands. The
  subject can still sign in, read the action list (callerRole: subject) and
  cancel a request of its own; its event stream carries only actions and the
  mode banner. It approves and decides nothing, acknowledges nothing, and is no
  role assigner for the attrition guard; raising a cooling-off checks the guard
  as though the subject were already gone, and only one cooling-off runs on a
  subject at a time. Its sessions are revoked at suspension, as any reduction's
  are. The row is never changed, so cancelling restores it exactly. A
  suspended subject cannot raise a counter-removal, so the first to act wins
  outright; refuse_if_reduced_first stays as a backstop.

  The suspension is derived from the open action and kept beside the entry as
  a marker (suspended:<did> in the ACL keyspace). admin_actions::save writes
  it before an action that suspends and lifts it after one that no longer does
  (R2.1), so a crash can only over-restrict, and reconcile_suspensions settles
  either half at start (before serving), on every sweep, and after a restore.

  Remove now (vtc-action-list.md §8.5, single-administrator mode only). No new
  task: a reduction's payload carries ext["org.openvtc"].immediate =
  {confirm, actionId?}. confirm must be the subject's DID (or the action id
  being landed), checked before any gesture; the gesture is bound to the
  payload digest, which includes `immediate`, so a gesture for the delayed
  removal is never spent on the immediate one or the reverse (VTI-APV-015).
  Sending the same operation with `immediate` naming an open cooling-off lands
  it now. Refused without the mode (naming the cooling-off and that the mode
  is host-set), on a mismatched confirmation, without the gesture, and by the
  attrition guard. Audited Critical as SingleAdminMode reductionImmediate
  before the write, then AuthorityReducedUnopposed, and the subject is told.
  The landed cooling-off closes landedAfterCoolingOff with ext landedNow; a
  reduction that never waited enters the history with the same marker.

- **vtc**: A subject may relabel its own entry; single-administrator mode is one person under many identifiers (VTI-ACL-052, VTI-APV-022) ([#1941](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1941))

Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#54 and #55 (both merged).

  VTI-ACL-052 item 2 — a subject may change its own entry's label and
  nothing else, on every door that writes it (acl/update 0.1 and 0.2,
  acl/grant re-stating the same entry, vtc/members/update). No step-up: the
  label confers no authority (VTI-ACL-001). The change is audited as a
  MemberUpdated row naming the old and new label and `labelSetBySubject`,
  and the entry carries `label_set_by_subject` (serde-default false,
  cleared when anyone else sets the label), shown to other parties as
  `ext["org.openvtc"].labelSetBySubject` on acl/list and acl/show 0.2 — an
  ext member, so the published response schemas are untouched. A request
  that changes the label and anything else is refused whole. A subject's
  own write never re-affirms a delegation under review.

  VTI-ACL-052 item 3 (as widened by #55) — in single-administrator mode a
  subject whose entry has unrestricted act scope (granting::is_unrestricted:
  a community-admin acting everywhere with its full ceiling) may modify its
  own entry on acl/update/0.2 and acl/change-role/0.2. It takes the
  subject's step-up bound to the operation (VTI-APV-015) and a Critical
  SingleAdminMode{event: selfEditWaived} row written before the write
  (acl::single_admin::authorize_self_edit), and is refused if it would leave
  no live unrestricted entry (narrowing, demoting or shortening the life of
  the only one). Ending the subject's vtc.roles.assign is attrition-checked
  like any removal. Every other self-edit is refused as before, and the
  refusals now say what the subject may do instead.

  VTI-APV-022 ([#55](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/55)) — single-administrator mode waives second-party consent
  whether or not other administrators' entries exist: one person may hold
  an administrator entry per device, and the node cannot tell one person's
  identifiers from two people's. gesture_then_consent_for and the session
  door's require() no longer test for an empty approver set; git-ns rule 7
  is waived the same way (others_eligible is gone). A reduction of another
  administrator (VTI-APV-019) is not parked for a third party's consent in
  the mode: it takes the unopposed path — step-up, notice to the subject,
  Critical row — and keeps its cooling-off, which now lands in the mode even
  with a third administrator present (recheck_cooling_off and the sweeper's
  invalidation skip the "a third party can now consent" check).

title: fix(capabilities): wait on a request's thread before sending it
body:
## Problem

**1. A fast reply was lost to the send that asked for it.** Pressing `c` (Capabilities) on an Active community showed *"no reply within 30s — the community's governance host may be offline"*. The VTC had in fact answered in about 300µs, with a signed `trust-task-error` (`unsupportedType`). A retry showed the right text, *"this community does not offer capability management"*.

The view armed `pending_thid` only when the spawned send's outcome was applied (`CapabilityOutcome::apply`). The reply comes in on the inbound channel and the outcome on the dispatch channel, so a fast reply could be applied first. `apply_capability_replies` then saw `pending_thid == None` and dropped the reply without a log line, and the 30 s sweep failed the view. The Repos panel had the same pattern for every git-ns send (`ReposOutcome::apply` armed `view.pending`, and `link.poll` for polls).

**2. A refusal was reported as a replay of itself.** A `trust-task-error` is offered to the capability view first. `community_reply_proven` verifies it **and records it** in `seen_documents`. It then falls through to the git-ns arm and to the join refusal arm. There `community_document` checked it again, found it already recorded, and logged `WARN unverified community refusal ignored reason=it was already acted on (replay)`. This also broke real join refusals. A genuine join refusal also passes the capability arm first, so it hit the same check, and the pending join was **never marked Rejected**. The new join test fails that way without this fix.

**3. Members are offered capability enable/disable.** Enabling and disabling capabilities is for VTC administrators only. A member who tried got the refusal as a bare code.

## Fix

**Bug 1: wait on the thread before the send starts** (`capability_actions.rs`, `repos_actions.rs`, `mod.rs`)
- The request document is built on the loop thread (`CapabilityJob::prepare` and, for repos, `git_ns::build` in `Loop::send`). Its `correlation_thread` (the doc id) is the `threadId` the reply carries. The view or link-poll slot is armed with it and `sent_at` **before** `spawn_dispatch`. The job only signs and sends; signing never changes the id. The persona secret is already resolved on the loop, as before.
- A send that succeeds reports nothing. A send that fails clears the wait and shows the error, but **only if the view is still waiting on that request's thread**. A late failure for an older request no longer ends a newer request's wait (or a different community's).
- `openvtc-core`: `git_ns::build` (unsigned; `build_signed` now wraps it). `capabilities` re-exports `correlation_thread` and adds a `RequestDocument` alias. `send_capability_document` threads and returns `correlation_thread(doc)` instead of the bare `doc.id`, which is the same value for every document we build. The shared crate is unchanged; replies are still classified with `parse_capability_reply`.
- A capability or git-ns reply that matches nothing pending is now logged. It is `warn` for a listing, toggle or git-ns answer. For a refusal it is `debug`, because every `trust-task-error` is offered to both views, whatever it refuses, so a refusal that is not ours is routine. The default filter (`openvtc=debug`) still records it.

**Bug 2: a refusal is checked once per pass** (`message_dispatch.rs`, join `trust-task-error` arm)
- If the refusal was already proven and recorded earlier in the same `process_inbound_message` pass (`reply_proven == Some(true)`), the join arm skips the second `community_document` check:
  - If the refusal's `thid` matches a pending join of ours, it goes to `handle_join_trust_task_error` as before. It is already recorded, so it is not committed again.
  - Otherwise it is let go with a debug line. Before, it went on to the misleading "trust-task-error did not match a pending request id" warning.
- Replay protection across messages is unchanged. A refusal not proven earlier in the pass goes through `community_document` exactly as before, and the same refusal delivered again is still refused (tested).

**Bug 3: enable/disable is for administrators, and a refusal says so** (`capability_actions::toggle_refusal`, `capabilities_panel.rs`)
- **Decision: keep `e`, explain the refusal.** The client cannot tell beforehand whether the persona is an administrator of the VTC:
  - Administration is the VTC's own ACL (an `admin` role there), which a member cannot read.
  - The role VAC a member holds names the roles it was issued with (normally `member`), not the current ACL. A later promotion or demotion is not reflected in it.
  - The community profile carries nothing about the viewer's role.

  Hiding `e` on that basis would sometimes hide it from real administrators. Instead, a `permissionDenied` (or `forbidden`) refusal of a toggle now reads *"only the community's administrators can enable or disable capabilities"*. Other refusals keep their code and message. The footer hint is now `e enable/disable (administrators)`.

## Tests

- Capabilities (`capability_actions.rs` tests):
  - `a_reply_that_overtakes_the_send_is_still_matched`: the `unsupportedType` refusal lands before the send's outcome, still produces "does not offer capability management", and the outcome does not re-arm the view.
  - `a_toggle_reply_that_overtakes_the_send_is_still_matched`
  - `a_late_failure_for_a_superseded_request_keeps_the_current_wait`
  - `another_communitys_request_does_not_touch_the_view`
  - `a_member_refused_a_toggle_is_told_it_is_for_administrators`
  - `another_toggle_refusal_keeps_its_code`
  - The existing tests were updated to the arm-then-outcome flow.
- Repos (`repos_actions.rs` tests):
  - `a_reply_that_overtakes_the_send_is_still_matched`
  - `a_poll_answer_that_overtakes_the_send_is_still_matched`
  - `a_late_failure_for_a_superseded_request_keeps_the_current_wait`
  - `a_failed_poll_frees_its_slot`
  - The existing outcome tests were updated.
- Dispatcher (`message_dispatch.rs` tests): both tests run a signed refusal through the real off-loop check and capture `WARN` output.
  - `a_capability_refusal_is_not_reported_as_its_own_replay`: the refusal reaches the capability view, no replay or "refusal ignored" warning is logged, and redelivering it is still refused.
  - `a_join_refusal_still_rejects_the_pending_join`: `permissionDenied` on our submit marks the join Rejected.
  - With the Bug 2 fix disabled, both tests fail.

### Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test --workspace`: all passed (openvtc bin 808, openvtc-core 887, plus integration suites; 0 failed). The `openvtc-vetting-pcs` `wire_fixture` test, which is known to be flaky under the parallel run, passed this time.
- Not exercised against a live VTC; the race is covered by the unit tests above.

### Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new clients
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): the wait is armed before the send, but it is display state that a failure clears and the reply window bounds; nothing is persisted
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): unchanged
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): a failed link poll frees its slot and is retried on the next tick, as before

title: fix(capabilities): wait on a request's thread before sending it (#427)
body:
fix(capabilities): wait on a request's thread before sending it (#427)

Pressing `c` on an Active community reported "no reply within 30s — the
community's governance host may be offline". The VTC had in fact
answered in about 300µs, with a signed trust-task-error
(`unsupportedType`), and a retry showed the right text: "this community
does not offer capability management".

The view armed `pending_thid` only when the spawned send's outcome was
applied. The reply comes in on the inbound channel and the outcome on
the dispatch channel, so a fast reply could be applied first. It found
nothing pending and was dropped without a log line, and the 30 s sweep
then failed the view. The Repos panel had the same pattern for every
git-ns send, link polls included.

The request document is now built on the loop thread, before the spawn.
Its id is the thread the reply carries (`correlation_thread`), so the
view waits on it from that point. The job only signs and sends; signing
never changes the id. A send that succeeds reports nothing. A send that
fails clears the wait only if the view is still waiting on that
request's thread, so a late failure cannot end the wait of a newer
request. git_ns gains an unsigned `build` so the Repos path can do the
same, and `send_capability_document` threads on `correlation_thread`
instead of the bare id (the same value for every document we build).
A capability or git-ns reply that matches nothing pending is now
logged. It is a warning for a listing, toggle or git-ns answer. For a
refusal it is a debug line, because every trust-task-error is offered to
both views, whatever it refuses.

A refusal was also reported as a replay of itself. A trust-task-error is
proven and recorded by the capability arm (`community_reply_proven`) and
then falls through to the join refusal arm. `community_document`
checked it again there, found it already recorded, and logged
"unverified community refusal ignored … (replay)". A genuine join
refusal also passes the capability arm first, so it hit the same check,
and the pending join was never marked Rejected. The new test fails that
way without this fix. When the refusal was already proven in this pass,
the join arm now skips the second check. If the refusal matches no
pending join of ours, the arm lets it go with a debug line. Replay
protection across messages is unchanged: the same refusal delivered
again is still refused.

Enabling and disabling capabilities is for administrators only. The VTC
refuses anyone else with `permissionDenied`. The client cannot know in
advance whether the persona is an administrator. That is the VTC's ACL,
which a member cannot read, and a role VAC lists the roles it was issued
with, not the current ACL. So `e` stays available, but that refusal now
reads "only the community's administrators can enable or disable
capabilities", and the hint says `e enable/disable (administrators)`.

title: feat(vtc): a suspended subject's git rights are withdrawn from the registry and the forge until its cooling-off closes (VTI-APV-019)
body:
**Stacks on #1944 and must merge after it.** Until #1944 merges this PR's diff against `main` includes #1944's commits. The changes here are `a323cf3f`, `0a90c11b` and `faedf826`. Once #1944 lands I'll rebase onto `main`.

## What and why

#1944 suspends the subject of a removal cooling-off. The VTC refuses everything the subject signs, but #1944 left one gap (its follow-up note): the **git-ns projection still published the subject's git rights**. Its Trust Registry records stayed up, including the implied `git.commit.sign`, so the community's commit check kept passing its commits. Its forge roles also stayed in every `desiredRoles`. Both lasted until the removal landed.

With this PR, a suspended holder is **projected as holding nothing** (`vtc-action-list.md` §8.2, VTI-APV-019):

- its registry records are withdrawn: explicit rights, the implied `git.commit.sign` of `own`/`maintain`/`ns.admin`, and any role-derived grant this projection owns;
- its linked accounts leave every repository's `desiredRoles`, so the bridge takes off the roles it gave. This works the same way as an unlinked account (git-namespaces.md, *Linking*);
- a repository created during the suspension gives it no role, and a drift revert never sends one back;
- **the pull-request gate counts none of its rights and not its role** (`faedf826`). It reads rights through `ProjectionView::effective_on`, so a suspended owner or maintainer is not always allowed, its reopen is no override, and its VTC role counts toward no `roles` level. It is still a member until the removal lands, so a `members` level still admits it. Membership is not authority.

**Nothing is deleted.** The rights stay recorded on the entry. Cancelling republishes, from the stored rights, exactly what they still give. When the removal lands, the rights go with the entry and nothing already withdrawn is withdrawn again.

## Design: reconcile, not events

The projector already re-derives everything on every pass: the registry diff against the mirror, and role projection by digest. So the cheapest crash-safe design is to make the projection's **input** a pure function of the stored rights and the suspension markers. No event path is involved.

- **`projection::ProjectionView`** is the stored records with every row of a subject holding a `suspended:<did>` marker left out. It is a **separate type from `Snapshot`**. It lends out row slices and the (unfiltered) namespace and repository records, but never a `Snapshot` or a `RightsSet`. Every write path loads its own `Snapshot` and writes with `put_rights`, so none of them can be given the view and persist the filtered rows. `Snapshot::load` is unchanged, as #1944's note asked.
- These consumers now read the view: registry `reconcile`, `bridge::project_roles`, `desired_roles_now` (drift revert), `desired_roles_for_repo` (repo create), `withdrawal_pending` (which has to agree with reconcile), and `projection/show`'s `pendingChanges`. `verify` and `role_mapped` are unchanged. Role-derived tuples are filtered in `desired_with`, not in `role_mapped`, because unbind's hand-back to the hook relay still reads `role_mapped`.
- **R2.1:** the marker is the only state. A crash after the marker and before the withdrawal, or after the lift and before the republish, converges on the next pass, including the first pass after a start. #1944 already orders marker → record → lift.
- **Landing race:** an `executing` action is still open, so the marker is held through the effect and lifted only after the record closes. A pass between the effect and the lift finds the rows already gone, so it withdraws nothing twice and republishes nothing.
- **R1.1:** role changes go through the existing `git_ns_jobs` queue and `dispatch_due` (`send_v0_4`, 0.4/0.5 only, retried until the bridge answers). Nothing is sent inline, and nothing is treated as delivered on a bare send `Ok`.

## Audit

`GitNsOperation` rows with target = the subject and detail = `{actionId, rights: <count>}` (plus `landsAt` on the first):

- `gitNs.projection.withheld`: a suspension now withholds a holder of git rights;
- `gitNs.projection.restored`: the suspension ended with rights still recorded (cancelled, or a demotion that keeps them), so they are republished;
- `gitNs.projection.released`: it ended with nothing left (the removal landed).

**Severity: normal (Info).** These rows record a mechanical consequence that only *removes* what is published. They bypass no control. The decision behind them is already audited at its own severity: the action's `raised`/`completed`/`cancelled` rows, and `AuthorityReducedUnopposed`/`SingleAdminMode` at `Critical` for an unopposed landing. A second high-severity row per suspension would only add noise. The projector writes these rows before its audit tail runs, so the row wakes the same pass. The order is audit first, then the record of what was audited: a crash between the two can give a duplicate row, never a missing one. The count only, never which rights, and never a grant's `reason`.

## Not done / follow-ups

- Grants that the v0.1 `[hooks.git-trust]` relay publishes **outside** every bound namespace are not the projection's, so they are not withheld. This is documented.
- Withdrawal takes effect on the next projector tick (`git_ns.tick_seconds`), not synchronously with raising the cooling-off.

## Boot ordering

`reconcile_suspensions` now runs **before** the git-ns projector is spawned (`server.rs`), so the projector's first pass never reads a marker the action list does not hold. #1944 already put it on the startup path. It is bounded local-store work: one pass over the action list and the markers, with no network and no wait on another task. So the startup path still reaches its shutdown select (mediator-connection invariant 1).

## Docs

- `docs/03-vtc/git-namespaces.md`: new *While its holder is suspended* section.
- `docs/05-design-notes/vtc-action-list.md`: §8.2 bullet and an as-built row.
- `docs/03-vtc/admin-access.md`: the cooling-off bullet.
- Console: the cooling-off card now says the subject's git rights are withdrawn.

## Tests

Unit tests in `vtc-service/src/git_ns/tests/suspension.rs`. They use the real projector pass (`Projector::run_once`), `reconcile`, `project_roles`/`dispatch_due`, the `FakeBridge`, and `MockRegistryClient`:

- `suspension_withdraws_projected_git_rights_without_deleting_them`
- `suspended_subjects_commit_signing_right_is_not_published`
- `cancelled_cooling_off_republishes_exactly_what_was_withdrawn`
- `bridge_receives_role_withdrawal_on_suspension_and_reprojection_on_cancel`: a queued `projectRoles` job without the subject's account, then one with it back at `git.repo.maintain`
- `landing_after_suspension_removes_rights_once`
- `reconcile_converges_projection_after_crash_between_marker_and_withdraw`: also covers a registry failure on the first pass
- `write_paths_never_persist_the_projection_view`

I disabled the filter in `ProjectionView::of` to check these tests: all 7 fail without it.

Pull-request gate tests (`git_ns/tests/pr_gate.rs`): `pr_gate_ignores_a_suspended_holders_rights`, `pr_gate_ignores_a_suspended_holders_role`, `pr_gate_counts_the_rights_again_after_cancel`. If the gate reads an unfiltered view, all three fail.

Integration tests (`tests/it/cooling_off_suspension.rs`) over a **real** cooling-off (`vtc/members/admin-remove` between two admins) on the signed spine:

- `cooling_off_withdraws_the_subjects_git_projection_and_cancel_restores_it`
- `landed_cooling_off_leaves_nothing_to_withdraw_twice`

Results (local, macOS, RAM disk):

- `TMPDIR=/Volumes/RAMDisk VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1 cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client -p cnm-cli --no-fail-fast`: 2946 run, 2940 passed, 6 failed, 1 skipped. All 6 are the ones the skip flag is known to fail: the four `admin_ui::tests` and `routing_modes::path_mode_admin_{bare_prefix,trailing_slash}_serves_admin_spa`.
- `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1 cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1 cargo check --workspace --all-targets`: clean.
- admin-ui (after `npm ci`, `package-lock.json` unchanged): `npx vitest run` → 65 files, 788 tests passed; `npm run lint` → exit 0.

title: fix(join): an id-less poll's answer resolves the join that never got a reply
body:
## Problem

A member joined a VTC. The VTC approved the join and lists them as a member, but OpenVTC still shows the join as **Pending** with "no response from the community yet".

#226 added the recovery for this: when we hold only our own placeholder id, the status poll leaves the request id out and the community answers with its own. But `handle_join_status_response` correlates strictly by `requestId`. The answer carries the community's id, which matches nothing we hold, so it is dropped with `status-response did not match a pending request id — ignoring`. The #226 commit message says the handler "already calls `confirm_request_id`". It never has (checked with `git log -L`).

## Fix

- `Account::membership_awaiting_request_id`: finds the Pending membership for the VTC that still holds our placeholder. If several personas are waiting, the reply's `to` decides, and an ambiguous reply resolves nothing.
- `handle_join_status_response`: falls back to that membership when no record matches by id, then adopts the community's id with `confirm_request_id`. The adopted id is persisted whatever the status says.
- A `pending` answer now stamps acknowledgement, because the VTC knows the request, so the "no response" warning clears.

For an approved join, recovery then runs on the existing path. `approved_at` is stamped, and the next poll after the grace period carries `resendCredentials`. The VTC re-sends, because it counts delivery by the member's reciprocal VMC, which this client never sent. The credential is matched to the record by VTC and persona, so it activates the membership. This requires a vtc-service that includes VTI #1900, which answers an id-less poll for an already-approved request.

## Tests

- `an_id_less_poll_answer_resolves_the_join_that_never_got_a_reply`: the field scenario.
- `an_id_less_poll_answer_still_pending_acknowledges_and_adopts`
- `an_id_less_poll_answer_goes_to_the_persona_it_was_sent_to`
- `status_response_with_mismatched_request_id_is_ignored` now holds a confirmed id, which is the case it was always about.

`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` is clean. `openvtc-core` passes all 887 tests. `openvtc-vetting-pcs`'s `wire_fixture` failed once during the parallel workspace run (fixture `NotFound`). It passes on its own, both with and without this change, so it looks flaky and is unrelated.

title: feat(repos): manage checkouts and commit signing from the Repos panel
body:
## Summary

A developer can now see and manage their community's repositories and commit signing from the Repos panel. did-git-sign still does the signing behind it.

- **What's on this machine.** Each repository shows its local state: not cloned, signed, not signing, or signing as another identity. A repository's screen adds an *On this machine* section with:
  - the checkout's path, branch, ahead/behind and changed files;
  - whether commits there are signed as this persona;
  - whether `HEAD` is signed and carries the `Signed-by-DID:` claim `verify-trust` checks.
- **One key per action:**

  | Key | Action |
  |---|---|
  | `c` | Clone into `<workspace>/<forge>/<owner>/<repo>`, set did-git-sign up if needed, and make the checkout sign |
  | `e` / `E` | Make a checkout sign as you (`did-git-sign enable --profile`) / stop it |
  | `u` | Adopt an existing checkout, once its `origin` proves to be the repo |
  | `s` / `S` | Set up or repair did-git-sign (re-prove the credential, rewrite an outdated hook) / remove the identity and revoke its credential |
  | `w` | Workspace directory and HTTPS/SSH |
  | `p` | Copy a checkout's path |

- **A narrowed credential, not the account's.** openvtc mints a `did:key` for did-git-sign and grants it `admin` of the persona's own context, narrowed to `key-export`. The previous (removed) wizard copied openvtc's account admin credential, which can reach every persona. Before anything is stored, the grant is proven: the new credential exports the key, and it must be the key the persona's DID document publishes. If the proof fails, the grant is revoked. Personas whose keys sit in the account's top context are refused. No `did-git-sign init` or `pnm` step is needed.
- **The signing row no longer depends on the directory openvtc was started in.** It now reports:
  - the persona's did-git-sign profile and keyring credential;
  - whether the `did-git-sign` binary git runs is on `PATH` (≥ 0.14);
  - did-git-sign's own commit-msg hook.

### Commits
1. `chore(deps)!`: `vta-sdk` 0.63, `trust-tasks-rs` 0.27, `affinidi-tdk` 0.23, `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.33, `did-git-sign` 0.15.1. 0.15.1 is the signer on VGI `main`; 0.16.0 changed only vgi-bridge and vgi-core. `cargo tree -d` shows no duplicate vta, trust-tasks or affinidi crate. Two code changes came with it:
   - the join submit body now carries `criterion` natively;
   - the tests that answer as a pre-0.3 community derive the dropped `manifest/0.2` response type themselves.
2. `feat(core)`: `git_workspace` and `git_signing`.
   - `git_workspace`: locating, inspecting and cloning checkouts. Resources are parsed strictly before reaching a command line or path, and every git call passes `--`.
   - `git_signing`: grant, prove, install, status, enable/disable, remove.
3. `feat(repos)`: the panel. It adds two dispatch domains, `GitWorkspace` and `GitWorkspaceProbe`, so local work never waits on a `git-ns` send. A probe runs on open, when the view lands, after each change, and every 20 s. Only explicit probes read the keyring.

### Worth knowing
- **The VTA releases a private key only over DIDComm or TSP, never REST.** So did-git-sign signs through the VTA's mediator. The e2e (`git_signing_e2e`) runs against `MockVta::start_with_transports()`, which needed the `transport-harness` dev feature.
- **Proving the grant connects as a fresh `did:key`, so the VTA's mediator must admit unknown DIDs.** did-git-sign's own `init` and every later signature already depend on this.
- **Wipe now removes did-git-sign's identity for every persona** in the profile, not only the detected default. It has no VTA session, so it logs each granted credential with the `pnm acl delete` that revokes it.
- **Not covered here:**
  - A private HTTPS clone needs a git credential helper; openvtc never prompts.
  - The `did-git-sign` binary is installed separately; the panel says how.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test --workspace`: 884 core + 796 TUI pass. New tests cover:
  - resource parsing and injection refusal, remote matching, status parsing;
  - a real local clone read back;
  - profile naming, grant shape, checkout signing classification;
  - reducer, outcomes, key map and rendering.
- [x] `cargo test --workspace -- --ignored`: all MockVta / mediator suites pass. This includes the new `git_signing_e2e`, which checks that:
  - the grant exports Alice's key and is refused Bob's;
  - revocation works, and revoking twice is a no-op;
  - openvtc's own DID is never revoked;
  - a mismatched key is refused and leaves no grant;
  - the top context is refused.
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`
- [ ] Manual run against a live VTA + forge: set up, clone, commit, and check that `verify-trust` passes

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). VTA calls are wrapped in a 30 s timeout. `git clone` is bounded at 15 min, and `did-git-sign enable`/`disable` at 30 s.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). The grant is proven before the keyring and profile are written, and a failed write revokes the grant.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). There are no retries; a failed step reports and stops.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). The probe is periodic and stateless, and a failed probe is simply superseded.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). The previous credential is revoked only after the new one is stored.
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*). None are new; the ACL grant uses the SDK builder.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*). There is no VTA backend or session → no setup. Top-context personas are refused.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*). Clone errors tell credentials, SSH, not-found and network apart (R6.4). A panicked job clears its busy marker and says so.
- [ ] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1). **Deviation:** if openvtc dies between the ACL grant and storing the credential, an orphaned grant remains. It is narrowed to one persona's `key-export`, and its private key was never written anywhere, so it cannot be used. It shows up in `pnm acl list` labelled `did-git-sign · … (openvtc)`.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers
