* Make second-party consent recommended practice, with single-administrator mode as the declared way not to apply it

VTI-APV-014 and -018 to -020 become SHOULD: second-party consent is the
recommended practice, but a community run by one person has no second party.
VTI-APV-022 is reframed accordingly: a node that does not apply those
recommendations MUST do so only through single-administrator mode, whose own
guard rails stay MUST (enabled only from the host, never waiving consent where
another eligible party exists, reported in every session, audited at highest
severity). VTI-APV-019's notify-and-audit floor still applies whenever a
removal proceeds without another party's consent.

title: fix: a failed listener rebuild is retried, not forgotten
body:
## Summary

After a laptop slept, the TUI sat on `Connecting...` indefinitely. The activity log stopped at two `Listener '…' is still disconnected (no transport error reported)` lines, and only a restart brought the listeners back.

**Cause.** `supervise_transports` rebuilds a listener that has been down for longer than `REBUILD_GRACE` (90 s). It removes the listener before adding it again, because the mediator allows one socket per DID. If `add_listener` failed, nothing was left installed: the spec was gone with the wire, and with no transport there was nothing for the supervisor to see as down. `down.retain(live)` then dropped the tracking, so one failed attempt stranded the listener for the life of the process. Sessions still existed with no listener behind them, which `apply_session_aggregate` renders as `Connecting...`. After a wake, the first rebuild is likely to fail because it races a network that is not back yet.

Rebuild attempts and failures also went only to `tracing`, so none of this reached the activity log. `LifecycleLog::Restarting` existed but was never emitted.

## Fix (`openvtc-core/src/didcomm.rs`)

- `MessagingInner::stranded` holds the spec of each listener whose rebuild failed. The supervisor records it before each add and clears it on success. Stranded listeners are candidates on every pass and are retried on the existing backoff (5 s → 60 s cap, never giving up).
- `Messaging::remove_listener` clears a stranded entry, so a deliberate removal (community left) is not resurrected. If anyone else re-installs the id (a manual reconnect or a re-join), the supervisor's claim on it ends.
- One pass is now `supervise_once(service, down, now)`, so tests can drive it with a clock that is already past the grace period.
- A supervisor broadcast channel feeds the activity log: `restarting (attempt N, …)` and a new `LifecycleLog::RestartFailed`, which renders as "could not be restarted (attempt N): `<transport error>` — retrying in Ns" (R6.4).

## Companion SDK fix

affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#926 fixes the two SDK defects that made the listener fail to recover by itself: a websocket connect with no timeout, and a missed-pong watchdog that never fired. This PR covers the case those don't. A transport that does end up stranded is no longer stranded forever. openvtc is still locked to `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.32.1, so it gets #926 only once that is released and bumped here.

## Tests

- `a_failed_rebuild_is_retried_not_forgotten`: an unreachable spec stays stranded after a failed attempt, `Restarting` and `RestartFailed` are broadcast, the next attempt waits out the backoff, and then it is retried.
- `removing_a_stranded_listener_stops_its_rebuilds`.
- All 9 `supervisor_policy_tests` and the TUI lifecycle-log tests pass. `cargo clippy -p openvtc-core -p openvtc --all-targets -D warnings` and fmt are clean.

Not yet verified by a real sleep/wake cycle. To check, run with `OPENVTC_DEBUG_LOG`, sleep the laptop, wake it, and look for the restart lines followed by a reconnect.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). `add_listener`'s connect wait is bounded by the SDK (10 s); #926 bounds the socket connect.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3). The `stranded` mutex is a std mutex, never held across an await.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). The stranded spec is recorded *before* the add, which is what makes a failed add resumable.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). Existing `rebuild_backoff`.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). This is the fix.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). Unchanged.
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*). None.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*). N/A.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*). Rebuild failures now reach the activity log with their error.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1). `stranded` is in-memory; a restart rebuilds listeners from config.
- [x] Deviations flagged. None. One known race is unchanged from before: a community left *during* an in-flight rebuild can be re-added by that rebuild.

fix: a failed listener rebuild is retried, not forgotten (#421)

The supervisor rebuilds a listener by removing it and then adding it again,
because the mediator allows one socket per DID. If the add failed, nothing was
left installed: no wire to read the spec from and no transport to see as down.
The listener was stranded for the life of the process, and the indicator sat
on `Connecting...`. Waking a laptop from sleep triggers it: the first rebuild
races a network that is not back yet.

Specs of failed rebuilds are now held and retried on the existing backoff
(5s → 60s cap). A deliberate `remove_listener` clears them, so a left
community is not resurrected. Rebuild attempts and failures, with the
transport's error, now reach the activity log. Before, they went only to
tracing.

title: Add DTG nodeType property
body:
The [WD02 base structure for DTG credentials](https://trustoverip.github.io/dtgwg-cred-spec/#base-structure) still does not include a property identifying the type of DTG node to which a credential is being issued.

This is how all DTG participants can have an unambiguous shared understanding of the types of nodes with which they have relationships — and apply policy against this metadata (canonical example: applying [proof of personhood](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2408.07892) policies to a `person`).

Proposal: in WD03 (aka WD 0.3.0) under the `CredentialSubject` property, add a subproperty following the `id` property

- `nodeType` (string, REQUIRED): MUST include exactly one of `"person"`, `"device"`, `"agent"`, `"VTC"`, or `"VTN"`.

title: ci(deps): hold rand_chacha with rand 0.8
body:
Dependabot proposed `rand_chacha` 0.10 (#418). It implements the newer `rand_core`, while `openvtc-vetting-pcs` passes the `ChaCha20Rng` to `Issuer::generate`, which is bounded by rand 0.8's `RngCore + CryptoRng` — so `from_seed` stops resolving and every build fails.

This adds `rand_chacha` to the Dependabot ignore list next to `rand`, which is already held at 0.8 by the OpenPGP stack. Lift both together. When that happens, check that `Issuer::derive` still produces identical keys, since it derives each community's long-lived keys from this stream.

Supersedes #418.
author: stormer78

title: fix: the TUI starts on Windows (Initial console modes not set)
body:
## Problem

On Windows, `openvtc.exe` exits immediately with:

```
Error: Initial console modes not set
```

`setup_terminal` and `restore_terminal` (`openvtc/src/ui/mod.rs`) sent crossterm's `DisableMouseCapture`, though mouse capture is never enabled. On Windows crossterm 0.29 always executes that command through the WinAPI (`is_ansi_code_supported` is `false`), restoring a console mode only `EnableMouseCapture` saves. With none saved it errors, and `?` aborted startup. On Unix it is an escape sequence and harmless.

## Fix

Drop both `DisableMouseCapture` calls — there is nothing to disable.

## Testing

- `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets` clean (macOS).
- **Not yet run on Windows** — needs confirmation from the tester that the TUI now opens.

Note: `EnableBracketedPaste` would still fail on a legacy console without VT support (crossterm returns `Unsupported` there); Windows Terminal and modern PowerShell/conhost are fine.
author: stormer78

title: feat(cnm): setup onboards the personal VTA the way pnm does — self-minted key, grant, rotate
body:
feat(cnm): setup onboards the personal VTA the way pnm does — self-minted key, grant, rotate

`cnm setup` used to require a sealed bundle from an administrator before cnm
could touch the personal VTA. It now follows pnm's admin cold start: mint an
ephemeral did:key, park it, print the grant routes (`vta import-did`,
`admin_did` in setup.toml, `pnm acl create`), and on
`cnm setup continue [<name>] [--vta-did <did>] [--vta-url <url>]` authenticate,
which rotates to a fresh did:key over `acl/swap-key` and removes the temp DID's
entry. A continue before the grant prints the routes and stays resumable.
Non-interactive mode mirrors pnm (#1753): `cnm setup --name <name>
[--overwrite]` and `continue --vta-did` each print one `{slug, admin_did,
state}` line.

Alternatives in the wizard:
- "Bootstrap from your existing pnm session" when a pnm profile on this
  machine ($PNM_HOME honoured) is bound to the same VTA DID. pnm's config and
  session store are read only; pnm's key authenticates in memory once, over
  REST (so no mediator socket is taken from a running pnm), to grant cnm's
  own freshly minted key, which then rotates as above. The grant is an
  unrestricted admin: cnm creates a top-level context per community on the
  personal VTA, which the VTA gates on super-admin.
- "I have a sealed bundle from an admin" — unchanged, digest pinned.

Communities now get an admin identity each, so one operator's communities
share no key. `cnm community add <name> [--vtc-did] [--vta-did] [--slug]
[--overwrite]` mints a did:key for that community, parks it in
`pending_communities` (not selectable by --community or as default until
confirmed), and prints the VTC grant routes: `co_admin_did` in vtc setup,
`vtc acl add` offline, or an existing admin's `cnm access grant` / console,
noting the second-administrator approval an online unrestricted grant waits
for. `cnm community continue <slug> [--vtc-did] [--vta-did]` confirms with a
DI-signed authenticate to the VTC (VTC audience) before promoting the
profile. The VTC has no key-rotation task (no acl/swap-key; a successor admin
entry is itself an unrestricted grant needing a second admin's consent,
VTI-APV-014), so the minted key is kept rather than a rotation invented.
Reusing another community's key takes `--reuse-identity <community>` (or an
explicit, warned choice in the wizard). `cnm community list` shows each
community's identity and the pending ones; `delete` drops a pending one.
Holding a community identity as a persona on the personal VTA is a follow-up.

Docs: getting-started ("Administering from cnm"), bootstrap-runbook,
admin-access walkthrough, CLAUDE.md cold-start flow.

feat(cnm): setup onboards the personal VTA the way pnm does — self-minted key, grant, rotate (#1923)

`cnm setup` used to require a sealed bundle from an administrator before cnm
could touch the personal VTA. It now follows pnm's admin cold start: mint an
ephemeral did:key, park it, print the grant routes (`vta import-did`,
`admin_did` in setup.toml, `pnm acl create`), and on
`cnm setup continue [<name>] [--vta-did <did>] [--vta-url <url>]` authenticate,
which rotates to a fresh did:key over `acl/swap-key` and removes the temp DID's
entry. A continue before the grant prints the routes and stays resumable.
Non-interactive mode mirrors pnm (#1753): `cnm setup --name <name>
[--overwrite]` and `continue --vta-did` each print one `{slug, admin_did,
state}` line.

Alternatives in the wizard:
- "Bootstrap from your existing pnm session" when a pnm profile on this
  machine ($PNM_HOME honoured) is bound to the same VTA DID. pnm's config and
  session store are read only; pnm's key authenticates in memory once, over
  REST (so no mediator socket is taken from a running pnm), to grant cnm's
  own freshly minted key, which then rotates as above. The grant is an
  unrestricted admin: cnm creates a top-level context per community on the
  personal VTA, which the VTA gates on super-admin.
- "I have a sealed bundle from an admin" — unchanged, digest pinned.

Communities now get an admin identity each, so one operator's communities
share no key. `cnm community add <name> [--vtc-did] [--vta-did] [--slug]
[--overwrite]` mints a did:key for that community, parks it in
`pending_communities` (not selectable by --community or as default until
confirmed), and prints the VTC grant routes: `co_admin_did` in vtc setup,
`vtc acl add` offline, or an existing admin's `cnm access grant` / console,
noting the second-administrator approval an online unrestricted grant waits
for. `cnm community continue <slug> [--vtc-did] [--vta-did]` confirms with a
DI-signed authenticate to the VTC (VTC audience) before promoting the
profile. The VTC has no key-rotation task (no acl/swap-key; a successor admin
entry is itself an unrestricted grant needing a second admin's consent,
VTI-APV-014), so the minted key is kept rather than a rotation invented.
Reusing another community's key takes `--reuse-identity <community>` (or an
explicit, warned choice in the wizard). `cnm community list` shows each
community's identity and the pending ones; `delete` drops a pending one.
Holding a community identity as a persona on the personal VTA is a follow-up.

Docs: getting-started ("Administering from cnm"), bootstrap-runbook,
admin-access walkthrough, CLAUDE.md cold-start flow.

title: Skip the PR preview deployment for Dependabot pull requests
body:
## What

Adds `github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]'` to the `preview` job's `if:` in `validate.yml`, and extends the comment above the job to say why.

## Why

On #25 the preview job failed with `In a non-interactive environment, it's necessary to set a CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN environment variable for wrangler to work.` A Dependabot-triggered run reads the repository's Dependabot secrets store, not the Actions store, so the Cloudflare token is empty. The job is not a required check, but the red X is noise on every tooling bump, and a dependency bump does not need a rendered preview.

The condition tests the actor rather than the PR author because the actor is what selects the secrets store. If a maintainer pushes to a Dependabot branch, the run gets the Actions secrets and the preview runs again.

## Not fixed here

EasyCLA on #25 stays red until `dependabot[bot]` is allowlisted for the `trustoverip` org, which only the EasyCLA support team can do. That request is going to the ToIP CLA manager separately.

## Verification

- This PR runs under a human actor, so its own `preview` job must still run and post a URL.
- After merge, `@dependabot rebase` on #25 should show `validate` passing and `preview` skipped.

title: fix(vtc-console): admission criteria load within the listing's page limit
body:
**Bug:** Vetting → Requirements shows *Could not load the admission criteria — malformed request: payload failed schema validation: 100 is greater than the maximum of 50*, so operators can't see or edit join criteria.

**Cause:** `plugins/vetting/api.ts`'s shared `allItems` helper sent `limit: 100` to every signed listing. `vtc/schemas/accepts/list` (0.1 and 0.2) caps `limit` at 50, so the VTC correctly refused it. The other listings using the helper (vetter grants, revocations) allow 100, as does `rooms.tsx`'s rooms listing — checked against the published schemas.

**Fix:** `allItems` takes the listing's page size; the admission criteria use `ACCEPTS_PAGE_SIZE = 50`. New test pins the bound and that the cursor is followed across pages.

Console only. `npm run lint` clean; vitest 58 files / 646 tests passed.

title: feat(vgi-bridge): several GitHub organisations on one bridge, one private App each
body:
**Merge order: #92, then this PR, then #95.** #89 (VTA mode) is in `main`. This branch has `main` (with #91's role-map report, event 0.3 and trust-tasks-rs 0.23) and `feat/bridge-job-0.4` (#92) merged in, so it merges cleanly whichever of the two lands first.

Design §5.7, "Several orgs: one private App per org, one bridge".

## What changes
- **`[[github]]` is keyed by `(host, app_owner)`.**
  - Each entry names its own `app_name`, since GitHub App names are unique per instance.
  - Validation refuses two entries for one owner on a host, a duplicate `app_name` on a host, an owner that is not a login, and a Forgejo host that is also a GitHub host.
- **An App serves its own `app_owner` only**, even when it is the host's only App. GitHub installs a private App only on its owner. A namespace whose owner has no entry fails its bind with `notCapable`.
- **Secrets are per App** at `github/<host>/<owner>/app`, in the sealed store or, in VTA mode, in the context's app-state.
  - The stored App records its `owner` (required), and an App stored under another owner is refused.
- **Each App has its own routes**, `/github/<host>/<owner>/{register,registered,setup,webhook}`, verified with that App's own webhook secret.
  - The manifest the bridge generates points the App at them.
  - A setup redirect must match the App that serves the namespace being bound.
  - There are no owner-less GitHub routes.
- **The bridge picks the App from a resource's host and owner** (`Adapters::for_resource`, `vgi_for`, `github_for`). This covers jobs, events, status reports, the bridge-posted check, the Dependabot re-sign and the role map.
- **Manifest flow:** one registration link per organisation, one click each.
- **VTC:** it still maps a forge host to one bridge DID (`[git_ns] bridges`, `vtc-service/src/git_ns/ops.rs`). No VTC change is needed.

## Breaking changes (no migration; test deployments are recreated)
- **A store in the single-App layout is refused at start.** That layout is `github/<host>/app` with owner-less routes. The error says to re-register: delete the App on GitHub, start on a fresh store (an empty `data_dir`, or a fresh VTA context), and register one App per organisation.
- The owner-less routes `/github/<host>/{register,registered,setup,webhook}` are gone. The proxy must forward `/github/<host>/<owner>/…`.
- A lone App no longer serves other owners on its host.
- Config: duplicate owners, or a duplicate `app_name`, on a host are refused.
- API: `Adapters::insert` takes the owner, `get(host)` is Forgejo-only, `get_github(host, owner)` is exact, `vgi(host)` becomes `vgi_for(resource)`, `github_app_secret` takes `(host, owner)`, and `StoredApp.owner` is required.

## Docs
- SETUP-GITHUB-VTC: removes "one namespace per bridge on github.com", and adds the second-org config example and the per-org registration.
- BRIDGE.md: routes, one App per org, and refusing a single-App store.
- RUNBOOK: troubleshooting row.

## Tests
`tests/multi_org.rs`:
- two orgs are each served by their own App (logins are case-insensitive);
- webhooks are routed per App and verified with that App's own secret; there is no owner-less route;
- per-org registration links and manifests carry their own routes, and one org's link is refused on another org's route;
- a single-App store is refused with re-register guidance;
- a lone App serves only its own owner;
- an App stored under the wrong owner is refused.

The existing suites moved to the owner routes. Bind tests for a second org register that org's own App. Personal-account tests use an App owned by that account. Config unit tests cover the keying.


## Security review follow-up (39cb210): an App acts only on its own organisation
An organisation's owners can set their App's webhook secret, so a delivery verified with that App's secret speaks for that organisation only. The verifying App's `(host, owner)` now scopes every delivery:
- An event naming a namespace or repository outside the owner is dropped and logged. A transfer must have one of its sides in the owner.
- Namespace and repository lookups are filtered by the scope. A forge id that another namespace records or manages is never detached, renamed or transferred on this App's word.
- An installation event must match the namespace's recorded installation id.
- Pushes (the Dependabot provenance ledger) are kept only for a repository this owner's namespace manages, matched by name and forge id. Check triggers for another owner's repository or forge id are dropped.
- A transfer between two served organisations is reported by each organisation's App for its own side.
- An account link's device-flow poll and redirect resolve their adapter from the namespace, not the host.

Regression tests from the probe are in `tests/multi_org.rs`. Each failed before the fix:
- another org's App cannot delete, rename or transfer this org's repository, whether it names the repository directly or by forge id;
- it cannot remove this org's installation, and a wrong installation id is ignored even through the org's own App;
- it cannot feed the provenance ledger or trigger checks.

## Re-review follow-up (08fe2fc): transfers only the new owner reports
- Another organisation's record of a repository no longer stops the new owner from reporting it `repoCreatedUnmanaged`.
- The old side is detached, and told `repoTransferred`, only once GitHub confirms the move: `GET /repositories/{id}` through the new owner's own installation must place the repository in the new namespace. An unconfirmed claim leaves the other organisation's state alone.
- New adapter read: `GitHubForge::repository_by_id`.
- Tests:
  - only the new owner reports: confirmed, old side detached, and a late old-owner delivery is harmless;
  - the old owner reports first: nothing to confirm;
  - an unconfirmed claim leaves the old side untouched.

## Merged with `main` (#91) and #92
- Role-map reports (event 0.3) are per organisation. A report picks its adapter with `Adapters::for_resource`, which finds the owner's App. It builds the map from `role_map`, which finds the owner's `[[github]]` entry.
- Fix: `role_map_repos` now finds the owner's `[[github]]` entry (`github_for`), not the first entry on the host. Before, a second organisation's configured repository maps were left out of its report. Test: `role_map_repos_are_the_owners_own`.
- trust-tasks-rs 0.23: the test resolver in `vta.rs` is main's `ProofPurposeResolver`. This PR adds no new signing path, so every bridge document is still signed through `BridgeIdentity::sign`, with `assertionMethod`.
- Job 0.4 and the rule that only `own` maps to admin come from #92 unchanged.

title: chore(deps): take vta-sdk 0.38
body:
Held as a draft until OpenVTC is ready to consume the release this produces — see below.

**Why.** OpenVTC has moved off its git patches and onto the published VTI releases, which puts it on `vta-sdk` 0.38. `did-git-sign` 0.4.9 asks for `^0.36`, and that is precisely what leaves **two `vta-sdk`s in OpenVTC's graph** — it is the only crate there depending on 0.36.0. Nothing in this repository needs 0.38; as with every step before it, the bump exists so the ceiling moves.

**Neither minor's content reaches this crate.**
- **0.37** replaced the hand-written vetting wire types with the generated `trust_tasks_rs::specs` ones, and domain-separated the opaque signing oracle (VTI #1417). The signing change is the one worth checking on a signing tool, and it does not apply: the framing is for payloads a VTA cannot parse, while this crate's `vta_sdk::keys` use is a `KeyType` comparison and a `KeyRecord` read.
- **0.38** refuses `did:webvh` resolution to non-public hosts by default (VTI #1448).

The features these members enable — `client`, `session`, `didcomm`, `provision-client`, `agent-names` — all exist unchanged across both minors.

**One duplicate collapses on the way.** `didwebvh-rs` was two nodes, 0.6 and 0.7; `vta-sdk` 0.38 declares `^0.7`, so the lockfile now resolves 0.7.0 alone. The `trust-tasks-rs` 0.19.4 / 0.20.4 split stays, bounded exactly as the trql-client note in the manifest describes, until the registry releases on 0.20 — `trql-client` 0.17.0 is still its latest and still declares `^0.19.4`.

**Verified:** `cargo tree` resolves a single `vta-sdk` 0.38.0 node, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is silent, and all 158 tests pass.

**Sequence.** Merge this, then release, and OpenVTC's `did-git-sign` floor moves to that release — at which point its second `vta-sdk` is gone.
author: stormer78

title: docs: bring the runbook and guides up to v0.11.0 and current VTC behaviour
body:
Documentation only. No versions, code or config values change (`bridge.example.toml` comments only).

## What was wrong

- **Example workflows** in the runbook and README pinned `verify-trust@v0.4.6` and a mutable `actions/checkout` tag. v0.4.6 predates `transport`, attestation and `resource-format`. They also lacked `merge_group`, `permissions` and `persist-credentials: false`. They now match what `vgi repo init` and the bridge generate.
- **RUNBOOK §8** still pointed operators at `GET /v1/git-ns/*`. Those routes are gone on the VTC; the reads are signed Trust Tasks, and the ones with no `cnm` command are console panels.
- **Missing VTC behaviour:** separation of duties and break-glass (new §8l), `--subject` on drift adopt, `cnm git unlink`, `reproject` (positional resource), the policy second-administrator step, and their refusal codes.
- **Verdict tables** lacked `malformed`, and the signer DID is read from the `Signed-by-DID:` trailer first.
- **SETUP-GITHUB-VTC** versions (0.4.14, trust-tasks 0.22), the `transport` key and registry mediator requirement, `--owner` on create, Forgejo `read:user` and `runs_on`.
- **Smaller:** BRIDGE.md/bridge README (`public_url` loopback, uid 10001 + HEALTHCHECK, `[vta]` keys, `authentication` proof purpose), verify-trust and did-git-sign READMEs, vgi-cli README flags.

## How it was checked

Each claim was read against the code at `2b6b609` (v0.11.0), and VTC/`cnm` claims against VTI `origin/main` (argument definitions in `cnm-cli/src/git.rs`, `consent.rs`, `actions.rs`). Nothing was built or run.

## Please look at

- SETUP-GITHUB-VTC's Versions table now says VGI **0.11.0 or later**. That is the version the guide was checked against, not a verified lowest compatible release.
- The runbook's `malformed` fix text ("re-sign with `did-git-sign`") is inferred, not stated in the code.
- BRIDGE.md §2a internals (lease timing, 503 thresholds), §3 App permissions and §6a/§6b Dependabot windows were not re-verified.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.27.1
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: Cooling-off actions, a reduction-pending notice and an offline-write record type ([#719](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/719))

Three gaps the VTC implementation (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1920)
  found in the vtc/admin/actions family.

  vtc/admin/actions/_shared/0.2 adds the cooling-off action. A removal of an
  administrator with no third party to consent is parked for a cooling-off
  period and lands by itself unless its requester cancels. 0.1 could only say
  that by omitting threshold and expiresAt against its own prose and carrying
  the landing time in ext. 0.2 adds category coolingOff, landsAt (when it lands),
  cancellableBy (requester), closedReason landedAfterCoolingOff, and callerRole
  subject, so the administrator being removed can see the action. list, show,
  cancel and acknowledge 0.2 re-point at _shared 0.2; their request payloads
  and error codes are unchanged.

  vtc/members/authority-reduction-pending-notice/0.1 tells the subject that a
  reduction is cooling off, before it lands. The subject cannot block it,
  because a veto held by the subject would protect a compromised subject. One-way,
  proof REQUIRED.

  vtc/operator/offline-write/0.1 is a record type, never sent. An acknowledge
  action for an operator's offline write (vtc admin emergency-bootstrap and its
  siblings) names it as typeUri and carries the record as payload. Before, there
  was no Type URI to name, because those commands are not Trust Tasks.
  sideEffects none. It follows the registry's existing never-sent-on-its-own
  documents (auth/step-up/approver/attest, auth/signing-key/authorize).

| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.5.0` → `0.5.1` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(vtc): operator writes need acknowledging, reductions notify and cool off, and execution survives a crash (VTI-VTC-023, VTI-APV-019) (#1920)
body:
feat(vtc): operator writes need acknowledging, reductions notify and cool off, and execution survives a crash (VTI-VTC-023, VTI-APV-019) (#1920)

Phase A2 of the administrator action list (docs/05-design-notes/vtc-action-list.md).

VTI-VTC-023: every offline access-control write (vtc acl add/remove, vtc admin
invite, vtc create-did-key --admin, vtc admin enrol-approver, vtc admin
emergency-bootstrap) is raised at the next boot as an acknowledge-category
action (kind operator.offlineWrite) for the administrators who held a role
when it was made, minus any who has since lost every admin role; an emergency
bootstrap's item is for the administrators it installed. No expiry.
vtc/admin/actions/acknowledge/0.1 now has a producer; acknowledging is
audited. Markers are cleared only after the item is raised (R2.1). The census
baseline for acknowledge:alreadyAcknowledged is removed (witnessed).

VTI-APV-019: every reduction of an administrator that lands (acl/revoke,
downward acl/change-role, narrowing acl/update or acl/grant, by consent, after
a cooling-off, or on a step-up alone) sends the subject a VTC-signed
vtc/members/authority-reduced-notice/0.1 (code, previousRole, resultingRole,
agreement, reason, decidedAt, decidedBy). admin-remove keeps the removal
notice and never sends both. An unopposed reduction of an unrestricted
administrator is parked for acl.removal_cooling_off (default 24 h, 0-7 days,
live), lands by itself unless the requester cancels, is audited Critical, and
the first of two administrators to act wins (the counter-request lands the
earlier one and the loser's own actions are invalidated).

VTI-APV-017: task-consent/decision/0.2 approverSigned evidence is verified
through acl::approver::verify_statement (purpose decision). An action is
persisted executing with an execution id before its operation runs; the
operation records its effect (marker + new AdminActionEffect audit row) and an
interrupted execution is reconciled from that evidence, not failed by age
(CLAUDE.md R2.1).

Also: task-consent/request pushes default off (acl.consent_request_push);
claim/start 0.3 voids the install token after five wrong codes; an action
that makes an unrestricted administrator issues them a step-up approver
invite, shown once to the requester; a console-key-signed approve-response 0.6
is refused subjectMismatch; the console gains acknowledge cards, the
operator-write and cooling-off banners, cooling-off cards and the claim 0.3
wallet install path. Docs updated.

author: stormer78

title: feat(extension): vouch for a VTC task-consent decision with the approver (#293)
body:
feat(extension): vouch for a VTC task-consent decision with the approver (#293)

Adds window.vtaWallet.approveDecision({audience, subject, action,
decision}), which signs an auth/step-up/approver/attest/0.1 statement with
purpose decision for a VTC administrator's task-consent/decision/0.2 (VTI
#1920's approverSigned decision evidence): subject the administrator who
signs the decision, audience and recipient the VTC, challenge the
decision's challenge, boundTo its payloadDigest.

- The wallet recomputes payloadDigest from action.{type,payload} and the
  challenge as the task-consent wire digest (vta/task-consent/v1, salted
  with the challenge the VTC issued this administrator; pinned to
  vti_common's vectors) and refuses on a mismatch before any prompt, in the
  background and again in the offscreen beside the key.
- The prompt shows the action (type, payload, action id), APPROVE or DENY,
  the administrator's note and the VTC's summary labelled unverified; the
  biometric's binding includes approve/deny.
- Never mints: no approver for the audience is
  step-up-approver/not-enrolled.
- attestApprover stays enrolment only and now names the right method when
  asked for decision or stepUp.

signTrustTask routes any decision/0.2 claiming approverSigned evidence to
decisionResponseRefusal: signed once, without a second prompt, spent
before signing, only when it carries the statement just issued to this
origin, unchanged, with the same RP, challenge, payloadDigest, decision,
reason and actionId, signed as the statement's subject. Anything else of
that shape is refused rather than prompted for. Step-up and decision
statements cannot ride each other's document.

All #291 protections are kept: audience pinned to the origin's login,
approver chosen by the wallet from the audience, biometric gesture,
single-use statement.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.27.0
body:
### Build & CI

- Faster Rust CI and releases — parallel jobs, a lighter test build, verify on the Release PR ([#716](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/716))

The Rust test job (10-19 min) gated every PR and release-plz's publish
  (16-18 min) gated every release. Nearly all of both was compiling the
  46 MB generated trust-tasks-rs, again and again.

  - trust-tasks-codegen moves the per-spec conformance tests out of each
    generated module into one generated integration test,
    trust-tasks-rs/tests/conformance/, and leaves every family but `acl`
    out of the crate's cfg(test) build. The unit-test harness no longer
    compiles a second copy of the whole tree. The validate test build
    went from 63s to 23s locally, peak RSS 9.0 GB to 4.3 GB. All 1558
    generated tests and 126 unit tests still run.
  - rust.yml runs workspace tests, validate tests and cargo doc as three
    parallel jobs, and clippy's two feature sets as a matrix.
  - release-plz publishes with publish_no_verify. The verify build moves to
    a new package-workspace job on the Release PR (cargo package
    --workspace, with unpublished siblings from the local registry
    overlay), so a tarball that cannot compile now blocks the merge
    instead of failing partway through an irreversible upload.
  - rust-cache saves from main only. PR saves were 1 GB duplicates of
    main's key and had filled the 10 GB cache quota.
  - PR workflows cancel superseded runs.
  - The codegen drift check now also catches untracked generated files.



### Specifications

- **git-ns**: Activity/list 0.1 declares the `source` its ActivityItem requires ([#718](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/718))

`$defs/ActivityItem` listed `source` in `required` but defined no `source`
  property, under `additionalProperties: false`. No item could validate, so no
  non-empty `git-ns/activity/list/0.1#response` could either: a consumer that
  validates rejected every conforming response. The `Source` enum (`audit` |
  `job`) was defined in `$defs` but never referenced. The spec prose, its
  examples and the one implementation (the VTC) all carry `source`; only the
  schema lost it. The property now references `#/$defs/Source`.

  The spec is a draft and the change makes the schema accept the wire its prose
  and implementation already use, so it is edited in place (SPEC §5.2).

  The registry's unsatisfiable-schema lint (added after
  `provision/integration/0.3`, #326) checked only the root and
  `$defs.Response`, so an item definition reached through `Response.items`
  went unseen. It now walks every subschema closed by
  `additionalProperties: false`; against main it reports exactly this defect
  and nothing else.

  Breaking for Rust: the generated `ActivityItem.source` was an untyped
  `serde_json::Value` (the codegen's fallback for a required member with no
  schema) and is now the generated `Source` enum. Go and Dart gain a typed
  `source` field; TypeScript gains it on the interface and the embedded schema.

  Reported by the VTA browser plugin's schema-satisfiability test against
  @openvtc/trust-tasks 0.22.7.

The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.26.3` → `0.27.0` | breaking |

| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.26.3` → `0.27.0` | breaking |

| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.5.0`) | `0.4.7` → `0.5.0` | breaking |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.4.7` → `0.5.0` | breaking |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(extension): answer a VTC step-up with a per-community approver
body:
The wallet half of OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1919 (VTC `approverSigned` step-up). Three optional, feature-detected members of `window.vtaWallet`, matching what the VTC console (`vtc-service/admin-ui/src/lib/wallet.ts` on `feat/vtc-approver-step-up`) calls.

## Surface

- **`approverIdentity({ audience }) → { approverDid }`** — the approver `did:key` for that relying party. Signs nothing. No gesture once the wallet's approver sealing key exists; in a wallet with none, the first call raises a one-off setup prompt (biometric, signs nothing) to create it.
- **`approveStepUp({ request, operation, audience }) → { statement, approverDid }`** — refused **before any prompt** unless this wallet's approver for `audience` is in `request.approvers`, `request.accepts` includes `approverSigned`, and `request.boundTo` equals `"z" + base58btc(0x12 0x20 ‖ SHA-256("vtc/step-up/v1\0" ‖ u64be(len type) ‖ type ‖ u64be(len JCS payload) ‖ JCS payload ‖ challenge))` recomputed from `operation`. The approver prompt (APPROVER mode) then shows the community, the operation (type plus the whole payload, with bidi/zero-width characters escaped), and the reason (marked unverified, because the page supplies it). It takes a UV WebAuthn-PRF gesture and returns a signed `auth/step-up/approver/attest/0.1`: issuer = approver, recipient = payload.audience = audience, `urn:uuid` id, issuedAt now, `purpose: stepUp`, eddsa-jcs-2022, `proofPurpose: authentication`, `verificationMethod did:key:…#<multibase>`.
- **`attestApprover({ purpose: "enrol", subject, audience, challenge, boundTo })`** — the same prompt, then signs attest/0.1 with `purpose: enrol` over exactly what it was given.

## Per-audience approvers: minted and sealed, not derived

Each VTC gets a fresh CSPRNG Ed25519 key, so communities cannot correlate the user by it. Its seed is **sealed** (ephemeral-static X25519 → HKDF-SHA256 → AES-256-GCM, with audience and DID bound into both the HKDF info and the AAD) to a wallet **sealing key**. The sealing key's secret half is wrapped under the existing approver KEK (`ApproverPrfSecretWrap`). Because minting needs only the public half, `approverIdentity` works with no gesture while the seed is never at rest unsealed. Every *use* needs the gesture that unwraps the sealing secret. An unsealed seed is checked against the DID it was filed under before it signs anything.

HKDF from one PRF-protected root (`info = "vta-approver/v1" ‖ audience`) was considered and rejected on three counts:
1. A derived key can't be named without the gesture, which breaks `approverIdentity`'s no-gesture contract.
2. Unwrapping the root to sign for one community yields every community's key, including ones not yet visited.
3. Deleting a derived key's record forgets nothing, since it can be derived again.

The VTA DTTE approver (`approver-identity.ts`, one per VTA) is a separate key and store and is untouched. A new step-up approver also refuses any DID already on file in either store.

## Security bounds

- **Origin-gated.** Every call requires `audience === ` the RP the origin is pinned to by an approved login (`pageApproverAudienceRefusal`). Without that, a page could read every community's approver DID or have one sign for a community the user never signed in to from it.
- **The page never names the key.** The approver is chosen from the audience.
- **Checks run twice.** The background runs them to decide whether a human sees anything. The offscreen document runs them again beside the key (`signStepUpApproval`).
- **`signTrustTask`.** `pageSignRefusal` still refuses every `auth/step-up/approve-*`, with one exception: an approve-response 0.6 can be signed when it carries, **unchanged**, a statement `approveStepUp` issued to that origin within 5 min, for the same RP, subject and challenge, signed `asDid` the subject. The statement is single-use, consumed before signing. There is no second generic prompt, because the human approved this operation on the approver prompt a moment earlier.
- **Proof purpose.** The holder path's `proofPurpose` now comes from the document type (`proofPurposeForDocumentType`, mirroring `vta_sdk`'s `ATTESTATION_SLUGS`), so an approve-response is `assertionMethod`. It was hard-coded `authentication` before. On the `asDid` path the VTA decides the purpose the same way. Neither path ever signs with the approver key or a console key.

## Note on types

attest/0.1 and approve-request/0.4 are transcribed in `trust-tasks/approver-attest.ts`. The only `@openvtc/trust-tasks` release that generates them, 0.22.7, ships a `git-ns/activity/list` schema that requires a member it doesn't define. `inbound.consent-schema.mjs` refuses that, and its instruction is to report it upstream, not work around it. Swap in the generated types when a fixed release lands. `task-surface.mjs` gains `NOT_IN_SDK` entries for both URIs (VTC-addressed, not VTA).

## Tests

- `core/tests/store.step-up-approver.mjs`:
  - `domainDigest` matches `vti_common::task_consent::digest_matches_its_pinned_vectors` (all four vectors, copied with a citation).
  - Refusal when the approver isn't offered, on a `boundTo` mismatch (changed payload, changed type, forged salt), and when `approverSigned` isn't accepted.
  - Distinct DIDs per audience, distinct from the DTTE approver.
  - Seed stored sealed only, and a sealed seed can't be moved to another audience.
  - attest/0.1 shape, with the proof verified by `verifyTrustTaskProof`.
  - The purpose rule.
- `extension/tests/approver-policy.test.mts`: origin/audience gating, the approve-response exemption and each of its refusals, payload rendering, and `doSignTrustTask` taking its purpose from the type.
- `npm run lint`, `npm run build` and `npm test` all pass. Core: 740 tests, 0 failed. Extension: 885 tests, 0 failed. `background.js` has no dynamic `import()`.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

```
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no network code added
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — the only writes are local key records and a session-scoped issued-statement record
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — no retries
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — attest/0.1 members exactly; approve-response members checked against an allow-list
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — no pin, no approver; closed window or missing PRF output = deny
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — a mint that dies before put leaves no record; the issued statement is consumed before signing
- [x] Deviations flagged: types transcribed pending a trust-tasks release without the git-ns schema defect
```

Do not merge before the VTI side (#1919) lands; the two cut over together.

title: feat(vtc): an approver device can be an administrator's step-up factor (VTI-APV-015, VTI-APV-016)
body:
Phase B1 of `docs/05-design-notes/vtc-approver-step-up.md`. A VTC administrator who signs in with a VTA wallet, and so holds no passkey at the community, can now step up with an approver device. An approver is an Ed25519 `did:key` bound to the administrator as their step-up factor, such as the browser plugin's approver identity.

Requirements: **VTI-APV-015** as amended (a signature counts only from a key bound as a factor under VTI-APV-016, distinct from the caller's signing keys, held behind user verification), **VTI-APV-016** (bind only on independent evidence, prove possession, audit the evidence), **VTI-SES-001–004**. Wire types are the generated ones from `trust-tasks-rs` **0.26.3** (the bump landed with #1918). **Rebased on #1918** (the action list): the inline step-up request type moved to approve-request 0.4, so #1918's `admin_consent.rs`, `ceremony/orchestrate.rs`, `routes/acl.rs` and `trust_tasks/acl_tasks.rs` refer to `bound_step_up::ApproveRequest` (type path only; #1918's park-and-reply behaviour is unchanged).

## Changes

**Approver store and statement verification** (`vtc-service/src/acl/approver.rs`)
- New keyspace `step_up_approvers`, which is **backed up** (design §4/§11.3). It holds bindings as `approver:<did>` (live, or a revoked tombstone so the DID is burned) and `subject:<did>` (the subject's live approvers, at most 5). It also holds the enrolment rows and spent statement ids, all of which expire.
- `check_distinct`: an approver must not be the subject's DID, must not be a key in the subject's DID document, must not be any console signing key, and must hold no ACL row. This is checked at enrolment and again at every use (`live_approvers` drops one that is no longer distinct).
- `verify_statement` returns `VerifiedApproverStatement` (typestate) after the attest/0.1 consumer checks:
  - the proof, `authentication`, made by the issuer's `did:key` and checked over the statement as received;
  - the acceptance window, and `recipient` and `audience` both this VTC;
  - `purpose`, `subject`, `challenge` (constant-time) and `boundTo` equal to the pending record's, with `issuedAt` inside that record's lifetime;
  - the issuer is a live, distinct approver of the subject that was offered (or, when enrolling, the approver being enrolled), and is never the subject;
  - the statement `id` is spent once.

  It is `pub` so the action-list work can use it for decision evidence.

**Gate** (`acl/bound_step_up.rs`)
- The inline request is now `approve-request/0.4`. `accepts` lists `approverSigned`, with its `approvers`, when the subject holds a live approver, and `webauthn`, with its options, only when a passkey counts.
- Factor-union rule (`factors_of`): once a subject holds an approver or a step-up passkey, their session passkeys stop counting. An existing session elevation is revoked when an approver is bound.
- New `approve_with_statement` for `approve-response/0.6` `approverSigned`. The outer proof must be the subject's own DID: the spine verifies it as an approval, makes it `assertionMethod`, and refuses a console key's delegation before lookup.
- Recorded marks carry `StepUpEvidence { kind, … }`, with the approver DID as the credential id, and the challenge, which self-service enrolment binds to.
- New audit event `OperationStepUpApproved` names the evidence kind and the approver DID.
- 0.4 and 0.5 work as before. A `webauthn` answer to a request that did not accept `webauthn` is `noGate`.

**Enrolment and revocation**, all as Trust Tasks on the signed-document spine (`step_up_approver.rs`, `trust_tasks/step_up_approver_tasks.rs`):

| Task | Notes |
|---|---|
| `invite/0.1` (R2) | Community admin only, behind their own bound step-up. Refused for yourself (`selfInvite`), for a non-member (`subjectUnknown`), and for a TTL over 24 h (`ttlTooLong` with `maxTtl`); the default is 15 min. Token and claim code are stored hashed. URL is `/admin/enrol-approver#token=…`. |
| `redeem/start/0.1` | Must be signed by the invited subject's own DID; a console key is `notInvitedSubject`, and that attempt is not counted. `codeMismatch` carries `attemptsRemaining`; the 5th wrong code gives `inviteVoided`, permanently. |
| `redeem/finish/0.1` | The subject's DID plus the approver's `enrol` statement over `enrollmentId`. Binding and invite consumption are atomic. Codes: `approverNotDistinct`, `approverAlreadyBound` (also for burned DIDs), `tooManyApprovers`. |
| `enroll/0.1` (R3) | The subject's own DID; a console key is `subjectMismatch`; no factor is `noFactorHeld`. The bound step-up is over the terms (payload minus `statement`). The new approver's statement is bound to that step-up's challenge and the terms digest. `replaces` is supported, and the step-up is left in place after `statementInvalid`. |
| `list/0.1` | Your own approvers, or those of a member within your administrative authority. |
| `revoke/0.1` | Yourself, or an admin on your behalf, behind the caller's step-up. The last approver may be revoked. A repeat is a no-op. Codes are a uniform `notFound`. The reason is audited. |

- Every binding is audited as `StepUpApproverChanged`, with `enrolledVia` and the anchor (VTI-APV-016).

**Install claim 0.3** (R1)
- `vtc/install/claim/{start,finish}/0.3` claims under the DID the install token names. The claim code is required.
- Before verifying the finish, the spine evicts that DID from the resolver cache and resolves it afresh, so the proof is checked against the live document. Failure is `didUnresolvable`.
- The approver is parked as `pending:<jti>` and bound only when `vtc/admin/bootstrap` consumes the setup-session token. The bootstrap now accepts a pending approver in place of a passkey. If the token lapses the binding is discarded.
- 0.2 is unchanged.

**Offline R4**
- `vtc admin enrol-approver --did <subject> [--ttl]` (daemon stopped) mints an R2-shaped invite with `enrolledVia: offline` and queues an `install:break_glass:*` marker.
- The boot-time audit of those markers is now `server::audit_offline_break_glass`.

**Console** (`admin-ui`)
- Reads `accepts` and `approvers`.
- `answerStepUp` tries, in order: the plugin's `approveStepUp` (approve-response 0.6, signed by the wallet as the subject); then WebAuthn; then guidance that names R2 and R4.
- New "Approver devices" card under My passkeys (list, revoke, self-service add) and under Members → member (revoke, "Invite to enrol an approver").
- New redemption page at `/enrol-approver`.

**Docs**
- `docs/03-vtc/admin-access.md`: §3.1 step-up factors, new §3.1a on enrolment, walkthrough step 5b, known gaps, quick reference.
- `docs/03-vtc/bootstrap-runbook.md`: wallet founder (Path C), offline `enrol-approver`.
- Design-note status updated. CLAUDE.md has no step-up flow entry to update.


## Tests

- `tests/it/step_up_approvers.rs`:
  - `approverSigned` success, including that the challenge is single use;
  - refused for: a statement by a non-bound approver, an approver bound to another subject, a wrong audience or recipient, a challenge mismatch, a `boundTo` mismatch, the wrong purpose, the approver being the subject DID, and a different outer signer;
  - a console key signing the answer is refused before lookup;
  - the factor-union rule;
  - a subject with no factor gets guidance naming the routes;
  - invite refusals (self, stranger, TTL, non-admin), with no step-up asked;
  - redeem/start: other signers are not counted, `codeMismatch` counts down, 5 wrong codes void the invite;
  - redeem/finish: `statementInvalid`, `notInvitedSubject`, `approverNotDistinct`, already bound, a burned revoked DID, the cap of five;
  - self-service enroll with `replaces`, plus its refusals;
  - list authority;
  - admin revoking a member's last approver, after which a pending step-up offered to that approver gets `approverNotBound`;
  - the offline invite is audited at boot and redeems as `offline`.
- `tests/it/install_claim_v0_3.rs`: an end-to-end wallet founder (claim, bootstrap, approver bound, approver step-up), plus every declared 0.3 error code, with census witnesses.
- Unit tests:
  - 0.4 request shape (`accepts` and `approvers` exactly as held);
  - the terms-digest construction, pinned vectors, and the console's vector;
  - `did:key` approver parsing.
- Census and registry updates:
  - `DISPATCHED_URIS`;
  - the error-code census witnesses (5 new 0.3 codes; `invalidToken` and `registrationMismatch` are shared with 0.2);
  - conformance rows for claim 0.3;
  - `DISPATCHED_WITHOUT_PROOF` (claim/start 0.3);
  - the backup handle map;
  - `trust_task_manifest` console document types, with `attest/0.1` as embedded-only.
- `vta_sdk::retry_safety` covers VTA tasks only; no VTC task, including the existing step-up passkey family, is classified there, so nothing was added.

Local results, after rebasing on #1918:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: all green (lib 1646, `it` 920).
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: all green, full run.
- `admin-ui`: `npm run lint` clean, `npm test` 614 passing.

## Wallet plugin API contract

All three are optional members of `window.vtaWallet` and are feature-detected. Each needs a user-verification gesture to unlock the approver key before anything is signed.

The approver is an Ed25519 `did:key` (`z6Mk…`). There is **one per audience**: derive a distinct approver per VTC DID so communities cannot correlate the user (design §11.1). It must be distinct from every persona and console key.

### `approverIdentity({ audience }) → Promise<{ approverDid }>`
- Returns the approver `did:key` for `audience` (the VTC DID).
- Signs nothing and needs no gesture.
- Used for self-service enrolment, before the first enrol send.

### `approveStepUp({ request, operation, audience }) → Promise<{ statement, approverDid }>`
- **When:** a refused signed act carries `details.stepUpRequest` and its `accepts` includes `approverSigned`.
- **Inputs:**
  - `request` is the inline `auth/step-up/approve-request/0.4` payload.
  - `operation` is `{ type, payload }` of the refused document the VTC will execute.
  - `audience` is the VTC DID.
- **The plugin must:**
  - refuse if its approver for `audience` is not in `request.approvers`;
  - recompute `boundTo` and refuse if it differs from `request.boundTo`. The value is `"z" + base58btc(0x12 0x20 ‖ SHA-256("vtc/step-up/v1\0" ‖ u64be(len(type)) ‖ type ‖ u64be(len(JCS(payload))) ‖ JCS(payload) ‖ challenge))`. Test it against the pinned vectors of `vti_common::task_consent::domain_digest`;
  - render `request.reason`, the operation and the VTC, then take the gesture.
- **Returns** a complete signed `auth/step-up/approver/attest/0.1` document:
  - `issuer` = the approver `did:key`, `recipient` = `audience`, `issuedAt` = now;
  - `payload { purpose: "stepUp", subject: request.subject, audience, challenge: request.challenge, boundTo: request.boundTo }`;
  - an `eddsa-jcs-2022` proof with `proofPurpose: "authentication"` and `verificationMethod: did:key:…#<multibase>`.
- **Afterwards:** the console embeds the statement unchanged in `auth/step-up/approve-response/0.6` as `evidence: { kind: "approverSigned", statement }` and calls `signTrustTask({ envelope, asDid: subject })`.
  - That proof must be the subject's own DID with `proofPurpose: "assertionMethod"`. `signTrustTask` must choose that purpose for approve-response; `vta-sdk`'s `purpose_for_document_type` rule does.
  - It must never be a console key or the approver.

### `attestApprover({ purpose: "enrol", subject, audience, challenge, boundTo }) → Promise<{ statement, approverDid }>`
- Proof of possession at enrolment. `challenge` and `boundTo` depend on the route:
  - **invite redemption:** both from `redeem/start/0.1`, with `boundTo` = `enrollmentId`;
  - **self-service:** `challenge` is the authorizing bound step-up's challenge, and `boundTo` is the terms digest `"z" + base58btc(0x12 0x20 ‖ SHA-256(JCS({ type: "https://trusttasks.org/spec/auth/step-up/approver/enroll/0.1", subject, challenge, terms })))`. `terms` is the enrol payload without `statement`; the pinned vector is in `step_up_approver::tests`;
  - **install claim 0.3:** `boundTo` = `claimId`.
- **Signs** an `attest/0.1` document after the gesture: `payload.purpose: "enrol"`, `issuer` = the approver for `audience`, `recipient` = `payload.audience` = `audience`, `proofPurpose: authentication`.
- The redemption and enrolment documents around it are signed with `signTrustTask({ asDid: subject })`, with `proofPurpose: authentication`.

## Deferred / not done

- **Plugin side** (`approveStepUp`, `approverIdentity`, `attestApprover`): a separate repo; the contract is above. Until it ships, the console falls back to WebAuthn or shows guidance.
- **Console install page for claim 0.3:** the VTC serves 0.3, but `Install.tsx` still drives the 0.2 passkey claim.
- **Notices:** the specs' SHOULD "tell the subject" notices for invite, enrol and revoke are not sent. The existing `vtc/members/step-up-passkey-notice/0.1` is passkey-shaped and doesn't fit.
- **Wrong-code counting on claim/start 0.3:** the spec's SHOULD (invalidate the token after 5 wrong codes) is not implemented; the install token row has no counter.
- **Co-administrator at install:** named at install, they have no token of their own. They enrol through an invite after bootstrap.
- **Automatic invite for new administrators** (design §11.4): not done. It touches `acl/grant` and admin creation, which the action-list PR owns.
- **Phase 2 mobile approvers.**

title: feat(vtc): an approver device can be an administrator's step-up factor (VTI-APV-015, VTI-APV-016) (#1919)
body:
feat(vtc): an approver device can be an administrator's step-up factor (VTI-APV-015, VTI-APV-016) (#1919)

An administrator who signs in with a VTA wallet holds no passkey at the
community, so every operation behind the operation-bound step-up was refused
for them. A step-up approver — an Ed25519 did:key bound to one subject as
their step-up factor, such as the browser plugin's approver identity — can
now answer it.

- Gate: the inline request is auth/step-up/approve-request/0.4, accepting
  `approverSigned` (naming the subject's approvers) and/or `webauthn`.
  auth/step-up/approve-response/0.6 carries the approver's attest/0.1
  statement, verified as received against this service's own pending
  record; the answer itself must be signed by the subject's own DID, never
  a console key. Once a subject holds a dedicated factor (approver or
  step-up passkey) their session passkeys stop counting. Audited as
  OperationStepUpApproved with the evidence kind and approver DID.
- Store: new backed-up keyspace `step_up_approvers`; one approver DID per
  subject, once (revoked DIDs are burned), at most five per subject,
  distinct from the subject's DID, DID-document keys and every console key,
  checked at enrolment and at every use (VTI-APV-015 as amended).
- Enrolment on the signed-document spine, every binding resting on an anchor
  independent of the subject's signing key and audited with `enrolledVia`
  (VTI-APV-016): auth/step-up/approver/{invite,redeem/start,redeem/finish}
  (R2), enroll (R3, behind a factor already held, bound to the terms
  digest), list and revoke; vtc/install/claim/{start,finish}/0.3 (R1,
  claim under the token's DID verified against its live document, binding
  written at bootstrap); `vtc admin enrol-approver` (R4, offline invite,
  audited at boot as a break-glass).
- Console: approverSigned via a feature-detected window.vtaWallet
  approveStepUp, falling back to WebAuthn; Approver devices card; member
  invite; redemption page.

title: spec(git-ns)!: activity/list 0.1 declares the `source` its ActivityItem requires (#718)
body:
spec(git-ns)!: activity/list 0.1 declares the `source` its ActivityItem requires (#718)

`$defs/ActivityItem` listed `source` in `required` but defined no `source`
property, under `additionalProperties: false`. No item could validate, so no
non-empty `git-ns/activity/list/0.1#response` could either: a consumer that
validates rejected every conforming response. The `Source` enum (`audit` |
`job`) was defined in `$defs` but never referenced. The spec prose, its
examples and the one implementation (the VTC) all carry `source`; only the
schema lost it. The property now references `#/$defs/Source`.

The spec is a draft and the change makes the schema accept the wire its prose
and implementation already use, so it is edited in place (SPEC §5.2).

The registry's unsatisfiable-schema lint (added after
`provision/integration/0.3`, #326) checked only the root and
`$defs.Response`, so an item definition reached through `Response.items`
went unseen. It now walks every subschema closed by
`additionalProperties: false`; against main it reports exactly this defect
and nothing else.

Breaking for Rust: the generated `ActivityItem.source` was an untyped
`serde_json::Value` (the codegen's fallback for a required member with no
schema) and is now the generated `Source` enum. Go and Dart gain a typed
`source` field; TypeScript gains it on the interface and the embedded schema.

Reported by the VTA browser plugin's schema-satisfiability test against
@openvtc/trust-tasks 0.22.7.

title: feat(vtc)!: consent-gated operations wait in an action list and complete on the N-th approval (VTI-APV-017) (#1918)
body:
feat(vtc)!: consent-gated operations wait in an action list and complete on the N-th approval (VTI-APV-017) (#1918)

A VTC operation that needs other administrators' approval -- an unrestricted
grant (VTI-APV-014), a reduction of another unrestricted admin (VTI-APV-019),
a lowered consent threshold (VTI-APV-020), an authority-policy change
(VTI-VTC-022) -- is no longer refused with `auth:consent_required` and re-sent.
Phase A1 of docs/05-design-notes/vtc-action-list.md.

Once every other check passes and the requester's operation-bound step-up is
spent (VTI-APV-015), the operation is parked as an action in the new
`admin_actions` keyspace (excluded from backup: it binds the ACL as it stood on
this host). The record keeps the requester's signed document verbatim, the
payload, requester, step-up evidence, approver set, threshold, one challenge
per approver, a state pin and its lifetime. The requester is answered
`trust-task-next-step/0.1` (202, continuation `proceed`, expecting
`vtc/admin/actions/show/0.1` with the action id) and never sends it again.

Approvers decide with `task-consent/decision/0.1` or `/0.2`, signed by their
own DID (a delegated console key is refused). The approval that reaches the
threshold moves the action out of `open` under a lock -- so concurrent final
approvals execute it once -- and dispatches the stored document through the
handler it was submitted to, re-running every check against the community as
it is then; the consent gate re-checks approver eligibility, threshold and
state pin. It closes `completed`, or `failed` with nothing written. One deny
closes it for everyone; the requester can cancel; it expires; it is
invalidated when the requester loses authority, the pinned state moves, or the
eligible approvers can no longer reach the threshold (VTI-APV-004/-005/-006/
-007/-008/-009/-017). Freshness and replay are held once, at submission
(VTI-OPS-024..027).

decision/0.2 `webauthn` evidence is verified against the approver's passkeys
with user verification required, as an additional factor. `approverSigned`
evidence is refused (evidenceInvalid, approverSignedUnsupported) until the
approver store lands.

New config keys, runtime-patchable: acl.action_lifetime (72 h, 15 min-14 d),
acl.action_max_open_per_requester (5, 1-20), acl.action_max_open (50,
10-500), acl.action_decline_cooldown (1 h, 0-24 h). More than three actions by
one requester in ten minutes writes a Critical `AdminActionBurst` audit row
and flags approvers' cards; an approver may decide at most ten a minute
(VTI-APV-021, section 7a.1).

Summaries are templates as data (title/effect prose, JSON Pointer fields, a
closed format set) keyed by (kind, typeUri), each pinned by digest in the
build, with shared vectors run by the service and the console (VTI-APV-011,
-013).

Served on the signed-document spine: vtc/admin/actions/{list,show,cancel,
acknowledge}/0.1 (acknowledge answers notAcknowledgeable until A2 raises
acknowledge items), with conformance witnesses and declared-code witnesses.

cnm: `cnm actions {list,show,cancel}` and `cnm consent approve|deny --action
<id>`; the file-based `cnm consent approve <request>` still answers a pushed
request. vtc-client: `VtcError::Parked`, list/show/cancel/decide_action, and
`actions::{verify_action, decision_for}`.

Console: an Actions page (Waiting for me / Requested by me / History), a badge,
banner and tab-title count, decisions signed with the browser wallet (plus
passkey evidence when the session has one), and a success-styled "Sent for
approval" notice in place of the old consent error.

Breaking: the re-send model is gone with no shim (design section 8a). The
`task_consent` keyspace is replaced by `admin_actions`, the
`task-consent/granted` notice is no longer sent, `admin_consent::{decide,
require_for, ReadyGrant::spend}` changed, `vti_common::audit::AuditEvent`
gains `AdminActionBurst`, and `vtc_client::VtcError` gains `Parked`.

Deferred to A2: operator-write acknowledge items, sending the authority-
reduced notice, the two-admin 24 h cooling-off, approverSigned evidence and
requireRequesterAtCompletion.

title: ci: faster Rust CI and releases — parallel jobs, a lighter test build, verify on the Release PR
body:
## Why

Recent runs: the Rust `cargo test` job takes **10–19 min** and gates every PR (including the Release PR), and `release-plz release` takes **16–18 min** to publish. Every other workflow finishes in under 2 min. Nearly all of the time is compiling the 46 MB generated `trust-tasks-rs` over and over. Dependencies come from the cache, and the tests themselves run in about 5s.

## What

1. **Lighter test build (codegen).** The per-spec conformance tests move out of each generated module into one generated integration test, `trust-tasks-rs/tests/conformance/`. Every spec family except `acl` gets `#[cfg(not(test))]`, so the lib's unit-test harness no longer compiles a second copy of the whole tree. Locally, rebuilding the `validate` tests went **63s → 23s**, peak RSS **9.0 GB → 4.3 GB**. All 1558 generated tests (998 + 560 validate-only) and the 126 unit tests still run. The trap this creates is documented in CLAUDE.md.
2. **Parallel jobs.** Workspace tests, `validate` tests and `cargo doc` are now separate jobs, and clippy's two feature sets run as a matrix. None of these are required checks; branch protection requires only `DCO`, `EasyCLA`, `build-ts-bindings drift`, `bindings match specs` and `trust-tasks-codegen drift`.
3. **Verify on the Release PR, not during publish.** `publish_no_verify = true`, and a new `package-workspace` job runs `cargo package --workspace` on the `release` branch PR only. I checked locally that, with the lockstep crates bumped to an unpublished version, all nine crates package and verify against each other through cargo's local registry overlay. A broken tarball now blocks the merge instead of failing partway through an irreversible upload.
4. **Cache.** `rust-cache` saves from `main` only. PR saves were 1 GB duplicates of main's key, and the cache was at 9.8 of its 10 GB.
5. **Cancel superseded PR runs** in all seven PR workflows. On `main` the group is per-commit, so nothing there is ever cancelled.
6. The codegen drift check now uses `git status`, so it also catches *untracked* generated files.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Consider making `cargo package (every published crate)` a required check. It only runs on the Release PR; elsewhere it is skipped, and a skipped job satisfies a required check.
- `package-workspace` has no cache, since nothing on `main` saves one. It runs beside the Release PR's other checks.

## Verified locally

`cargo test --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --all-targets`, both clippy feature sets with `-D warnings`, `cargo doc` with `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and regenerating twice is idempotent.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.26.3
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: Administrator action list, approver-device step-up, and role-based authority ([#714](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/714))

* feat(vtc): administrator action list, approver-device step-up, and role-based authority

  Wire shapes for role-based administration at a community, the N-of-M
  approval action list, and an approver device as a re-authentication factor.
  Requirements: trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#51 (VTI-APV-016 - 021,
  VTI-ACL-035 - 037, VTI-VTC-022 - 023). Design:
  OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure docs/05-design-notes/
  vtc-{action-list,approver-step-up,admin-roles}.md.

  Action list (new family vtc/admin/actions):
  - _shared/0.1 Action (category approval|acknowledge|queue, status, threshold,
    approvals, summary rendered from the digested payload via JSON Pointers,
    templateDigest, per-approver challenge).
  - list/0.1 (views waitingForMe|requestedByMe|history|all, counts for the
    console badge), show/0.1, cancel/0.1, acknowledge/0.1.
  - A parked operation is answered with the existing trust-task-next-step/0.1
    (continuation proceed, expects vtc/admin/actions/show/0.1).
  - task-consent/decision/0.2: optional evidence (webauthn | approverSigned)
    and actionId; the document proof stays the approver's own.

  Approver step-up (new family auth/step-up/approver):
  - attest/0.1, the approver's signed statement (purpose stepUp|decision|enrol),
    carried embedded.
  - invite/0.1, redeem/start/0.1, redeem/finish/0.1, enroll/0.1 (self-service
    from an existing factor, subject's own signature), list/0.1, revoke/0.1,
    _shared/0.1 Approver.
  - auth/step-up/approve-request/0.4 (accepts, approvers) and
    approve-response/0.6 (approverSigned evidence).
  - vtc/install/claim/{start,finish}/0.3: claim under an existing DID with an
    approver instead of a passkey.

  Roles and capabilities:
  - acl/_shared/0.2 AclEntry with explicit act, keys and capabilities
    (VTI-ACL-006 - 008, -020), optional approve and approveCapabilities,

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.
