title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.26.1
body:
### Added

- **vtc/join-requests**: A criterion states its admission, so any join policy is expressible (Keyring VTI-13) ([#710](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/710))

* feat(vtc/join-requests): a criterion states its admission, so any join policy is expressible (Keyring VTI-13)

  A community's join criteria could not express its join policy. A criterion
  was a DCQL query (presentation-definition) with optional vetting, so it could
  not say:
  - that nothing is required: DCQL asks for at least one credential, so an
    open community had to delete every criterion;
  - that a submission meeting it is reviewed rather than admitted;
  - that an invitation is required, outside `vetting`;
  - whose credentials count.
  And submit decided against an unseen "active join policy", so an applicant
  could not tell an automatic path from a queue.

  A criterion is now one way into the community: what it requires and how a
  submission meeting it is decided.
  - vtc/_shared/0.2 schema-registry: AcceptsCriterion gains `admission`
    (REQUIRED: automatic | review), `credentialIssuers` (community | recognised
    | any, with `query`) and `invitationRequired`. `query` becomes OPTIONAL.
  - vtc/schemas/accepts/register, show, list 0.2: adopt it.
    register/0.2 adds `unsupportedRequirement`.
  - vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.3: `admission`, `credentialIssuers` and
    `invitationRequired` on Criterion; `presentationDefinition` OPTIONAL;
    `requirementsDigest` REQUIRED on every criterion. Criteria are listed in the
    order the community decides by. An empty list means no applications are
    accepted.
  - vtc/join-requests/submit/0.3: `criterion` names the criterion by digest. A
    submission naming none is decided under the first criterion it meets.
    Deciding is stated normatively. Not meeting a criterion never admits;
    `review` refers and never admits by itself; `automatic` admits unless the
    community refuses or refers on recorded grounds outside its criteria.
    Nothing outside a criterion admits anyone. New codes `criterionUnknown` and
    `notAccepting`.

  The specifications state no default criterion and prefer none. Open
  admission, review only (where invitations and trusted credentials admit no
  one), invitation only, credential-gated, vetted, and any combination or set
  of alternatives are expressed the same way, and each community's
  administrators choose. Earlier versions are unchanged.

  Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).



### Specifications

- **vtc/join-requests/status**: An approved applicant can ask for its credentials again ([#709](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/709))

* spec(vtc/join-requests/status): an approved applicant can ask for its credentials again

  An approved join is not finished until the membership credential reaches the
  applicant, and nothing in the family could say it had not, or ask for it again.
  In the field a persona was approved, listed as a member, and stayed Pending in
  its client: the credential push was lost, and a poll answering `approved` sent
  nothing.

  status/0.1 (draft, in place):
  - request `resendCredentials`: ask for the already-issued credentials again.
  - response `credentialsDelivered` (on `approved`): whether the community holds
    the applicant's acknowledgement.
  - response `credentialResend` (`queued` | `notNeeded` | `rateLimited`) and
    `retryAfter`. Absent after the flag means the consumer does not support it.
  - A re-delivery MUST send what was issued and MUST NOT issue anew; it goes to
    the request's applicant only, and the consumer rate-limits it.
  - `sideEffects` moves from `none` to `mutating`, so the task declares
    `issuedAtRequirement: REQUIRED` and carries an `## Authorization` section:
    ownership of the request.

  All four bindings regenerated.

title: vta-service-v0.50.0
body:
### Fixed

- A TSP reply reaches a sender on another mediator ([#1894](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1894))

Both the VTC (`handle_tsp`) and the VTA (`handle_tsp` → `send_to`) answered
  an inbound TSP Trust Task by routing `[own_mediator, sender]`. That ends at a
  mediator that does not host a sender on another one, which refuses it. The
  request arrived and the answer never did. In the field: an OpenVTC persona
  on ic3-mediator joined a VTC on cpunks-mediator, the admin approved it, and
  the persona stayed Pending. Its submit receipt and every
  `join-requests/status` poll reply were refused at the VTC's mediator. #405
  fixed the same failure in the other direction.

- **deps**: Affinidi-messaging-test-mediator 0.17 ([#1896](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1896))

test-mediator 0.17 / mediator 0.36 (affinidi-tdk-rs #920) are the releases on
  vta-sdk ^0.61, the line this workspace publishes. vta-service and vtc-service
  expose the test mediator to external consumers behind an optional feature, so
  the requirement is part of what they publish: breaking for those crates.

  Deciding is stated normatively. Not meeting a criterion never admits;
  `review` refers and never admits by itself; `automatic` admits unless the
  community refuses or refers on recorded grounds outside its criteria.
  Nothing outside a criterion admits anyone. New codes `criterionUnknown` and
  `notAccepting`.

The specifications state no default criterion and prefer none. Open
admission, review only (where invitations and trusted credentials admit no
one), invitation only, credential-gated, vetted, and any combination or set
of alternatives are expressed the same way, and each community's
administrators choose. Earlier versions are unchanged.

Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>


## Policies this expresses (examples in accepts/register/0.2 and manifest/0.3)

| Policy | Criteria |
|---|---|
| Open, straight through | `{admission: automatic}` |
| Open by review | `{admission: review}` |
| Review only: invitations and trusted credentials admit no one | only `{admission: review}` |
| Invitation only | `{admission: automatic, invitationRequired: true}` |
| A partner community's members | `{admission: automatic, query, credentialIssuers: recognised}` |
| Credential + vetting, then reviewed | `{admission: review, query, credentialIssuers, vetting}` |
| Invited or vetted, otherwise reviewed | three criteria, the review one last |

## Checks run locally

- `npm run validate`: 647 specs.
- `npm run check-bindings`: all four languages agree.
- `TT_STRICT_SECURITY_PRIVACY=1 npm run build`: passes.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace --all-targets` on rustc 1.99: pass.
- Every `requirementsDigest` in the manifest/0.3 examples was recomputed. The same JCS/SHA-256/base58btc code reproduces the two published 0.2 values.

## Follow-up

VTI implements this once a trust-tasks-rs release carries it. The VTC will serve the new versions, ship today's default as three ordinary criteria (invitation → automatic, a recognised issuer's credential → automatic, otherwise → review), and enforce "never admit outside a criterion; review never admits" as a host invariant.

feat(vtc/join-requests): a criterion states its admission, so any join policy is expressible (Keyring VTI-13) (#710)

* feat(vtc/join-requests): a criterion states its admission, so any join policy is expressible (Keyring VTI-13)

A community's join criteria could not express its join policy. A criterion
was a DCQL query (presentation-definition) with optional vetting, so it could
not say:
- that nothing is required: DCQL asks for at least one credential, so an
  open community had to delete every criterion;
- that a submission meeting it is reviewed rather than admitted;
- that an invitation is required, outside `vetting`;
- whose credentials count.
And submit decided against an unseen "active join policy", so an applicant
could not tell an automatic path from a queue.

A criterion is now one way into the community: what it requires and how a
submission meeting it is decided.
- vtc/_shared/0.2 schema-registry: AcceptsCriterion gains `admission`
  (REQUIRED: automatic | review), `credentialIssuers` (community | recognised
  | any, with `query`) and `invitationRequired`. `query` becomes OPTIONAL.
- vtc/schemas/accepts/register, show, list 0.2: adopt it.
  register/0.2 adds `unsupportedRequirement`.
- vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.3: `admission`, `credentialIssuers` and
  `invitationRequired` on Criterion; `presentationDefinition` OPTIONAL;
  `requirementsDigest` REQUIRED on every criterion. Criteria are listed in the
  order the community decides by. An empty list means no applications are
  accepted.
- vtc/join-requests/submit/0.3: `criterion` names the criterion by digest. A
  submission naming none is decided under the first criterion it meets.
  Deciding is stated normatively. Not meeting a criterion never admits;
  `review` refers and never admits by itself; `automatic` admits unless the
  community refuses or refers on recorded grounds outside its criteria.
  Nothing outside a criterion admits anyone. New codes `criterionUnknown` and
  `notAccepting`.

admission, review only (where invitations and trusted credentials admit no
one), invitation only, credential-gated, vetted, and any combination or set

title: spec(vtc/join-requests/status): an approved applicant can ask for its credentials again
body:
An approved join isn't finished until the membership credential reaches the applicant. Until now nothing in the family could report that it hadn't arrived, or ask for it again.

**Field case.** A persona was approved and listed as a member, but stayed Pending in OpenVTC. The credential push was lost, and a `status` poll answering `approved` sent nothing. A related routing defect, the TSP replies themselves going astray across mediators, was fixed in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1894.

## Change (status/0.1, draft, edited in place)

| Member | Where | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `resendCredentials` | request | Ask for the already-issued credentials again |
| `credentialsDelivered` | response, on `approved` | Whether the community holds the applicant's acknowledgement that the credential arrived |
| `credentialResend` | response | `queued`, `notNeeded` or `rateLimited`. Absent after the flag means the community doesn't support re-delivery |
| `retryAfter` | response | With `rateLimited`: the earliest time another re-delivery will be honoured |

Normative rules:
- A re-delivery **MUST** send what was issued and **MUST NOT** issue anew. Re-issuing would mint a second credential for one membership; that's what `members/renew` does, and why renew isn't the right tool here.
- It goes only to the request's applicant, never to a party named in the payload.
- The consumer rate-limits it and should back off. A producer must not set the flag on every poll.

The task's classification changes too:
- `sideEffects` moves from `none` to `mutating`, which makes the task consequential.
- It therefore declares `issuedAtRequirement: REQUIRED`, so a captured poll can't be replayed to trigger a delivery.
- It gains an `## Authorization` section, which names ownership of the request as the authority.

The new members are additive on the wire. The generated Rust types are `#[non_exhaustive]`, so the new fields don't break source either.

## Checks

- `npm run validate` passes, including the freshness floor (363/363). `npm run check-bindings` passes (Rust, TS, Go and Dart all agree).
- Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings are regenerated, and `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features` passes (1539 passed).
- A new invalid example rejects `resendCredentials: "true"`.

## Follow-ups

The VTC implementation (vtc-service status handler, plus vta-sdk carrying the fields) and the OpenVTC client both follow a trust-tasks-rs release. OpenVTC ships a manual rescue meanwhile: `R` / `members/renew` for an approved join whose credential never arrived.

title: feat: an approved join whose credential never arrived can be rescued with R
body:
A community can approve a join while the membership credential is lost in delivery. The persona is on its member list, but OpenVTC stays Pending and says the request "may not have been received", which is wrong. A status poll answering `approved` only stamped `receipt_at`, so nothing could tell the two cases apart, and `R` (`vtc/members/renew/0.1`) was Active-only.

## Change

- **`CommunityRecord::approved_at`** is set by the `approved` status arm (`mark_approved`). `approved_awaiting_credential()` and `can_renew()` read it. It's serde-defaulted, so existing configs load unchanged.
- **The row** reads "✓ approved — membership credential not received yet. Press R to ask the community to re-issue it." and offers `R`. The "may not have been received" warning no longer appears for it, because an approval stamps `receipt_at`.
- **`apply_renewal`** accepts that membership and activates it, as a delivered credential would. It returns the request it closed (`RenewalSummary::closed_join`), so the reciprocal VMC goes out with `closes_request` exactly as on delivery.
- The **key handler, hint row and runtime guard** all use the same `can_renew` gate.

It's manual only, because renewal re-issues. The automatic path re-sends the credentials already issued, and is OpenVTC/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf `resendCredentials` on `join-requests/status/0.1`, which needs a VTI release.

The persona this was found on became reachable once OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1894 (TSP replies to a sender on another mediator) is deployed. Its next status poll gets `approved`, and `R` then rescues it.

## Testing

- **Renewal:** `a_renewal_rescues_an_approved_join_whose_credential_never_arrived` checks that it activates, closes the right request, and that an Active renewal closes nothing. The existing `a_renewal_needs_an_active_membership` still refuses a Pending join nobody approved.
- **Status:** `status_response_approved_awaits_the_credential` now asserts `approved_at`, `can_renew`, that the join no longer reads as unacknowledged, and that a repeat poll changes nothing.
- **Panel:** `renew_is_offered_on_an_approved_join_awaiting_its_credential` checks the hint row and the panel text.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass, with and without default features. `cargo test --workspace` passes (1747 passed).

title: fix: a TSP reply reaches a sender on another mediator
body:
Both the VTC (`vtc-service/src/messaging.rs::handle_tsp`) and the VTA (`vta-service/src/messaging/service.rs` → `TspTransport::send_to`) answered an inbound TSP Trust Task by routing `[own_mediator, sender]`. That ends at a mediator that does not host a sender on another one, which refuses it. The request arrives and the answer never does.

**Field report.** An OpenVTC persona on `ic3-mediator` joined a VTC on `cpunks-mediator`. The admin approved the join and the persona is listed as a member, but it stayed Pending in OpenVTC: "no response from the community yet (sent over TSP)". Its submit receipt and every `join-requests/status` poll reply (OpenVTC polls Pending joins with backoff) were refused at the VTC's mediator. OpenVTC #405 fixed the same failure in the other direction. The admin sees at most a `warn!` "failed to send TSP reply", and only when the refusal comes back on the send call.

## Change

- **`vti_common::tsp_route::send_reply`** looks the sender's mediator up through the SDK's `peer_mediator`, which takes a mediator learned from the sender's routed invite first, else its DID document's `#tsp` service. When that is another mediator, it nests the reply `[own, peer_mediator]`, the same route VTI-56 gave sends a node starts. Otherwise it keeps the routed `[own, peer]` send.
  - The lookup is bounded by `PEER_MEDIATOR_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT` (10s, R1.2). A failed or timed-out lookup falls back to the old route with a warning.
  - `send_routed_to` is the route choice on its own, for a caller that already knows the peer's mediator.
- **VTC** `handle_tsp` replies through `send_reply`.
- **VTA** gains `TspTransport::send_reply`, and `handle_tsp` uses it.
- The relationship accept is unchanged: the SDK already routes it via the Reply_Path or the learned mediator.

Not yet catalogued in `design-docs/vti-networking-remediation-plan.md`.

**Known follow-up (not in this PR).** On approval the credentials go out through `trust_task_push`, which does route via the persona's `#tsp` mediator. In the field report they still did not arrive, and a `status` reply of `approved` does not re-send them. So a persona whose credential push was lost stays Pending even with this fix. That needs either a re-send path on the VTC or a re-request from OpenVTC, to be decided separately.

## Testing

- New `a_reply_reaches_a_sender_on_another_mediator` (two in-process mediators, no mediator handed in): fails on the old `send_to` route (bob's inbox stays empty for 15s) and passes on `send_reply`.
- `send_metadata_private_reaches_a_cross_mediator_peer` and `vti_56_a_cold_relationship_with_a_cross_mediator_peer_forms` still pass.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service --all-features --lib -- messaging` (37 passed) and `cargo test -p vti-common --all-features --lib -- tsp_route` pass.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy -p vti-common -p vtc-service -p vta-service --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` pass on the rebased branch. Full workspace suite left to CI.

title: fix: a TSP reply reaches a sender on another mediator (#1894)
body:
fix: a TSP reply reaches a sender on another mediator (#1894)

Both the VTC (`handle_tsp`) and the VTA (`handle_tsp` → `send_to`) answered
an inbound TSP Trust Task by routing `[own_mediator, sender]`. That ends at a
mediator that does not host a sender on another one, which refuses it. The
request arrived and the answer never did. In the field: an OpenVTC persona
on ic3-mediator joined a VTC on cpunks-mediator, the admin approved it, and
the persona stayed Pending. Its submit receipt and every
`join-requests/status` poll reply were refused at the VTC's mediator. #405
fixed the same failure in the other direction.

`vti_common::tsp_route::send_reply` looks the sender's mediator up through
the SDK (`peer_mediator`: learned from its routed invite first, else its DID
document's `#tsp` service) and nests the reply `[own, peer_mediator]` when
it is another mediator, the same route VTI-56 gave sends a node starts. The
lookup is bounded (`PEER_MEDIATOR_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT`, 10s, R1.2). A failed or
timed-out lookup falls back to the old route with a warning. The
relationship accept was already routed by the SDK and is unchanged.

`a_reply_reaches_a_sender_on_another_mediator` (two in-process mediators)
fails on the old `send_to` route and passes on `send_reply`.

title: fix(ci): release guard catches a moved dependency on an unbumped crate
body:
This is the guard fix promised in #1890. It closes the gap that let #1888 stop part-way through publishing.

**The gap.** `check-release-bump-sizes.py` skipped any crate whose current version was already on crates.io, on the grounds that nothing of it was about to ship. In #1888, release-plz moved `vti-rooms` to `vti-common ^0.33` but left it at 0.4.0, which was already published on ^0.32. `vti-rooms-dtg` was released in the same run and packaged against the published 0.4.0, so it found two `vti_common::AppError` types and the release stopped (run 36917925028).

**Rule 3.** On a release, a crate whose version is already published must keep its internal requirements in the same compatibility ranges as that published release. If one has moved, the crate needs a new breaking version. Like rule 2, it only reports when some member is about to publish, so a feature PR that moves a dependency floor isn't held to a version the Release PR will set. The shared requirement comparison is factored out into `moved_reqs`.

**Verified locally:**
- **`1a5d7f65` (#1888):** fails. It names `vti-rooms`, plus `vta-keyspaces`, `vta-persona`, `vta-sweepers` and `vta-tee`, which had the same latent problem.
- **`5427f96f` (#1890 head):** passes, 23 published members checked.

> [!NOTE]
> **Merge after #1890 publishes.** Main is currently mid-release: crates #1888 never published are still at unpublished versions. Rule 3 correctly fails on that state, so this PR's `lockfile self-pins` job stays red until #1890 has published.

title: vta-cli-common-v0.31.0
body:
### Added

- Serve vta/webvh/dids/create/1.1, whose response states `serverless` (VTI-20) ([#1886](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1886))

A serverless did:webvh exists only in the VTA until the caller serves its
  first log entry. create/1.0 said so only by leaving out `serverId`, so a
  client could infer it but not be told. The Keyring report met a persona
  minted on a VTA with no hosting server get through whoami, contexts, mint
  and key borrow, then fail resolving a document nobody published, with an
  error naming the persona rather than the cause.

  create/1.1 (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#702, trust-tasks-rs 0.25.4) REQUIRES
  `serverless` in its response. The VTA serves both. 1.1 states it. 1.0 is
  answered in 1.0's shape, whose response refuses unknown members.
  VtaClient::create_did_webvh sends 1.1. CreateDidWebvhResultBody gains
  `serverless: Option<bool>` (None from a 1.0 answer or a bundle written
  before 1.1) and `is_serverless()`, which falls back to an absent
  `server_id`. `pnm did-mgmt dids create` reads it: the summary says
  "Hosting: serverless" and the hosting guidance keys off it.

  The VTA already refuses a create that names neither `serverId` nor `url`,
  so a serverless mint is always one the caller asked for. Choosing it when no
  hosting server is registered is a client decision.

  trust-tasks-rs floor 0.25.4.

body:
This moves VTI onto the **affinidi-data-integrity 0.8** stack in one step and **drops the `=0.7.13` pin** from #1882.

| Dependency | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| affinidi-data-integrity | =0.7.13 | 0.8 |
| affinidi-bbs | 0.3 | 0.4 |
| affinidi-tdk | 0.21 | 0.22 |
| affinidi-messaging-sdk | 0.31.1 | 0.32 |
| affinidi-tdk-common | 0.6.11 | 0.7 |
| affinidi-messaging-test-mediator | 0.15 | 0.16 |
| affinidi-messaging-mediator-admin / -tui | 0.6 | 0.7 |
| didwebvh-rs | 0.7 | 0.8 |
| affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk | 0.8.39 | 0.8.41 |
| trust-tasks-* | 0.25 (rs 0.25.4) | 0.26 (carries #702, so the 0.25.4 floor holds) |
| dtg-credentials | 0.12 | 0.13 |

Where these come from:
- The affinidi crates are from affinidi-tdk-rs #918 and the earlier steps of the same update.
- The trust-tasks crates are from trust-tasks-tf #705 and #707.
- `dtg-credentials` 0.13 is from OpenVTC/dtg-credentials#35. It is the same crate on data-integrity 0.8, with no wire change.

**Why it moves in one step.** Data-integrity 0.8 uses `affinidi-bbs` 0.4 in its public API. Holding back any crate in this list would put two `affinidi_bbs` or two `DataIntegrityProof` types into the build. That is exactly what the `=0.7.13` pin was preventing.

**Source changes:** none.

**Breaking:** `vta-sdk` and the other crates expose types from trust-tasks and the tdk, so their next releases are breaking minors.

**Checks run locally**
- `cargo tree -d` shows no duplicate affinidi, trust-tasks, didwebvh, vta, vti or dtg crate.
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features` is clean.
- `check-workspace-version-reqs`, `check-nitro-copies-every-member` and `check-lockfile-self-pins` pass, and fmt is clean.

**After this:** release VTI. Then tell the VGI and affinidi-tdk-rs sessions the new `vta-sdk` version. The affinidi-tdk-rs session will then tighten the mediator's `vta-sdk` requirement.

title: feat!: serve vta/webvh/dids/create/1.1, whose response states `serverless` (VTI-20)
body:
A serverless did:webvh exists only in the VTA until the caller serves its
first log entry. create/1.0 said so only by leaving out `serverId`, so a
client could infer it but not be told. The Keyring report met a persona
minted on a VTA with no hosting server get through whoami, contexts, mint
and key borrow, then fail resolving a document nobody published, with an
error naming the persona rather than the cause.

create/1.1 (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#702, trust-tasks-rs 0.25.4) REQUIRES
`serverless` in its response. The VTA serves both. 1.1 states it. 1.0 is
answered in 1.0's shape, whose response refuses unknown members.
VtaClient::create_did_webvh sends 1.1. CreateDidWebvhResultBody gains
`serverless: Option<bool>` (None from a 1.0 answer or a bundle written
before 1.1) and `is_serverless()`, which falls back to an absent
`server_id`. `pnm did-mgmt dids create` reads it: the summary says
"Hosting: serverless" and the hosting guidance keys off it.

The VTA already refuses a create that names neither `serverId` nor `url`,
so a serverless mint is always one the caller asked for. Choosing it when no
hosting server is registered is a client decision.

trust-tasks-rs floor 0.25.4.

Breaking: CreateDidWebvhResultBody has a new public field. An older VTA
answers create/1.1 with unsupportedType.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>


## Testing

- New `vti_20_create_1_1_states_serverless_and_1_0_keeps_its_shape` drives both versions through dispatch. A serverless mint over 1.1 answers `serverless: true`, a `logEntry` and no `serverId`, and parses as the generated `create::v1_1::Response`. The same mint over 1.0 has no `serverless` and parses as `v1_0::Response`. The SDK reads both, and `is_serverless()` is true for each.
- New SDK unit tests for `is_serverless`. The CLI hosting-guidance tests are updated.
- The `conformance` census has a 1.1 entry.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast` and `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 7794 passed, 0 failed. fmt is clean, and clippy is clean workspace-wide and with `--features rest`.

Not covered: a server-managed mint over 1.1 (`serverless: false`). It needs a mock hosting server; the code path sets `Some(false)` beside `serverId`.

body:
## Problem
Joining a community whose VTC is on a different mediator than the persona fails:

```
Failed to submit join request: ... could not form the Rev 3 relationship its mediator did:webvh:...:cpunks-mediator requires ... (posted through our own mediator did:webvh:...:ic3-mediator): ... status(403) ... e.p.delivery.refused "Message not accepted for delivery"
```

The sender's mediator log shows `delivery refused ... reason=recipient is not local to this mediator`: the invite was posted Direct to the VTC's DID rather than routed.

## Cause
`send_trust_task` knows the VTC's mediator but only used it for the later `send_routed`. The invite is sent by the SDK's `send_control`, which routes `[our_mediator, peer_mediator, peer]` only when it knows a peer mediator (learned earlier, or a `TSPTransport` service in the peer's DID document). The VTC's DID document did not supply it, so the invite went out Direct and was refused.

## Fix
Call `set_peer_mediator` with the known mediator before `form_relationship_routed`.

## Testing
`cargo check -p openvtc-core` passes. Not yet verified end to end against the reporting user's setup, and no regression test added.

## Note
The peer's mediator must also allow inter-mediator relay (`enable_inter_mediator_relay`), or the relayed hop will be refused there.

title: vta-sdk-v0.60.0
body:
### Added

- **vta-sdk**: A holder client's grant hint names persona-holder ([#1885](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1885))

When the setup DID is not authorized, verify_authorization prints the
  `pnm acl create` the operator should run. For a holder client — OpenVTC, a
  personal agent — that grant also needs `--capabilities persona-holder`,
  which no role carries: the hint without it gets the client through
  provisioning and then refused the holder's attribute pool.

  `ProvisionAsk` gains `holder` (set via `as_holder()`). It changes nothing on
  the wire and is read only to word the hint, so an integration is never told
  to take holder authority. verify_authorization now takes the ask rather than
  its context.

title: fix(vta-sdk): read a DTG credential's shape without its proof, so a proof set parses (VTI-57)
body:
dtg-credentials 0.12 models `proof` as one DataIntegrityProof. A community
holding two signing keys signs each credential once per key and writes a
proof set, so every DTGCredential parse of such a credential failed. #1868
taught the proof *verifiers* to read a set (VTI-44), but these shape parses
were left:

- vetting::eligibility::community_roles returned None in silence, so
  openvtc filed a two-key community's vetter grant as a plain role and never
  seated the vetter (the Keyring report's VTI-57, blocking TUI-as-vetter).
- verify_eligibility_vp refused the same grant as malformed when a vetter
  presented it.
- vetting::statement::verify_statement refused the community's own
  vetted/1 statements.
- vtc-service's statement intake (credentials/ingress.rs) and its predicate
  check (vetting/mod.rs).

vta_sdk::vetting::dtg_shape parses the credential with its proof set aside,
and every site above uses it. It is a shape check (classification, subtype
members, predicate profile) and reads nothing from the proof. Each proof is
still verified over the credential as received, by verify_attached_proof,
which reads a set. A tampered proof in a set is still refused (pinned).
dtg_shape becomes a plain parse once dtg-credentials models `proof` as
one-or-many.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>


## Testing

- New tests: `vti_57_a_grant_carrying_a_proof_set_names_its_roles`, `vti_57_an_eligibility_vp_over_a_proof_set_grant_verifies` and `vti_57_a_statement_carrying_a_proof_set_verifies`. Each fails with the proof kept in the parse and passes with it set aside. `vti_57_a_tampered_proof_in_the_set_is_still_refused` passes either way, as it should.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast` and `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 7796 passed, 0 failed.
- fmt is clean, and clippy is clean workspace-wide and for `vtc-service --features vetting-pcs`.

Not covered: no new VTC-side test drives a proof-set statement through intake. The two VTC sites use the same helper the SDK tests pin.

title: fix(vtc): emit the declared codes for invitation issue/revoke and hidden-vetting publish (#1600)
body:
`vtc/invitations/issue`, `vtc/invitations/revoke` and `vtc/vetting/hidden/publish` answered every refusal through the generic `app_error_to_reject`, so the codes their specifications declare reached callers as a bare `taskFailed`.

- `invitations/issue:unknownRole` for a role that does not parse. `admin` parses and stays the framework's refusal (the privilege ceiling); a test pins that it is not reported as `unknownRole`. A community keeps no register of its `custom:<name>` roles, so any well-formed custom name is one it can seat.
- `invitations/revoke:notFound` for an absent invitation, including one outside the caller's inviter scope.
- `vetting/hidden/publish:noSuchCriterion` and `:noVetting`, now driven by a signed-document test.

Each gains a census witness. The unwitnessed baseline falls from 10 to 8 (12 to 8 with `vetting-pcs`), and the ceiling ratchets down to match.

Raised from the RAHP assurance review: sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit#691 and #849.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --features vetting-pcs --no-fail-fast` — 2504 passed, 0 failed
- [x] census tests with and without `vetting-pcs`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`, default and `--features vetting-pcs`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
